findings.claim: LCM has two file backends: kXML (single process, exclusive lock) and kSharedXML ("A FieldWorks XML file that can be accessed by multiple local clients"). A kXML request is silently upgraded to kSharedXML when the project's ProjectSharing setting is on.
findings.evidence: IProjectIdentifier.cs: 'kSharedXML = 104 ... A FieldWorks XML file that can be accessed by multiple local clients.' LcmCache.GetProviderTypeFromProjectId: 'case BackendProviderType.kXML: return LcmSettings.IsProjectSharingEnabled(projectId.ProjectFolder) ? BackendProviderType.kSharedXML : BackendProviderType.kXML;' IsProjectSharingEnabled reads ProjectLexiconSettings.ProjectSharing from the project's shared settings file.
findings.implication: FDAT never chooses the backend itself; whether it can coexist with a running FLEx is decided per project by the user's Sharing setting. FDAT must detect the setting (LcmSettings.IsProjectSharingEnabled) and tell the user to enable it (FLEx: Project Properties > Sharing tab) if FLEx is to stay open.

findings.claim: The Sharing setting is the checkbox on the Sharing tab of FLEx's Project Properties dialog, persisted as ProjectLexiconSettings.ProjectSharing.
findings.evidence: FwProjPropertiesDlg.cs: 'protected const int kSharingTab = 2;' 'm_enableProjectSharingCheckBox.Checked = m_projectLexiconSettings.ProjectSharing;' 'm_projectLexiconSettings.ProjectSharing = m_enableProjectSharingCheckBox.Checked;'. flexlibs docstring: 'project sharing can be enabled within the Fieldworks Project Properties dialog. In the Sharing tab, turn on the option "Share project contents with programs on this computer".'
findings.implication: Documented user instruction for FDAT: enable this checkbox once per project before running FDAT alongside FLEx.

findings.claim: Non-shared mode locks the project with a SimpleFileLock file at '<project>.fwdata.lock'; a second opener gets LcmFileLockedException ('FieldWorks cannot open the project {0} because another program is using it'). A static check exists: XMLBackendProvider.IsProjectLocked / ProjectLockingService.IsProjectLocked(path).
findings.evidence: 'm_fileLock = SimpleFileLock.CreateFromFilePath(ProjectId.Path + ".lock"); if (!m_fileLock.TryAcquireLock()) throw new LcmFileLockedException(...)'. 'public static bool IsProjectLocked(string projectPath) { var fileLock = SimpleFileLock.CreateFromFilePath(projectPath + ".lock"); if (fileLock.TryAcquireLock()) { fileLock.ReleaseLock(); return false; } return true; }'. libpalaso SimpleFileLock stores PID, timestamp ticks and process name in the lock file, and treats the lock as stale if the PID is no longer running.
findings.implication: Before opening, FDAT can call ProjectLockingService.IsProjectLocked(fwdataPath) to give a friendly 'close FLEx or enable sharing' message; stale locks from crashed processes are auto-recovered by PID check.

findings.claim: Shared mode works via a per-project GlobalMutex named '<ProjectName>_Mutex' and two memory-mapped files '<ProjectName>_CommitLogMetadata' and '<ProjectName>_CommitLog' (Windows: MemoryMappedFile.CreateOrOpen; Unix: files in /dev/shm). The commit log is a circular buffer of commit records; a single 'master' peer is responsible for writing the XML file.
findings.evidence: Class comment: 'uses memory mapped files to maintain a shared commit log that all applications use to update their state ... A single peer is responsible for updating the XML file.' 'private string MutexName => ProjectId.Name + "_Mutex"; CommitLogName => ProjectId.Name + "_CommitLog"; CommitLogMetadataName => ProjectId.Name + "_CommitLogMetadata"'. 'return MemoryMappedFile.CreateOrOpen(name, capacity);'
findings.implication: No network/DB server: sharing is same-machine only, keyed by project NAME (two projects with the same name in different folders would collide). FDAT as a peer does not write the .fwdata itself unless it is master.

findings.claim: In shared mode the first peer (or a peer that finds Master empty) also takes the .fwdata.lock file and becomes Master; therefore a shared-mode opener still fails with LcmFileLockedException if some other process holds the project in non-shared (exclusive) mode, and vice-versa.
findings.evidence: StartupInternal: 'if (metadata.Master == Guid.Empty) { base.LockProject(); metadata.Master = m_peerID; }' where base.LockProject is the SimpleFileLock acquisition that throws LcmFileLockedException.
findings.implication: Mixed modes are safe (they fail fast rather than corrupt). Since both processes read the same project setting, mixing only happens if the setting was toggled between the two opens.

findings.claim: Only the master peer writes the .fwdata file. A non-master peer's Commit appends a record to the shared log; the master writes it to disk on the master's next Commit or at master shutdown ('commit any unseen foreign changes'). If the log is full a non-master Commit throws; the master just skips the log.
findings.evidence: Commit: 'if (metadata.Master == m_peerID) PerformCommit(newbies, dirtballs, goners, cfiList);' ... 'if (metadata.Master != m_peerID) throw new InvalidOperationException("The current commit cannot be written to the commit log, because it is full.");'. ShutdownInternal: 'if (metadata.Master == m_peerID) { // commit any unseen foreign changes ... base.WriteCommitWork(...)'. Default log size: 'm_sharedXMLBackendCommitLogSize = 100000 * SharedXMLBackendProvider.PageSize' (PageSize 4096); FLEx overrides from registry value SharedXMLBackendCommitLogSize.
findings.implication: If FLEx is open (master), FDAT's saved data is durable on disk only after FLEx's next save (idle autosave, exit) - FDAT must not assume the .fwdata on disk reflects its writes immediately, and must save (Commit) before the user closes FLEx or runs Send/Receive.

findings.claim: When the master exits, the next peer to Commit becomes master, but only if the log and file are consistent; otherwise it throws 'The commit log and XML file are in an inconsistent state.'
findings.evidence: Commit: 'CheckExitedPeerProcesses(metadata); if (metadata.Master == Guid.Empty) { if (metadata.CurrentGeneration != metadata.FileGeneration) throw new InvalidOperationException("The commit log and XML file are in an inconsistent state."); base.LockProject(); metadata.Master = m_peerID; }'
findings.implication: FDAT should handle InvalidOperationException from Save() gracefully (report, do not retry blindly); a FLEx crash mid-session can leave FDAT unable to save.

findings.claim: Cross-process changes are exchanged only inside Commit(): a peer reads unseen foreign records and reconciles them into its in-memory UOW stacks (ChangeReconciler) before writing its own. If reconciliation is not possible (both clients changed the same object property), Commit registers a pending conflict; UnitOfWorkService then calls ILcmUI.ConflictingSave() and, if the user agrees, reverts all unsaved changes; autosave is suspended until then.
findings.evidence: 'if (GetUnseenForeignChanges(...)) { ... IReconcileChanges reconciler = uowService.CreateReconciler(...); if (reconciler.OkToReconcileChanges()) { reconciler.ReconcileForeignChanges(); ... } else { uowService.ConflictingChanges(reconciler); SaveMetadata(metadata); return true; } }'. UnitOfWorkService: 'if (m_pendingReconciliation != null) { GetUserInputOnConflictingSave(); return; }' and 'if (m_ui.ConflictingSave()) RevertToSavedState();'. ILcmUI: 'Check with user regarding conflicting changes ... True if user wishes to revert to saved state.' FwLcmUI shows ConflictingSaveDlg.
findings.implication: FDAT and FLEx editing the SAME object (e.g. FDAT writing a custom field on a ConstChartRow the user is simultaneously editing in the chart) can produce a conflict dialog and loss of unsaved edits on one side. Design FDAT writes to touch objects FLEx rarely edits concurrently, and keep FDAT's unsaved window short (save often).

findings.claim: FLEx autosaves on idle: no sooner than 10 s after the last save and 2 s after the last user activity (or 5 min regardless); FLEx also saves explicitly on shutdown. Each such Save is a Commit that both publishes FLEx's changes and pulls in FDAT's.
findings.evidence: '// Don't autosave less than 10s from the last save. if (now - m_lastSave < TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10.0)) return; // If it is less than 2s since the user did something don't save ... (unless the user has been busy ... for more than 5 minutes)'. FieldWorks.cs: 's_cache.ServiceLocator.GetInstance<IUndoStackManager>().Save();'
findings.implication: Latency of FDAT->FLEx visibility is seconds while the FLEx user is idle. Conversely, FDAT only sees FLEx's edits when FDAT itself calls Save()/Commit (a Save with no local changes still runs Commit and reconciles foreign changes - inferred from SaveInternal always calling m_dataStorer.Commit).

findings.claim: flexlibs opens the project with LcmCache.CreateCacheFromExistingData using SIL.FieldWorks.ProjectId(projectFileName) (type inferred as 'xml' -> kXML, hence auto-shared when the setting is on), LcmSettings.DisableDataMigration = True, FwLcmUI and FwDirectoryFinder.LcmDirectories; it references FLEx's own installed assemblies.
findings.evidence: FLExLCM.py: 'clr.AddReference("SIL.LCModel")' ... 'projId = ProjectId(projectFileName)' ... 'settings.DisableDataMigration = True' ... 'return LcmCache.CreateCacheFromExistingData(projId, "en", ui, dirs, settings, dlg)'. ProjectId.cs: 'public ProjectId(string name) : this(GetType("xml", name), name)'.
findings.implication: Using flexlibs gives FDAT exactly the same backend/lock behaviour as FLEx, and because it loads the installed FLEx DLLs the model version always matches the user's FLEx - no separate liblcm to keep in step.

findings.claim: flexlibs maps open-time failures: LcmFileLockedException -> FP_FileLockedError; LcmDataMigrationForbiddenException/WorkerThreadException -> FP_MigrationRequired (with the stated policy that migration must be done by the FieldWorks user, per Jason Naylor Dec 2018); other StartupException -> FP_ProjectError.
findings.evidence: 'except LcmFileLockedException as e: raise FP_FileLockedError()' ... 'Jason Naylor [Dec2018] said not to do migration from an external program: "We think that is something a FieldWorks user should explicitly decide." raise FP_MigrationRequired()'
findings.implication: FDAT must follow the same policy: never migrate; on FP_MigrationRequired tell the user to open the project in FLEx first.

findings.claim: LCM version gate on open: data newer than the library throws LcmNewerVersionException ('This project is for a newer version of FieldWorks'); data older with DisableDataMigration throws LcmDataMigrationForbiddenException; otherwise LCM migrates in place. In shared mode a non-master peer can never migrate ('non-master peers cannot migrate the XML file').
findings.evidence: 'if (currentDataStoreVersion > ModelVersion) throw new LcmNewerVersionException(...); if (currentDataStoreVersion == ModelVersion) return false; if (m_settings.DisableDataMigration) throw new LcmDataMigrationForbiddenException();'. SharedXML StartupInternal: 'if (startupModelVersion < currentModelVersion && metadata.Master != m_peerID) throw new LcmDataMigrationForbiddenException();'. FLEx on that exception: 'tell the user to close all other applications using this project'.
findings.implication: Version skew is handled safely by LCM; FDAT just needs clear messages. If FDAT ever bundled its own liblcm newer than the user's FLEx, it would trigger a migration the user did not choose (or, in shared mode, fail) - another reason to load the installed FLEx assemblies.

findings.claim: flexlibs write model: OpenProject(writeEnabled=True) calls MainCacheAccessor.BeginNonUndoableTask() once for the whole session; CloseProject() calls EndNonUndoableTask(), then IUndoStackManager.Save(), then Dispose(). Each Set* method refuses when not writeEnabled (FP_ReadOnlyError).
findings.evidence: 'if self.writeEnabled: ... self.project.MainCacheAccessor.BeginNonUndoableTask()' ... CloseProject: 'self.project.MainCacheAccessor.EndNonUndoableTask() ... usm = self.ObjectRepository(IUndoStackManager); usm.Save()' ... 'self.project.Dispose()'. 'if not self.writeEnabled: raise FP_ReadOnlyError()'.
findings.implication: With the stock flexlibs pattern nothing reaches disk (or FLEx) until CloseProject, and no Save is possible mid-session because Save requires the UOW state ReadyForBeginTask. A long-running FDAT desktop app should instead open/close short UOWs per user action and Save() after each, rather than holding one session-long task.

findings.claim: The canonical LCM way to wrap a write is NonUndoableUnitOfWorkHelper.Do(cache.ActionHandlerAccessor, () => {...}) (or UndoableUnitOfWorkHelper.Do(undoText, redoText, actionHandler, task)); it begins the task, ends it on success, and rolls back and rethrows on exception. Save() requires that no task is open ('Commit at wrong place').
findings.evidence: 'public static void Do(IActionHandler actionHandler, Action task) { using (var undoHelper = new NonUndoableUnitOfWorkHelper(actionHandler)) { task(); undoHelper.NoteSuccessfulCompletion(); } }' with Dispose: 'if (RollBack) RollBackChanges(); else EndUndoTask();'. Save: 'm_activeUndoStack.CheckReadyForCommit("Commit at wrong place.");'. LcmCache itself uses NonUndoableUnitOfWorkHelper.Do(createdCache.ActionHandlerAccessor, ...).
findings.implication: FDAT write recipe: for each user action -> NonUndoableUnitOfWorkHelper.Do(cache.ActionHandlerAccessor, ...) -> cache.ServiceLocator.GetInstance<IUndoStackManager>().Save(). Exceptions inside the task roll back cleanly, so a bug in FDAT cannot leave a half-applied change in the model.

findings.claim: Before rewriting the .fwdata file LCM compares the file's last-write time with the one it recorded; if another program touched the file it refuses to save ('FieldWorks cannot safely save your changes, because another program has modified the file'). Saves go to a .tmp file, then the old file becomes .bak and .tmp is renamed to .fwdata.
findings.evidence: 'var currentWriteTime = File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc(ProjectId.Path); if (m_lastWriteTime != currentWriteTime) { var msg = String.Format(Strings.ksFileModifiedByOther, ...); ReportProblem(msg, null); return; }' ... CopyTempFileToOriginal: 'File.Move(ProjectId.Path, backPathName); File.Move(tempPathname, mainPathname);'
findings.implication: FDAT must NEVER touch <Name>.fwdata directly (no XML patching, no external validators/fixers) while any LCM process has it open; otherwise FLEx's next save silently fails. Writing FDAT's own files elsewhere in the project folder (e.g. LinkedFiles) does not trip this check.

findings.claim: FLEx refuses Send/Receive while another application is connected to a shared project, and it unlocks/saves the project (UnlockCurrentProject = Save + CompleteAllCommits + release .lock) before launching FLExBridge, re-locking afterwards.
findings.evidence: 'while (SharedBackendServices.AreMultipleApplicationsConnected(Cache)) { if (ShowMessageBox(... ksSendReceiveNotPermittedMultipleAppsText ... RetryCancel) == Cancel) return true; }' string: 'Send/Receive cannot be performed when there are other applications using this project. Please close all other applications that are using this project before continuing.' SaveAllDataToDisk -> 'ProjectLockingService.UnlockCurrentProject(Cache);' which does 'IUndoStackManager.Save(); ds.CompleteAllCommits(); ds.UnlockProject();'
findings.implication: Users must close FDAT (dispose the cache) before Send/Receive. FDAT should save on every action and release the project promptly (or at least expose a clear 'disconnect' so S/R can proceed).

findings.claim: FLExBridge writes its own '<Name>.fwdata.lock' file during Send/Receive 'to keep FW apps from starting up at such an inopportune moment', and Chorus excludes **/*.fwdata.lock from the repository. FLEx-ChorusPlugin has a message 'It appears that FLEx is running, since the file: {0}.fwdata.lock is present. You need to close FLEx or delete that file...'.
findings.evidence: SendReceiveActionHandler: 'var lockPathname = Path.Combine(projectDir, projectName + LibTriboroughBridgeSharedConstants.FwXmlLockExtension); ... File.WriteAllText(lockPathname, "");' FlexFolderSystem: 'projectFolderConfiguration.ExcludePatterns.Add("**" + LibTriboroughBridgeSharedConstants.FwXmlLockExtension);'
findings.implication: FDAT launched during an S/R will fail to open (lock file present) - expected; FDAT should surface 'project is locked (FLEx or Send/Receive running)' rather than crash. Note this bridge lock is an empty file, so SimpleFileLock's PID-based stale check will treat it as acquirable (inferred) - a small race FLEx itself accepts.

findings.claim: FLEx blocks adding custom fields and warns on 'single-user' dialogs while other applications are connected to the project.
findings.evidence: XWorksViewBase: 'if (SharedBackendServices.AreMultipleApplicationsConnected(cache)) { MessageBoxUtils.Show(... ksCustomFieldsCanNotBeAddedDueToOtherAppsText ...); return; }'. SharedBackendServicesHelper strings: 'Saving changes in this dialog while this project is open in other applications may cause those applications to crash or malfunction.'
findings.implication: Schema-level changes (creating custom fields, possibly new possibility lists/styles) are treated by FLEx as unsafe with multiple peers. FDAT should create any custom fields it needs only when it is the sole opener (e.g. a one-time 'set up project' step with FLEx closed), and afterwards only write values.

findings.claim: A post-write validator/fixer exists: SIL.LCModel.FixData.FwDataFixer(filename, IProgress, ErrorLogger, ErrorCounter).FixErrorsAndSave(), packaged by FieldWorks as the FixFwData.exe console tool (Src/Utilities/FixFwData) which takes the .fwdata path and returns exit code 1 if any error was reported. It reads and rewrites the XML file directly.
findings.evidence: 'public class FwDataFixer ... Fix errors in a FieldWorks data XML file.' 'public FwDataFixer(string filename, IProgress progress, ErrorLogger logger, ErrorCounter counter)' 'public void FixErrorsAndSave()'. Program.cs: 'var data = new FwDataFixer(pathname, prog, logger, counter); data.FixErrorsAndSave(); ... if (errorsOccurred) return 1;'
findings.implication: FDAT can offer 'Validate project' by running FixFwData.exe (from the FLEx install dir) only when the project is closed by every process; running it while FLEx/FDAT hold the cache would trip the modified-by-other check above.

findings.claim: Deep-link URL format: 'silfw://localhost/link?' + UrlEncode('database=<name>&tool=<tool>&guid=<guid>&tag=<tag>[&<PropName>=<value>...]'). Parsing splits on & and =; unknown names become PropertyTableEntries; guid may be 'null'. Requires the silfw protocol registration (HKCR\silfw\shell\open\command -> FieldWorks.exe %1) created by the installer. If FLEx is already running on that project, the running instance is asked (IPC) to HandleIncomingLink.
findings.evidence: 'public const string kFwUrlPrefix = kSilScheme + "://" + kLocalHost + "/" + kLink + "?";' ToString: 'uriBuilder.Query = HttpUtility.UrlEncode(query.ToString());' AddProperties: 'tool={0}&guid={1}&tag={2}' prefixed by FwAppArgs 'database={0}&'. InitializeFromUrl: 'foreach (string pair in decodedQuery.Split('?', '&')) ... ProcessArg(name, value)'; 'default: PropertyTableEntries.Add(new Property(name, Decode(value)))'. Class comment describes registry key and TryFindExistingProcess IPC.
findings.implication: FDAT can open FLEx at an object with os.startfile(url) exactly as flexlibs does.

findings.claim: flexlibs.BuildGotoURL builds such a URL with FwAppArgs(project.ProjectId.Handle, tool, guid) and picks tool 'interlinearEdit' for Text objects (TextTags.kClassId); other tools it knows: 'reversalToolEditComplete', 'Analyses', 'lexiconEdit'. There is no separate discourse/constituent-chart tool name; the chart is a tab inside interlinearEdit.
findings.evidence: 'elif flexObject.ClassID == TextTags.kClassId: tool = "interlinearEdit"' ... 'linkObj = FwAppArgs(self.project.ProjectId.Handle, tool, flexObject.Guid); return str(linkObj)'. toolConfiguration.xml: '<tool label="Interlinear Texts" value="interlinearEdit" icon="EditView">'. InterlinMaster: 'public enum TabPageSelection { Info = 0, RawText = 1, Gloss = 2, Interlinearizer = 3, TaggingView = 4, PrintView = 5, ConstituentChart = 6 }'.
findings.implication: FDAT deep links should target the IText GUID with tool=interlinearEdit.

findings.claim: The interlinear tab is driven by the property-table string 'InterlinearTab' (enum name, e.g. 'ConstituentChart'); InterlinMaster switches tabs in OnPropertyChanged("InterlinearTab"), and FLEx's own history links carry tag=<tab> plus a PropertyTableEntry InterlinearTab=<tab>. LinkListener applies every PropertyTableEntry via m_propertyTable.SetProperty after jumping to the record.
findings.evidence: InterlinMaster.UpdateContextHistory: 'FwLinkArgs link = new FwLinkArgs(toolName, guid, InterlinearTab.ToString()); link.PropertyTableEntries.Add(new Property("InterlinearTab", InterlinearTab.ToString()));'. OnPropertyChanged: 'case "InterlinearTab": if (m_tabCtrl.SelectedIndex != (int)InterlinearTab) ShowTabView();'. LinkListener: 'foreach (Property property in m_lnkActive.PropertyTableEntries) { m_propertyTable.SetProperty(property.name, property.value, true); }'
findings.implication: INFERRED recipe for 'open this chart in FLEx': silfw://localhost/link?database%3d<Proj>%26tool%3dinterlinearEdit%26guid%3d<TextGuid>%26tag%3dConstituentChart%26InterlinearTab%3dConstituentChart. The code path is the same one FLEx uses for Back/Forward history, but an external-launch end-to-end test on Windows is still needed.

findings.claim: The FLExTools wiki (Home, FLExTools-v2, Technical-documentation) and the local flextools/flexlibs docs contain no statements about running while FLEx is open, locking or sharing beyond the flexlibs docstring; FLExTools simply passes modifyAllowed to FLExProject.OpenProject(writeEnabled=...) per module run and closes the project after each run. Module metadata declares FTM_ModifiesDB and modules receive Main(flexProject, report, modifyAllowed).
findings.evidence: FTModules.__openProject: 'self.project.OpenProject(projectName, writeEnabled = modifyAllowed)'; __closeProject: 'self.project.CloseProject()'. Modules readme: 'FTM_ModifiesDB : True/False' ... 'def Main(flexProject, report, modifyAllowed)'. Wiki fetches returned only general descriptions.
findings.implication: The ecosystem precedent is open-write-close per operation with a save at close; FDAT should copy that granularity (short sessions or short UOW+Save cycles), not a long-lived writable cache.

openQuestions: Does liblcm itself allow a non-master shared peer to add a custom field (IFwMetaDataCacheManaged.AddCustomField) or does it only rely on the FLEx UI guard? The commit record carries CustomFieldInfo, so it may work, but FLEx's own UI forbids it - needs a test before FDAT creates fields with FLEx open.

End-to-end verification on Windows that an externally launched silfw:// link with tag/InterlinearTab=ConstituentChart lands on the chart tab (both when FLEx is closed and when it is already running on the project).

Whether FDAT should be a Python (flexlibs/pythonnet) or .NET process; either way it must load the user's installed FLEx assemblies so ModelVersion matches - confirm FwDirectoryFinder resolution for 64-bit FLEx 9.x installs.

Behaviour when the shared commit log wraps for a long-running FDAT session (default 100000*4096 bytes, registry-overridable): does FLEx as master purge records fast enough that FDAT never hits 'commit log is full'?

The FLExTools wiki pages about FAQ/Writing-Modules were not reachable (404); the flexlibs docstring is the only written guidance on the Sharing setting. software.sil.org help topic 'khtpProjectProperties_Sharing' is blocked from here.

result.summary: Answers to the four questions, from the code. (1) YES, with caveats: a TsString run can carry an external-file link (FwObjDataTypes.kodtExternalPathName=4) as the ktptObjData string property, serialized as externalLink="..." on the <Run>; FLEx marks such runs with the built-in "Hyperlink" character style (StringServices.MarkTextInBldrAsHyperlink) and, on click, VwBaseVc.DoHotLinkAction joins a non-rooted path onto LangProject.LinkedFilesRootDir and calls Process.Start (ShellExecute: a .json would open in whatever app Windows associates). FLEx's own Insert > Link to File copies/moves the chosen file into LinkedFiles/Others (user's choice), stores the path relative to LinkedFilesRootDir ("Others\x.json"), and registers a CmFile under LangProject.FilePathsInTsStringsOA; FDAT should mimic all three steps. Suitable fields: Text.Description (shown as "Comment" in the Text Info tab, multistring slice), Text.Source (MultiString), Note.Content (MultiString), ConstChartRow.Notes (String); Text.Abbreviation is MultiUnicode (no runs). FLExBridge syncs the string (TsStrings merge atomically) and the file (LinkedFiles/Others/**.* included), but Chorus treats .json with the DefaultFileTypeHandler: 1 MiB cap and no merge (UnmergableFileTypeConflict, ours/theirs). (2) YES: character styles are StStyle objects in LangProject.StylesOC (Type=character, Rules=TextPropBinary ITsTextProps), creatable via IStStyleFactory.Create(...isCharStyle:true...) or LcmStyleSheet.PutStyle, applied to runs via ktptNamedStyle; the chart body and interlinear views are RootSites rendered with the project stylesheet, so run-level styles show; FLExBridge writes LangProject.Styles to General/FLExStyles.style and merges it, but its validator rejects duplicate style names, so two machines independently creating "FDAT xxx" styles would collide—create with a fixed GUID or check-before-create. (3) Segment.NotesOS is per-sentence/segment (a sequence of Note objects each with MultiString Content, edited in the Interlinear "Note" line, add/delete via menu); ConstChartRow.Notes is a single non-multilingual TsString per chart row (row = clause; rows attach to segments only via ConstChartWordGroup.Begin/EndSegment + analysis indices), edited in-place in the chart's Notes cell (the only editable cell) and exported as <note>. (4) NO for a GUID run: kodtNameGuidHot/kodtOwnNameGuidHot runs (serialized as link=/ownlink=) are rendered through IVwViewConstructor.GetStrForGuid, and FwBaseVc.GetStrForGuid throws NotImplementedException for anything but footnotes and pictures; VwBaseVc.DoHotLinkAction only acts on kodtExternalPathName, and no FLEx VC in the checked-out sources handles GUID hot links. The supported way to hyperlink to a possibility is an external-link run whose URL is a FieldWorks silfw://localhost/link?app=flex&database=<proj>&tool=<toolId>&guid=<guid> URL (what "Copy Location as Hyperlink" + "Paste Hyperlink" produce; LinkListener.HandleLocalHotlink follows it in-process); tool id for the Chart Markers list is "chartmarkEdit".

findings.claim: A TsString run carries an external file/URL link as the ktptObjData string property whose first char is FwObjDataTypes.kodtExternalPathName (=4); the remaining chars are a relative (LinkedFilesRootDir-based) or absolute path; clicking reconstructs the absolute path and ShellExecutes the file.
findings.evidence: enum comment: "The following characters could either be a relative path (based on LangProject:ExtLinkRootDir) or an absolute path. The string will be hot: when clicked, the system reconstructs the absolute path if necessary, then calls ShellExecute to launch the file with the default program used for that file extension. kodtExternalPathName = 4"
findings.implication: An FDAT JSON link can be embedded in any TsString field; opening it from FLEx launches the OS default app for .json, not FDAT, unless FDAT registers itself for that extension or a custom scheme.

findings.claim: LCM's helper for making a hyperlink run sets two run properties: ktptNamedStyle = the link style's name and ktptObjData = (char)kodtExternalPathName + url; the overload taking linkedFilesRootDir first converts the path to one relative to LinkedFilesRootDir.
findings.evidence: MarkTextInBldrAsHyperlink: "var propVal = Convert.ToChar((int)FwObjDataTypes.kodtExternalPathName) + url; ... strBldr.SetStrPropValue(ichStart, ichLim, (int)FwTextPropType.ktptNamedStyle, linkStyle.Name); strBldr.SetStrPropValue(ichStart, ichLim, (int)FwTextPropType.ktptObjData, propVal);" and overload: "var relativeUrl = LinkedFilesRelativePathHelper.GetRelativeLinkedFilesPath(url, linkedFilesRootDir); ... returns relativeUrl (used to create a CmFile if it represents a file path)"
findings.implication: FDAT can call SIL.LCModel.DomainServices.StringServices.MarkTextInBldrAsHyperlink(bldr, ichMin, ichLim, fullPath, hyperlinkStyle, cache.LangProject.LinkedFilesRootDir) from flexlibs/pythonnet to produce exactly what FLEx produces.

findings.claim: The relative form FLEx stores is the path below LinkedFilesRootDir with the leading separator stripped (e.g. 'Others\fdat\chart.json'), and anything containing ':' after position 1 is treated as a URL and left untouched.
findings.evidence: GetRelativeLinkedFilesPath: "if (filePath.IndexOf(':') > 1) { // It's a URL... return null; } ... if (relativePath.StartsWith(directory,...)) { relativePath = relativePath.Substring(directory.Length); if (relativePath[0] == Path.DirectorySeparatorChar) relativePath = relativePath.Substring(1); }"
findings.implication: Store 'Others\fdat\<chart>.json' (relative), never an absolute path, so the link resolves on every colleague's machine after Send/Receive.

findings.claim: On click, VwBaseVc.DoHotLinkAction handles only kodtExternalPathName: a non-rooted file path is joined to LangProject.LinkedFilesRootDir, the link is first offered to LinkListener (silfw links), otherwise Process.Start(url) is called.
findings.evidence: "if (strData.Length > 0 && (int)strData[0] == (int)FwObjDataTypes.kodtExternalPathName) { string url = strData.Substring(1).Trim(); ... if (FileUtils.IsFileUriOrPath(url) && FileUtils.IsFilePathValid(url) && !Path.IsPathRooted(url)) { string linkedFilesFolder = GetLinkedFilesRootDir(sda); url = Path.Combine(linkedFilesFolder, url); } ... Publisher.Publish(...HandleLocalHotlink...); if (args.LinkHandledLocally) return; ... using (Process.Start(url)) {} }"; GetLinkedFilesRootDir reads sda.get_UnicodeProp(hvo, LangProject.LinkedFilesRootDir).
findings.implication: This is the resolver for question (1): the link is clickable in any FLEx view built on the views engine (chart Notes cell, interlinear note line, detail-view string slices).

findings.claim: Detail-view string slices (e.g. Text Info tab fields) override DoHotLinkAction to first try FieldWorks silfw:// links via FollowLink, then fall back to the base external-path handling.
findings.evidence: StringSlice.StringSliceVc.DoHotLinkAction: "if (strData[0] == (int)FwObjDataTypes.kodtExternalPathName) { string url = strData.Substring(1); ... if (url.StartsWith(FwLinkArgs.kFwUrlPrefix)) { FwLinkArgs linkArgs = new FwLinkArgs(url); ... Publisher.Publish(...FollowLink...); if (retObj.ReturnValue) return; } } base.DoHotLinkAction(strData, sda);"
findings.implication: Links placed in Text.Description/Source (Text Info tab) are clickable there.

findings.claim: FLEx's 'Insert > Link to File' command opens a file dialog, then offers to Move/Copy/Leave the file into LinkedFiles/Others, then converts the selection to a link.
findings.evidence: FwXWindow.OnInsertLinkToFile: "pathname = MoveOrCopyFilesController.MoveCopyOrLeaveExternalFile(pathname, Cache.LangProject.LinkedFilesRootDir, ...); ... helper.ConvertSelToLink(pathname, StyleSheet);"; MoveCopyOrLeaveExternalFile: "return MoveCopyOrLeaveFiles(new[] {sFile}, Path.Combine(sRootDirLinkedFiles, LcmFileHelper.ksOtherLinkedFilesDir), ...)" with File.Move/File.Copy per user choice; ksOtherLinkedFilesDir = "Others".
findings.implication: LinkedFiles/Others is exactly the folder FLEx itself uses for 'other' linked files, so LinkedFiles/Others/fdat/ is a conventional location; the copy is optional in FLEx (user may 'Leave'), so absolute links to files outside the project do occur in real data.

findings.claim: ConvertSelToLink uses the 'Hyperlink' style, converts silfw URLs for the current project, marks the run with MarkTextInBldrAsHyperlink(..., LinkedFilesRootDir), and registers a CmFile for the linked file under LangProject.FilePathsInTsStringsOA.
findings.evidence: "var hyperlinkStyle = stylesheet.FindStyle(StyleServices.Hyperlink); ... clip = FwLinkArgs.FixSilfwUrlForCurrentProject(clip, m_cache.ProjectId.Name); var filename = StringServices.MarkTextInBldrAsHyperlink(tsb, 0, tsb.Length, clip, hyperlinkStyle, m_cache.LanguageProject.LinkedFilesRootDir); if (FileUtils.IsFilePathValid(filename)) { ... DomainObjectServices.FindOrCreateFile(m_cache.LangProject.FilePathsInTsStringsOA, filename); }"
findings.implication: To be indistinguishable from a FLEx-made link, FDAT should also call DomainObjectServices.FindOrCreateFile(LangProject.FilePathsInTsStringsOA, relativePath) so FLEx's linked-file bookkeeping (move/rename of LinkedFiles folder) covers the JSON.

findings.claim: LangProject.FilePathsInTsStrings is an owning atomic CmFolder that holds a CmFile for every externalLink found in TsStrings; migration 7000030 made such links relative to LinkedFilesRootDir.
findings.evidence: <owning num="56" id="FilePathsInTsStrings" card="atomic" sig="CmFolder"> comment: "holds all externalLink's to files found in TsStrings"; model history: "7000030: Make externalLink's found in TsStrings a relative path for any files relative to LinkedFilesRootDir. Also create a FilePathsInTsStrings element in LangProject which owns a CmFolder which owns a set of CmFile."
findings.implication: Model-sanctioned place to register FDAT's JSON as a CmFile (InternalPath relative to LinkedFiles); no custom field needed for the file reference.

findings.claim: FLEx rewrites external-link paths when the LinkedFiles folder is moved (GetHyperlinksInFolder / FixHyperlinkFolder crawl all styled strings for runs whose ObjData starts with kodtExternalPathName + folder).
findings.evidence: "string prefix = Convert.ToChar((int) FwObjDataTypes.kodtExternalPathName).ToString(); var match = prefix + folder; CrawlStyledStrings(cache, (obj, flid, ws, tss) => { ... if (objData == null || !objData.StartsWith(match)) continue; ... result.Add(new LinkOccurrence{...}) })"
findings.implication: Links written by FDAT in the standard form are maintained by FLEx's own tooling; nothing FDAT-specific is required to survive a LinkedFiles relocation.

findings.claim: The 'Hyperlink' character style is a factory style present in every project: it is defined in FlexStyles.xml (blue, single underline) and data migration 7000018 creates it if missing.
findings.evidence: FlexStyles.xml: <tag id="Hyperlink" guid="7FF691E7-32F4-445D-ACEA-1DED6A6AC8EA" userlevel="1" context="internal" type="character"> <font color="blue" underline="single" underlineColor="blue"/>; StyleServices: public const string Hyperlink = "Hyperlink"; // CANNOT BE LOCALIZED; DataMigration7000018: "// if \"Hyperlink\" does not exist, create it. ... dtoHyperlink = CreateCharStyle(\"Hyperlink\", ...)"
findings.implication: FDAT can rely on stylesheet.FindStyle("Hyperlink") (or LangProject.StylesOC by Name) existing; no need to create a style for links.

findings.claim: In the .fwdata/FLExBridge XML an external link run is <Run ... externalLink="path">display text</Run>; GUID hot links are link="guid" / ownlink="guid" and their run text is written as empty.
findings.evidence: WriteStringProperty: "case FwObjDataTypes.kodtNameGuidHot: writer.WriteAttributeString(\"link\", GetGuidString(value)); case kodtExternalPathName: writer.WriteAttributeString(\"externalLink\", ...value.Substring(1)...); case kodtOwnNameGuidHot: writer.WriteAttributeString(\"ownlink\", ...)"; reader: "case \"externalLink\": propsBldr.SetStrPropValue((int)FwTextPropType.ktptObjData, (char)FwObjDataTypes.kodtExternalPathName + attr.Value)"; TsStringSerializer: for kodtNameGuidHot/kodtOwnNameGuidHot "hotGuid = true" ... "else if (hotGuid) { writer.WriteString(string.Empty); }"
findings.implication: FLExBridge sees the link as an attribute on a Run inside a Str element; it is plain model data, no special handler needed.

findings.claim: FLExBridge's object validator accepts the run attributes externalLink, link, ownlink, namedStyle etc., and merges every TsString (<Str>) and every <AStr> alternative atomically (whole-string ours/theirs on conflict).
findings.evidence: CheckTextPropertyAttributes attrs include "externalLink", "link", "ownlink", "namedStyle"; FieldWorksMergeServices: "AddSharedSingletonElementType(sharedElementStrategies, FlexBridgeConstants.Str, false); elementStrategy.IsAtomic = true; // TsStrings are atomic" and "AddSharedKeyedByWsElementType(..., FlexBridgeConstants.AStr, false, true); // ... is atomic"
findings.implication: A link run inside Row.Notes or Text.Description syncs, but concurrent edits to the same string by two users conflict as a whole (one side's whole string wins). Keep FDAT's link in a string nobody else edits, or accept that risk.

findings.claim: FLExBridge includes LinkedFiles/Others/**.* (and AudioVisual, Pictures) and all **.style files in the Chorus repository.
findings.evidence: projectFolderConfiguration.IncludePatterns.Add("**.style"); ...Add(Path.Combine("LinkedFiles", "AudioVisual", "**.*")); ...Add(Path.Combine("LinkedFiles", "Others", "**.*")); ...Add(Path.Combine("LinkedFiles", "Pictures", "**.*"))
findings.implication: Both halves of the owner's idea (string link + JSON under LinkedFiles/Others) are synced by Send/Receive. Note ExcludePatterns include "**.xml" (line ~35), so an .xml sidecar under LinkedFiles would NOT sync; use .json.

findings.claim: Chorus applies a per-extension size cap when committing; extensions not claimed by a handler fall back to LargeFileFilter.Megabyte (1,048,576 bytes). Chorus's TextFileTypeHandler claims only 'txt', so a .json file is handled by DefaultFileTypeHandler (MaximumFileSize = LargeFileFilter.Megabyte), which cannot merge: on conflict it records an UnmergableFileTypeConflict and keeps ours or copies theirs.
findings.evidence: LargeFileFilter: "public static uint Megabyte => 1048576;" and GetMaxSizeForExtension: "if (!extensionToMaximumSize.TryGetValue(extension, out maxForExtension)) { maxForExtension = Megabyte; }" (the 10 MB figure in the 2022 comment is applied through individual handlers' MaximumFileSize, e.g. image/audio). TextFileTypeHandler.GetExtensionsOfKnownTextFileTypes yields "txt". DefaultFileTypeHandler.Do3WayMerge: XmlMergeService.AddConflictToListener(..., new UnmergableFileTypeConflict(...)); TheyWin => File.Copy(pathToTheirs, pathToOurs, true); MaximumFileSize => LargeFileFilter.Megabyte.
findings.implication: An FDAT JSON per chart must stay under 1 MiB (files over the cap are silently excluded from the commit and never reach colleagues), and two users editing the same chart's JSON between syncs lose one side entirely. A per-chart file keeps both risks small. The 1 MiB vs 10 MB nuance was read via summarised fetch; verify against the installed Chorus build in Phase 0.

findings.claim: Text (a CmMajorObject) has these text fields: Name (MultiUnicode), Description (MultiString), Source (MultiString), Abbreviation (MultiUnicode); there is no 'Comment' property on Text in the model. The Text Info tab shows Description with the label 'Comment' as a multistring slice, and Source/Abbreviation/Title as multistring slices.
findings.evidence: MasterLCModel: CmMajorObject props Name MultiUnicode, Description MultiString; Text props Source MultiString (num 2), Abbreviation MultiUnicode (num 10), Contents StText, MediaFiles CmMediaContainer. CellarParts.xml: <slice label="Comment" editor="multistring" ws="analysis vernacular" field="Description" .../>, <slice label="Source" editor="multistring" ... field="Source"/>, <slice label="Abbreviation" editor="multistring" ... field="Abbreviation"/>
findings.implication: Text.Description or Text.Source can hold a styled link run (MultiString = formatted, per-WS TsString); Abbreviation and Name cannot (MultiUnicode has no runs/props). Any link FDAT puts there is user-visible and user-editable text, so it can be deleted by hand.

findings.claim: A Text can have only one media container (Text.MediaFiles is an atomic owning CmMediaContainer), and CmMedia/CmFile are the model's file-reference classes: CmFile has Name, Description, OriginalPath, InternalPath (relative to LinkedFiles), Copyright; CmMedia has Label and MediaFile (ref CmFile). CmFolder owns SubFolders and Files.
findings.evidence: <owning num="12" id="MediaFiles" card="atomic" sig="CmMediaContainer"> "A container for media files which are associated with this text, and possibly referenced by segments"; CmFile props: Name MultiUnicode, Description MultiString, OriginalPath Unicode, InternalPath Unicode, Copyright; CmMedia: Label MultiString, MediaFile rel CmFile; CmFolder: Name, SubFolders, Description, Files.
findings.implication: The 'linked file of the text' idea maps to either a CmFile registered in LangProject.FilePathsInTsStringsOA (via a link run) or, less appropriately, a CmMedia in Text.MediaFiles (FLEx treats those as audio/video for segments, so avoid). The CmFile/CmFolder route plus a link run is the model-sanctioned approach.

findings.claim: StStyle carries Name (Unicode), BasedOn, Next, Type (integer; character vs paragraph), Rules (TextPropBinary = an ITsTextProps), IsBuiltIn, IsModified, UserLevel, Context, Structure, Function, Usage; styles are owned in LangProject.Styles (owning collection).
findings.evidence: <class num="17" id="StStyle"> props: Name Unicode; BasedOn rel StStyle; Next rel StStyle; Type Integer 0-255; Rules TextPropBinary; IsBuiltIn Boolean ("FALSE means this style was added by the user"); IsModified; UserLevel; Context; Structure; Function; Usage MultiUnicode. LangProject: <owning num="23" id="Styles" card="col" sig="StStyle">
findings.implication: Character styles are ordinary model objects FDAT can create through LCM (IsBuiltIn=false), and their formatting lives in Rules as text props (bold, italic, colour, font size).

findings.claim: LCM exposes a factory for creating a character style in a style list and a stylesheet method that writes the style's Rules from an ITsTextProps.
findings.evidence: IStStyleFactory.Create(ILcmOwningCollection<IStStyle> styleList, string name, ContextValues context, StructureValues structure, FunctionValues function, bool isCharStyle, int userLevel, bool isBuiltin) { var retval = new StStyle(); styleList.Add(retval); retval.Name = name; ... retval.Type = (isCharStyle ? StyleType.kstCharacter : StyleType.kstParagraph); ... }; also Create(LcmCache cache, Guid guid) "Create a new style with a fixed guid". LcmStyleSheet.PutStyle(sName, sUsage, hvoStyle, hvoBasedOn, hvoNext, nType, fBuiltIn, fModified, ITsTextProps ttp): "lcmStyle.Type = (StyleType)nType; ... lcmStyle.Rules = ttp;"
findings.implication: FDAT can create e.g. an 'FDAT Band: Foreground' character style (Rules = ForeColor/BackColor/Bold props) via ServiceLocator.GetInstance<IStStyleFactory>().Create(LangProject.StylesOC, ...) inside a UOW, then set ktptNamedStyle on runs. Using the fixed-GUID overload (plus StylesOC.Add) lets two machines create the identical object so FLExBridge merges by GUID instead of producing duplicates.

findings.claim: FLExBridge splits LangProject.Styles into General/FLExStyles.style, merges it with the common FieldWorks 3-way merger, and its validator fails a .style file that contains two styles with the same Name.
findings.evidence: GeneralDomainBoundedContext: "// LP Styles (OC-StStyle) is used by everyone, but Scripture, so they go here. BaseDomainServices.NestStylesPropertyElement(... langProjElement.Element(FlexBridgeConstants.Styles), Path.Combine(generalBaseDir, FlexBridgeConstants.FLExStylesFilename));" StyleFileTypeHandlerStrategy.ValidateFile: finds "styleWithSameName" and returns "Duplicate Styles: ..."; Do3WayMerge => FieldWorksCommonFileHandler.Do3WayMerge(mergeOrder, mdc, true); Extension = "style".
findings.implication: Styles do sync. But if FDAT on two machines each creates a new style with the same name (different GUIDs) before syncing, the merged .style file has duplicate names and fails FLExBridge validation. Mitigation: deterministic GUIDs per FDAT style name, and always look up by name before creating.

findings.claim: The chart body is a RootSite whose root object is displayed with the project stylesheet; the Notes cell is added with AddStringProp(ConstChartRow.Notes) and is the only editable cell (row-number and data cells are explicitly set ktptNotEditable).
findings.evidence: ConstChartBody : RootSite; "m_rootb.SetRootObject(m_hvoChart, Vc, ConstChartVc.kfragChart, StyleSheet);" MakeNoteCell: "OpenNoteCell(); m_vwenv.AddStringProp(ConstChartRowTags.kflidNotes, m_this);" OpenNoteCell: "// LT-8545 remaining niggle; Note shouldn't be formatted. ... m_this.ApplyFormatting(m_vwenv, \"normal\"); m_vwenv.OpenTableCell(1, 1);" (no ktptNotEditable) vs OpenRowNumberCell "// Row number cell should not be editable [LT-7744]. vwenv.set_IntProperty(ktptEditable ... ktptNotEditable)" and MakeDataCell "set_IntProperty((int)FwTextPropType.ktptEditable, ..., ktptNotEditable)"
findings.implication: Row.Notes is edited in place in the chart with the views engine, so styled runs (named character styles, hyperlink runs) render there and are clickable via DoHotLinkAction. The 'normal' paragraph formatting is cell-level; run-level ktptNamedStyle should still render (INFERRED from views behaviour, verify visually in Phase 0).

findings.claim: FLEx's Insert menu offers 'Link to File...' (CmdInsertLinkToFile) and 'Paste Hyperlink' globally; only the Reversal Indices, RDE and Word Analyses tools set AllowInsertLinkToFile=false, so the interlinear/chart tool and Text Info tab allow inserting file links by hand.
findings.evidence: Main.xml: <command id="CmdInsertLinkToFile" label="L_ink to File..." message="InsertLinkToFile" icon="ExternalLink"/>, <command id="CmdPasteHyperlink" label="Paste _Hyperlink" message="PasteUrl"/>, menu item <item command="CmdInsertLinkToFile"/>; AllowInsertLinkToFile bool="false" only in Lexicon/ReversalIndices, Lexicon/RDE, Words/Analyses toolConfiguration.xml; FwXWindow.OnDisplayInsertLinkToFile enables when EditingHelper is RootSiteEditingHelper && CanInsertLinkToFile().
findings.implication: Users can also create/repair such links manually in FLEx, and FDAT-made links look identical to hand-made ones.

findings.claim: Segment represents a sentence-length unit and owns a sequence of Note objects (NotesOS); each Note has a single MultiString Content. ConstChartRow.Notes is a single non-multilingual TsString (sig String) on a row whose ClauseType is Normal/Dependent/Song/Speech.
findings.evidence: Segment: "Represents a sentence or segment length part of a paragraph." <owning num="4" id="Notes" sig="Note" card="seq"/>; Note: "Used for all manner of notes." <basic num="1" id="Content" sig="MultiString"/>; ConstChartRow: <basic num="1" id="Notes" sig="String"/>, ClauseType "enum with these values: Normal, Dependent, Song, Speech"
findings.implication: Segment notes = per sentence, many per sentence, multi-WS; Row.Notes = per clause row, exactly one, single WS. FDAT per-row free text maps naturally to Row.Notes; anything per sentence could use a Segment Note, but FLEx users also use those for their own notes.

findings.claim: Chart rows are linked to segments only indirectly: ConstChartWordGroup references BeginSegment/EndSegment plus BeginAnalysisIndex/EndAnalysisIndex, and DsConstChart.BasedOn references the StText.
findings.evidence: ConstChartWordGroup props: <rel num="1" id="BeginSegment" sig="Segment" card="atomic"/> <rel num="2" id="EndSegment" .../> BeginAnalysisIndex/EndAnalysisIndex "Indicate the words that occur in the indicated cell of the chart."; DsConstChart: <rel num="1" id="BasedOn" card="atomic" sig="StText"/> <owning num="2" id="Rows" card="seq" sig="ConstChartRow"/>
findings.implication: A row can cover part of a segment and a segment can span several rows, so a Segment Note cannot be assumed to belong to exactly one row; per-row data should key on ConstChartRow GUIDs, not segments.

findings.claim: FLEx edits Segment notes in the Interlinear 'Note' line: a menu command creates an INote and appends it to seg.NotesOS (auto-enabling the Note line), deletion removes it from NotesOS, and the note text is displayed/edited as Note.Content via AddStringAltMember in a RootSite-based view.
findings.evidence: InterlinDocForAnalysis: "var note = Cache.ServiceLocator.GetInstance<INoteFactory>().Create(); seg.NotesOS.Add(note);" ... "if (Vc.LineChoices.IndexInEnabled(InterlinLineChoices.kflidNote) < 0) { Vc.LineChoices.Add(InterlinLineChoices.kflidNote); ...}"; DeleteNote: "segment.NotesOS.Remove(note);"; InterlinVc: "case InterlinLineChoices.kflidNote: label = ITextStrings.ksNote_; flid = NoteTags.kflidContent;" and "vwenv.AddObjVecItems(SegmentTags.kflidNotes, this, kfragSegFfChoices + ispec);" and AddFreeformComment "vwenv.AddStringAltMember(flidTarget, ws, this);"
findings.implication: Styled runs in a Segment Note render in the interlinear Note line (views engine), but the line is hidden unless the user enables 'Note' in Configure Interlinear; FDAT-created notes would appear alongside the linguist's own notes.

findings.claim: Deleting chart rows in FLEx dumps their Notes text to <project>/SavedNotes.txt, and the chart exporter writes Row.Notes as a <note> element via WriteStringProp.
findings.evidence: ConstituentChartLogic: "string path = System.IO.Path.Combine(Cache.ProjectId.ProjectFolder, \"SavedNotes.txt\"); ... if (row.Notes != null && row.Notes.Text != null) ... sw.WriteLine(row.Notes.Text);"; DiscourseExporter.AddStringProp: "case ConstChartRowTags.kflidNotes: WriteStringProp(tag, \"note\", 0);"
findings.implication: Row.Notes is treated by FLEx as user prose (rescued on delete, exported as text); putting machine data or links there would surface in exports and in SavedNotes.txt.

findings.claim: A TsString run can carry a CmObject GUID as a 'hot' link (kodtNameGuidHot=3 / kodtOwnNameGuidHot=5, 8 chars of GUID bytes after the type char); the displayed text comes from the view constructor's GetStrForGuid and clicking calls DoHotLinkAction; if the property is on a normal character rather than U+FFFC the character displays normally but the hot behaviour still applies.
findings.evidence: "Next 8 characters give the GUID of a CmObject. A string obtained from this object using GetStrForGuid (typically its name in the first analysis writing system) is displayed. The string will be hot: when clicked, the system calls DoHotLinkAction ... (Note: if this property is associated with a character other than 0xfffc, the character is displayed normally, but the hot link behavior still happens when clicked.) kodtNameGuidHot = 3"; TsStringUtils.GetObjData/InsertOrcIntoPara/CreateOrcFromGuid build such runs.
findings.implication: The data model can express a GUID link to a possibility, but whether FLEx renders it depends on the view constructor (next finding).

findings.claim: FLEx's shared view constructor cannot render GUID hot links to arbitrary objects: FwBaseVc.GetStrForGuid handles only footnotes and pictures and otherwise throws; VwBaseVc.DoHotLinkAction acts only on kodtExternalPathName; no other DoHotLinkAction override exists in Src/Common, Src/xWorks or Src/LexText (only StringSlice, which also handles only external paths). The cursor becomes a hand over such runs.
findings.evidence: FwBaseVc.GetStrForGuid: "if (obj is IScrFootnote) return GetFootnoteIconString(...); if (obj is ICmPicture) return GetPictureString(); throw new NotImplementedException(\"Cannot get a string for objects other than footnotes and pictures.\");"; VwBaseVc.GetStrForGuid base: "No reasonable base implementation exists ... throw new NotImplementedException();"; VwBaseVc.DoHotLinkAction: "if (strData.Length > 0 && (int)strData[0] == (int)FwObjDataTypes.kodtExternalPathName) {...}" (nothing else); EditingHelper.GetCursor returns Cursors.Hand for kodtNameGuidHot/kodtOwnNameGuidHot/kodtExternalPathName; grep for DoHotLinkAction/kodtNameGuidHot across Src/Common, Src/xWorks, Src/LexText found only VwBaseVc, StringSlice, FwBaseVc and Scripture back-translation footnote code.
findings.implication: Do NOT write kodtNameGuidHot/kodtOwnNameGuidHot runs into Notes/Description: an ORC run would make FLEx views throw when rendering the string, and a non-ORC run shows a hand cursor that does nothing. Also kodtOwnNameGuidHot implies ownership semantics (delete-on-delete) FLEx would not honour for a possibility.

findings.claim: The supported way to hyperlink to a FLEx object is an external-link run whose URL is a FieldWorks link: silfw://localhost/link?app=...&database=...&tool=<toolId>&guid=<objectGuid>&tag=...; 'Copy Location as Hyperlink' produces it, 'Paste Hyperlink' inserts it as a kodtExternalPathName run styled 'Hyperlink', and on click LinkListener.HandleLocalHotlink follows it in-process when the database matches (otherwise the OS silfw protocol handler launches FieldWorks).
findings.evidence: FwLinkArgs: kSilScheme = "silfw"; kFwUrlPrefix = "silfw://localhost/link?"; ToString builds UriBuilder(kSilScheme, kLocalHost) Path="link" with query "tool={ToolName}&guid={TargetGuid}&tag={Tag}" (FwAppArgs adds app/database); LinkListener.OnCopyLocationAsHyperlink: "var args = new FwAppArgs(cache.ProjectId.Handle, m_currentContext.ToolName, m_currentContext.TargetGuid); ClipboardUtils.SetDataObject(args.ToString(), true);"; HandleLocalHotlink: "if(!url.StartsWith(FwLinkArgs.kFwUrlPrefix)) return; var fwargs = new FwAppArgs(new[] {url}); if (SameDatabase(fwargs, cache)) { OnFollowLink(fwargs); args.LinkHandledLocally = true; }"; RootSiteEditingHelper.ConvertSelToLink calls FwLinkArgs.FixSilfwUrlForCurrentProject before MarkTextInBldrAsHyperlink.
findings.implication: FDAT can make a clickable link to a possibility (e.g. a chart marker or salience band) by writing an external-link run whose URL is the silfw link; FLEx jumps to the object. Build the URL with FwAppArgs/FwLinkArgs (FwUtils.dll) or reproduce its format; the DB name portion must match the project (use database=this$ or the project name).

findings.claim: The FLEx tool id for the Chart Markers possibility list is 'chartmarkEdit' (list owned by DsDiscourseData.ChartMarkers).
findings.evidence: <command id="CmdJumpToDiscChartMarkerList" label="Show in {0} list" message="JumpToTool"><parameters tool="chartmarkEdit" className="CmPossibility" ownerClass="DsDiscourseData" ownerField="ChartMarkers"/></command>
findings.implication: A silfw link with tool=chartmarkEdit&guid=<marker guid> opens that marker in the Lists area; a custom FDAT list under Text Markup Tags would use that list's tool id (textMarkupTagsEdit or similar; verify).

findings.claim: CmPossibility owns an optional StText 'Discussion' (rich multi-paragraph text) in addition to Name/Abbreviation/Description, plus ForeColor/BackColor/UnderColor/UnderStyle/Hidden/IsProtected; StText owns Paragraphs (StTxtPara.Contents is a formatted String) and Tags.
findings.evidence: CmPossibility props: Name MultiUnicode, Abbreviation MultiUnicode, Description MultiString, <owning num="12" id="Discussion" card="atomic" sig="StText">, ForeColor/BackColor/UnderColor Integer, UnderStyle, Hidden, IsProtected; StText: <owning num="1" id="Paragraphs" card="seq" sig="StPara"/>, <owning num="3" id="Tags" sig="TextTag" card="col"/>; StTxtPara.Contents sig String "allows for embedded formatting".
findings.implication: A possibility (e.g. an FDAT band or the FDAT list's root item) can carry a link run or notes in Description or Discussion paragraphs; Discussion is an StText so it could hold a multi-paragraph, styled anchor block too.

findings.claim: flexlibs only wraps TsStringUtils.MakeString for plain strings; there is no helper for styled runs or links, but it imports the LCM types (ITsString, ITsStrBldr, TsStringUtils) through pythonnet, so StringServices.MarkTextInBldrAsHyperlink, IStStyleFactory and LcmStyleSheet are reachable the same way.
findings.evidence: FLExProject.py: "from SIL.LCModel.Core.KernelInterfaces import ITsString, ITsStrBldr" "from SIL.LCModel.Core.Text import TsStringUtils" ... "mkstr = TsStringUtils.MakeString(newValue, WSHandle)"; no occurrences of ktpt*, hyperlink or props builders in the file.
findings.implication: FDAT's sidecar must call the .NET APIs directly (import SIL.LCModel.DomainServices.StringServices etc.) and wrap writes in a UOW; flexlibs offers no shortcut for rich text.

openQuestions: Does the installed Chorus build in FLExBridge really cap unknown extensions at 1 MiB (LargeFileFilter.Megabyte fallback) or was the fallback raised to 10 MB in 2022? The summarised fetch showed Megabyte => 1048576 and a comment about raising 'the limit' to 10 MB; confirm by committing a ~2 MB .json under LinkedFiles/Others on a real Send/Receive.

Does the chart's Notes cell visually honour run-level named character styles and the Hyperlink style, given OpenNoteCell's comment 'Note shouldn't be formatted' and ApplyFormatting(vwenv, "normal")? Verify on screen; the code only sets cell-level paragraph formatting.

Does Process.Start on a .json path do something useful on a colleague's machine (default association is often a text editor or browser)? Consider registering an fdat:// URL scheme so the link opens FDAT, or point the link at the chart's silfw URL instead.

Which silfw 'database' value survives Send/Receive best (project name vs this$)? FixSilfwUrlForCurrentProject rewrites pasted links to the current project; confirm links FDAT writes with database=<name> still resolve after a colleague renames the project.
What is the tool id for a sub-list under Text Markup Tags (for silfw links to FDAT band possibilities)? Only chartmarkEdit was confirmed.

Is IStStyleFactory.Create(LcmCache, Guid) usable from outside LCM for a fixed-GUID style (it creates an unowned object that must then be added to LangProject.StylesOC), and does FLEx's stylesheet cache (LcmStyleSheet) pick up styles added by another process on next open? Test in Phase 0.

Whether FLEx (as opposed to the model) tolerates a hyperlink run inside ConstChartRow.Notes when the row is deleted (SavedNotes.txt dump uses .Text only) and when 'Export Text Chart' runs (WriteStringProp writes text; check whether href is emitted).

result.summary: Documentation sweep of the GitHub-hosted sources (SIL sites blocked). The developer-facing docs (flexbridge ReadMe/FileTypeHandlers, liblcm README/AGENTS, FieldWorks ReadMe/CLAUDE/AGENTS/CONTEXT/Docs, FLExTools wiki, chorus README, FlexToolsMCP README) contain almost nothing prescriptive about custom fields, linked files, or text tags; the substantive facts for FDAT storage come from code and comments adjacent to those docs. Key results: (1) Send/Receive syncs only an explicit include list (FlexFolderSystem.cs) - "LinkedFiles/Others/**.*", "LinkedFiles/Pictures/**.*", "LinkedFiles/AudioVisual/**.*", "SupportingFiles/**.*", "FLExProject.CustomProperties", "**.list", "**.style", "Linguistics/Discourse/<chart file>", plus split model files; "**.xml", "**.flextext", "**.zip", "**.log", "**.tmp", ".fwdata" and video extensions are excluded, and exclude has precedence. So an FDAT JSON in LinkedFiles/Others WOULD be synced as long as it is not named *.xml, and it is subject to Chorus's LargeFileFilter: files with an unknown extension (e.g. .json) get the DefaultFileTypeHandler limit of 1 MiB (audio/picture handlers were raised to 10 MB in 2022); an over-size file is silently added to the exclude list with a notification, and a file that grows too large is "forgotten". Unknown-extension files get no 3-way merge - Chorus merges only via type handlers, so a JSON blob would conflict as a whole file. (2) FLExTools/flexlibs docs establish the scripting model: OpenProject(writeEnabled=True) wraps everything in one BeginNonUndoableTask/EndNonUndoableTask + IUndoStackManager.Save on CloseProject; opening fails with FP_FileLockedError if FLEx has the project open unless the project's Sharing tab option "Share project contents with programs on this computer" is enabled (FwProjPropertiesDlg, ProjectLexiconSettings.ProjectSharing); data migration from a script is deliberately forbidden ("something a FieldWorks user should explicitly decide"). flexlibs custom-field helpers exist only for LexEntry/LexSense/LexExampleSentence/MoForm classes, but are implemented generically via IFwMetaDataCacheManaged.GetFields + GetIsCustomField, and support String, MultiString, Integer, ReferenceAtom (single list) and ReferenceCollection (multi list) field types. FLExTools documentation recommends custom fields as the place to write script-generated tags ("LexiconAddTagToField"). (3) FieldWorks docs: every model change needs a FLEx Bridge metadata-cache migration, which is why FDAT must use extension points and never the model; Text.MediaFiles is an atomic CmMediaContainer owning a collection of CmMediaURI (so a text can reference any number of media URIs, but the model comment says "Currently a placeholder for ELAN data, not modifiable or viewable in flex as of Nov 2011"), and FLExText export round-trips media-file references without UI. (4) The "Technical Notes on FieldWorks Send-Receive" PDF is referenced in FieldWorks as Help > Resources > "Technical Notes on FieldWorks Send-Receive..." (Main.xml CmdHelpNotesSendReceive), shipped at <FW code dir>/Helps/Language Explorer/Training/Technical Notes on FieldWorks Send-Receive.pdf and published under https://software.sil.org/fieldworks/support/technical-documents/ (blocked here). Chorus's own README says documentation is essentially non-existent ("we are not really interested in supporting any further uses until things mature and someone writes good developer documentation").

findings.claim: FLEx Bridge Send/Receive includes only an explicit allow-list of paths; every file under LinkedFiles/Others, LinkedFiles/Pictures, LinkedFiles/AudioVisual and SupportingFiles is included, so a JSON file placed in LinkedFiles/Others would be committed and synced.
findings.evidence: projectFolderConfiguration.IncludePatterns.Add(Path.Combine("LinkedFiles", "AudioVisual", "**.*")); ...Add(Path.Combine("LinkedFiles", "Others", "**.*")); ...Add(Path.Combine("LinkedFiles", "Pictures", "**.*")); ...Add(Path.Combine("SupportingFiles", "**.*")); and the header comment: "Exclude has precedence, but these are redundant as long as we're using the policy that we explicitly include all the files we understand."
findings.implication: A linked-file JSON is a viable sync vehicle only if it lives in LinkedFiles/Others (or Pictures/AudioVisual/SupportingFiles); a file elsewhere in the project folder (e.g. a new top-level FDAT folder) is NOT synced unless FLEx Bridge is changed.

findings.claim: Send/Receive explicitly excludes **.xml, **.flextext, **.zip, **.log, **.tmp, **.bak, .fwdata and all video extensions, and exclude patterns take precedence over includes.
findings.evidence: projectFolderConfiguration.ExcludePatterns.Add("**.flextext"); ... Add("**.xml"); ... Add("**.zip"); ... ProjectFolderConfiguration.AddExcludedVideoExtensions(projectFolderConfiguration); with the comment "Exclude has precedence". Chorus: foreach (var videoExtension in VideoExtensions) { projectFolderConfiguration.ExcludePatterns.Add("**." + videoExtension); }
findings.implication: An FDAT sidecar must NOT use the .xml (or .flextext/.zip) extension even inside LinkedFiles/Others, or it will never be synced. .json is not in the exclude list.

findings.claim: Chorus's LargeFileFilter limits files by extension: a file whose extension has no specific IChorusFileTypeHandler falls back to the DefaultFileTypeHandler limit of 1 MiB; audio/picture handlers use 10 MiB (raised from 1 MB in 2022). Over-size files are added to the exclude list with a user notification, and a previously-small file that grows too large is 'forgotten' (untracked).
findings.evidence: LargeFileFilter.cs: "Filter the files, before the commit. Files that are too large are added to the exclude section of the configuration."; GetMaxSizeForExtension: if (!extensionToMaximumSize.TryGetValue(extension, out maxForExtension)) { maxForExtension = Megabyte; }; message "File '{0}' is too large to include in the Send/Receive system. It is {1}, but the maximum allowed is {2}." and "File '{0}' has grown too large to include in the Send/Receive system."; 2022.03 comment: "we are increasing the limit to 10 MB. This will allow the inclusion of high-quality photos and .wav files up to 56 seconds." DefaultFileTypeHandler.MaximumFileSize => LargeFileFilter.Megabyte; AudioFileTypeHandler.MaximumFileSize => LargeFileFilter.Megabyte * 10. FLExBridge CHANGELOG: "Increase the audio and picture file size limit from 1 MB to 10 MB".
findings.implication: An FDAT JSON linked file must stay under 1 MiB (INFERRED: .json has no dedicated handler in Chorus/FLEx Bridge, so the default applies) or it silently drops out of Send/Receive with only a notification message; one large JSON per text rather than one per project mitigates this, but it is a hard ceiling.

findings.claim: Chorus performs 3-way, schema-aware XML merging only through file-type handlers; FLEx Bridge splits the fwdata model into per-domain files so each has modular merge logic. Files with no handler (e.g. an arbitrary JSON) are merged by the default handler, i.e. as opaque whole files.
findings.evidence: FileTypeHandlers.md: "FileTypeHandlers are used to define custom handling logic for different types of files managed by Chorus. They are used to merge, identify conflicts, or process files... FlexBridge breaks the fwdata file into a model based hierarchy. Different major portions of the model are split into separate files so that merging logic can be modular and specific. FlexBridge also handles the merging of configuration files and other non-model project data." Chorus README: "3-Way, schema-savvy XML merging. Various policies can be implemented for choosing a winner in the case of conflicts. Regardless of the policy, details of the conflict are logged in an XML file which also under version control."
findings.implication: Data stored inside LCM objects (custom fields, tags, possibility lists) gets per-object/per-field merging with conflict reports; a JSON sidecar gets whole-file last-writer-wins style conflict handling (INFERRED from absence of a JSON handler), so concurrent edits by two colleagues to the same text's FDAT JSON would clobber each other.

findings.claim: FLEx Bridge treats FLExProject.CustomProperties as a first-class synced file and orders it right after the model version file; custom fields therefore travel through Send/Receive by design.
findings.evidence: projectFolderConfiguration.IncludePatterns.Add("FLExProject.ModelVersion"); // Hope this forces the version file to be done first. projectFolderConfiguration.IncludePatterns.Add("FLExProject.CustomProperties"); // Hope this forces the custom props to be done next.
findings.implication: Custom fields (definitions and values) are a supported, merge-aware sync path for FDAT data.

findings.claim: Discourse charts have their own synced file and merge handler in FLEx Bridge (Linguistics/Discourse), and possibility lists (**.list) and styles (**.style) are synced as separate files.
findings.evidence: projectFolderConfiguration.IncludePatterns.Add("**.list"); ...Add("**.style"); ...Add(Path.Combine("Linguistics", "Discourse", FlexBridgeConstants.DiscourseChartFilename));
findings.implication: Chart rows/cells, custom possibility lists (e.g. an FDAT salience-band list) and custom styles all have existing merge handling; keying FDAT data to these GUIDs rides on tested S/R paths.

findings.claim: Every change to the FieldWorks data model requires both a liblcm data migration and a corresponding FLEx Bridge metadata-cache migration, otherwise Send/Receive stops working for migrated projects.
findings.evidence: "Every change to the FieldWorks data model requires a corresponding data migration." ... "There MUST be a corresponding metadata cache migration in FLEx Bridge. If you don't create this, you won't be able to use FLEx Bridge Send/Receive with projects that have been migrated."
findings.implication: Confirms the rule that FDAT must never add model classes/properties; only runtime extension points (custom fields via the metadata cache, lists, tags, linked files, styles) are safe.

findings.claim: All LCModel writes must occur inside a unit of work under IActionHandler; UndoableUnitOfWorkHelper / NonUndoableUnitOfWorkHelper are the sanctioned wrappers.
findings.evidence: "Unit of work: Groups data-model changes under IActionHandler. All LCModel writes must occur inside one. UndoableUnitOfWorkHelper (undoable) and NonUndoableUnitOfWorkHelper (non-undoable) are in SIL.LCModel.Infrastructure; use as a using block or via their static .Do(...) helpers." Also: "LcmCache: Root entry point to LCModel... Exposes the language project, writing system factory, action handler, and ServiceLocator."
findings.implication: FDAT's desktop writer must wrap every LCM mutation in a unit of work (flexlibs does this with one BeginNonUndoableTask per session).

findings.claim: flexlibs opens a project via LcmCache.CreateCacheFromExistingData with DisableDataMigration=True, and when writeEnabled it brackets the whole session in one BeginNonUndoableTask/EndNonUndoableTask and saves with IUndoStackManager.Save() on CloseProject.
findings.evidence: settings.DisableDataMigration = True  # Migration should be done within FieldWorks ... return LcmCache.CreateCacheFromExistingData(projId, "en", ui, dirs, settings, dlg). FLExProject.OpenProject: if self.writeEnabled: self.project.MainCacheAccessor.BeginNonUndoableTask(). CloseProject: self.project.MainCacheAccessor.EndNonUndoableTask(); usm = self.ObjectRepository(IUndoStackManager); usm.Save(); self.project.Dispose(). history.md 1.1.3: "FLExProject now requires a CloseProject() call to save data and release the lock on the FLEx project."
findings.implication: A proven template for FDAT's writer: open via flexlibs (or LCM directly), one non-undoable task, explicit Save+Dispose; changes are not persisted until CloseProject.

findings.claim: Opening a project from a script fails with a file-lock error if FieldWorks has it open, unless the project's Sharing tab option 'Share project contents with programs on this computer' is turned on; that flag is ProjectLexiconSettings.ProjectSharing stored in the project settings store.
findings.evidence: FLExProject.OpenProject docstring: "A call to OpenProject() may fail with a FP_FileLockedError exception if the project is open in Fieldworks (or another application). To avoid this, project sharing can be enabled within the Fieldworks Project Properties dialog. In the Sharing tab, turn on the option 'Share project contents with programs on this computer'." (except LcmFileLockedException as e: raise FP_FileLockedError()). FLExTools Help.doc: "If you try running a module on a project that is open in FieldWorks, then you will get an error message about the project being in use by another program. You must either close the project in FieldWorks, or configure the project to allow multiple programs to access it at the same time... File | Project Management | FieldWorks Project Properties, and select the Sharing tab." flextools history 2.1.2: "FLEx has a sharing mode that allows FLExTools to run on a project even when it is open in FieldWorks." FwProjPropertiesDlg.cs: m_enableProjectSharingCheckBox.Checked = m_projectLexiconSettings.ProjectSharing; resx value "Share project contents with programs on this computer".
findings.source: flexlibs/flexlibs/code/FLExProject.py:208-232; flextools/docs/src/FLExTools Help.doc (section 'Project sharing', extracted via strings); flextools/history.txt:205-208; FieldWorks/Src/FwCoreDlgs/FwProjPropertiesDlg.cs:139-146; FieldWorks/Src/FwCoreDlgs/FwProjPropertiesDlg.resx:2140
findings.implication: FDAT desktop can run concurrently with FLEx only when the user enables project sharing (which switches LCM to the shared XML backend, INFERRED); otherwise FDAT must require FLEx to be closed, or run inside FLExTools with the same restriction.

findings.claim: External programs must not perform data migration; a project needing migration must be opened in FieldWorks first (explicit FieldWorks-team guidance).
findings.evidence: # Raised if the FW project needs to be migrated to a later version. The user needs to open the project in FW to do the migration. # Jason Naylor [Dec2018] said not to do migration from an external program: "We think that is something a FieldWorks user should explicitly decide." raise FP_MigrationRequired()
findings.implication: FDAT must set LcmSettings.DisableDataMigration and surface a 'open in FLEx first' error rather than migrating.

findings.claim: flexlibs enumerates custom fields generically through the metadata cache (GetFields + GetIsCustomField) and supports custom-field values of type String, MultiString, Integer, ReferenceAtom (single list item) and ReferenceCollection (multiple list items); its convenience wrappers only cover LexEntry, LexSense, LexExampleSentence and MoForm classes.
findings.evidence: mdc = IFwMetaDataCacheManaged(self.project.MetaDataCacheAccessor); for flid in mdc.GetFields(classID, False, int(CellarPropertyTypeFilter.All)): if self.project.GetIsCustomField(flid): yield ((flid, mdc.GetFieldLabel(flid))). GetCustomFieldValue: "Returns the field value for String, MultiString, Integer and List (both single and multiple) fields. Raises FP_ParameterError for other field types." Wrappers: LexiconGetEntryCustomFields / LexiconGetSenseCustomFields / LexiconGetExampleCustomFields / LexiconGetAllomorphCustomFields. history 1.2.7: "Added support for Lists (single or multiple) in GetCustomFieldValue(); Added ListFieldPossibilityList(); ListFieldPossibilities(); ListFieldLookup(); LexiconSetListFieldSingle(); LexiconSetListFieldMultiple()".
findings.implication: The same MDC calls work for any class (INFERRED: nothing in the code restricts classID), so FDAT can locate/read custom fields on ConstChartRow etc. with the same pattern, but it will need its own helpers since flexlibs ships none for discourse classes; list-valued custom fields (e.g. salience band) are a supported field type.

findings.claim: FLExTools documentation recommends custom fields as the sanctioned place for script-written tags/flags, and notes custom fields can be created in FLEx at entry or sense level (documentation scope only).
findings.evidence: "Custom fields can be defined in FieldWorks at entry or sense level. The following helper functions are supplied in FLExProject to get a list of all the custom fields, or to locate a custom field by name" ... "Where automated changes have risks ... it is helpful to use a custom field as a place to flag the need for attention. LexiconAddTagToField() is provided for doing just this. It will append a tag string to the end of the given field and insert semi-colons (;) between tags." ... "FTFlags should be created in FieldWorks as a sense-level 'Single-line text' field using the 'First Analysis Writing System.' Note that field names are case-sensitive."
findings.source: flextools/docs/src/FLExTools Programming.doc (sections 'Custom fields' and 'Modifying the FieldWorks project', extracted via strings)
findings.implication: The doc describes creating custom fields in the FLEx UI; it says nothing about creating them programmatically. Whether FLEx's Custom Field dialog offers discourse-chart classes is a question for the FieldWorks-source investigation, not answered by any doc here.

findings.claim: FLExTools' safety model: modules receive a modifyAllowed flag that is False (dry run) unless the user explicitly chooses Run (Modify); FLExTools raises an exception on any write attempt when modifyAllowed is False, and a module must declare FTM_ModifiesDB: True to ever get write access.
findings.evidence: "The third parameter, modifyAllowed... By default, FLExTools passes False as a protection against accidental changes. It is only when the user clicks the Run (Modify) buttons or holds down the Shift key... (FLExTools will raise an exception if an attempt is made to change the project, but modifyAllowed is False.) Additionally, the module documentation value FTM_ModifiesDB must be set to True if the module can make changes to the project. FLExTools will never pass through True if FTM_ModifiesDB is False." flexlibs setters: if not self.writeEnabled: raise FP_ReadOnlyError.
findings.implication: If FDAT ships as a FLExTools module it inherits this dry-run/modify workflow; a standalone desktop app should replicate a read-only default and explicit write mode.

findings.claim: A Text owns at most one CmMediaContainer (atomic), which in turn owns any number of CmMediaURI objects; the model documents this as an ELAN placeholder that FLEx neither edits nor displays.
findings.evidence: Text: <owning num="12" id="MediaFiles" card="atomic" sig="CmMediaContainer"> "A container for media files which are associated with this text, and possibly referenced by segments in the text." CmMediaContainer: "This class collects any number of MediaURIs and provides an offset type"; "Currently a placeholder for ELAN data, not modifiable or viewable in flex as of Nov 2011 -NaylorJ"; <owning num="2" id="MediaURIs" card="col" sig="CmMediaURI"/>; CmMediaURI.MediaURI (Unicode): "The location and offset of the media file, this should be a subset of the MediaFragment specification." FieldWorks flextext doc: "FLEx has no UI for this data but stores and round-trips it, because ELAN and SayMore populate it for audio/video-aligned transcription."
findings.implication: Answers the owner's question: yes, a Text can carry more than one media reference (a collection of CmMediaURI strings), but these are plain URI strings intended for audio/video time alignment, with no FLEx UI, no CmFile/LinkedFiles-folder semantics, and they are round-tripped through FLExText/ELAN/SayMore import-export; hijacking them for an FDAT JSON pointer is a semantic misuse (INFERRED) and other tools may interpret the URI as media.

findings.claim: The 'Technical Notes on FieldWorks Send-Receive' document is a PDF opened from FLEx's Help > Resources menu and shipped in the FieldWorks install under Helps/Language Explorer/Training; the publicly hosted technical documents live at software.sil.org/fieldworks/support/technical-documents (blocked in this environment).
