findings.claim: Other SIL technical documents the FLExTools wiki points to for the data model (FLEx 9.1 Conceptual Model PDF, Python for FlexTools and FLEx 9.1 PDF, ModelDocumentation.chm, MasterFieldWorksModel classes-and-fields spreadsheet 7000072) are hosted on downloads.languagetechnology.org (blocked here); the wiki says MasterLCModel.xml on GitHub is the latest model definition and the CHM is outdated (FW 7.2; 'Interlinear text is not correct').
findings.evidence: "The model is described in FW 9.1 Conceptual Model (https://downloads.languagetechnology.org/fieldworks/Documentation/FLEx%209.1%20Conceptual%20Model.pdf). Detailed information on using the LCM with Python... Python for FlexTools and FLEx 9.1 (https://downloads.languagetechnology.org/fieldworks/Documentation/Python%20for%20FlexTools%20and%20FLEx%209.1.pdf)... The MasterLCModel XML file, which is the latest model definition... (This was built for the FieldWorks 7.2 model, so a number of things are out of date: Interlinear text is not correct...)"

findings.claim: Chorus supports marking files as team-shared vs user-specific and lets applications tell it which files are individual-specific or should not be shared; it also has a built-in notes system attached to data.
findings.evidence: "Files can be marked as shared by the team or user-specific. This allows things like preferences/configurations to be part of the repository but kept separate for each individual." ... "Applications generally know where their important files are, which files are individual-specific, and which should not be backed-up/shared at all. Applications that know about Chorus pass this information to it" ... "A built-in 'notes' system which makes it very cheap to give users the ability to add notes to any piece of data". FLEx Bridge includes **.ChorusNotes and excludes **.NewChorusNotes.
findings.implication: FDAT per-user display preferences should not be stored in shared project data; the README describes a capability, but only FLEx Bridge's include list (not any per-user mechanism) governs what a FLEx project actually syncs (INFERRED).

findings.claim: FLEx Bridge also syncs cached configuration settings (.fwlayout, .fwdictconfig, Overrides.css, .ldml, .plsx) and the General/ files for filters, annotations, unowned pictures and virtual ordering.
findings.evidence: IncludePatterns.Add(Path.Combine("CachedSettings", "ConfigurationSettings", "*.fwlayout")); ..."**.fwdictconfig"; ..."**Overrides.css"; ..."WritingSystemStore", "*.ldml"; ..."SharedSettings", "*.plsx"; ...Add(Path.Combine("General", FlexBridgeConstants.FLExFiltersFilename)); ...FLExAnnotationsFilename; ...FLExUnownedPicturesFilename; ...FLExVirtualOrderingFilename
findings.implication: Shows that FLEx already syncs some non-model configuration through dedicated files with handlers; there is no generic 'any project settings file' include, so an FDAT config file outside LinkedFiles/SupportingFiles would not sync.

findings.claim: The Chorus project's own documentation is acknowledged to be minimal and it does not support new consumers.
findings.evidence: "Chorus is functional and being used in several applications with different development teams. However, we are not really interested in supporting any further uses until things mature and someone writes good developer documentation. Documentation (what little exists) was kept on this blog (http://chorussr.wordpress.com/), which contains three posts from August 2009."
findings.implication: Adding a JSON merge handler to Chorus/FLEx Bridge for FDAT is not a realistic path; FDAT should rely on the existing model-object merge by storing data in LCM objects.

findings.claim: FlexToolsMCP documents nothing about linked files, media or custom fields; it is an API-index/code-generation server (LibLCM 2,295 entities, FlexLibs ~71 methods, Flexicon ~1,400 methods) that runs generated code dry-run by default and requires a backup and explicit write_enabled=True for mutations.
findings.evidence: "FLExTools MCP gives AI assistants... indexed, searchable documentation of LibLCM and FlexLibs APIs." "API Coverage - LibLCM: 2,295 C# entities - FlexLibs Stable: ~71 methods - Flexicon: ~1,400 methods". "Always backup before write operations - the MCP defaults to dry-run mode". "Cannot control the FLEx GUI (filters, display, etc.) - Only manipulates data, not UI state". USAGE.md: "flextools_run_module - Execute code against a FieldWorks project (dry-run by default, write_enabled=true for mutations)". Grep of README.md, USAGE.md and docs/WHY-MCP.md for 'custom', 'linked', 'media' found no relevant statements.
findings.implication: FlexToolsMCP (and its Flexicon wrapper) may help generate LCM code for FDAT but provides no guidance on the storage design question.

findings.claim: flexlibs/FLExTools require Python and FieldWorks architectures to match and support only Windows for FieldWorks 9.x (Linux path abandoned); flexlibs 1.2.8 supports FieldWorks 9.0.17-9.3.1, FLExTools up to 9.3.8.
findings.evidence: README.rst: "Python 3.8 - 3.13. Python for .NET version 3.0.3+. FieldWorks Language Explorer 9.0.17 - 9.3.1. The Python architecture must match that of FieldWorks." Wiki FLExTools-v2: "Unfortunately there are a number of obstacles to getting FLExTools to work with Fieldworks 9.1 and recent versions of Ubuntu. As of mid-2024 there's no solution in sight." flextools README: "FieldWorks Language Explorer 9.0.17 - 9.3.8."
findings.implication: Consistent with PLAN.md's Windows-only desktop app; flexlibs pins to specific FieldWorks version ranges, so FDAT must track FLEx releases.

findings.claim: FLEx's Send/Receive setup note ties collaboration to the default project folder location.
findings.evidence: "Note: If you will collaborate with Send/Receive or by sharing the project over a network connection, use the default folder location."
findings.implication: FDAT should resolve project paths through FwDirectoryFinder.ProjectsDirectory (as flexlibs does in FLExLCM.GetListOfProjects) rather than assuming custom locations.

(Docs only say it lets another program open the project; the mechanism is in liblcm Infrastructure/Impl/SharedXMLBackendProvider.cs - another investigation should confirm.)

Does Chorus/FLEx Bridge register any IChorusFileTypeHandler for .json (or a generic text handler with a larger limit)? The default handler's 1 MiB limit and whole-file merge are inferred from the absence of one; confirm by listing handlers in chorus/src/LibChorus/FileTypeHandlers and flexbridge/src/LibFLExBridge-ChorusPlugin/Handling.

Is there any FLEx UI or LCM API that lets a CmFile/linked file be attached to a Text (as opposed to CmMediaURI strings or CmPicture on senses)? Docs found none; the model shows Text.MediaFiles -> CmMediaContainer -> CmMediaURI (Unicode URI) only.

Which classes does FLEx's Custom Field dialog (and IFwMetaDataCacheManaged.AddCustomField) allow custom fields on? The FLExTools docs mention only entry/sense (plus example/allomorph helpers); whether ConstChartRow / ConstChartWordGroup / TextTag accept custom fields must be checked in liblcm's metadata cache and FieldWorks' AddCustomFieldDlg.

The actual content of 'Technical Notes on FieldWorks Send-Receive.pdf' (what it says about LinkedFiles, size limits, and 'do_not_share_project.txt') could not be read here; the owner should open it from FLEx Help > Resources or software.sil.org/fieldworks/support/technical-documents/.
How does FLEx Bridge handle a LinkedFiles/Others file on the receiving side (does FLEx re-link it, or is it just a synced blob)? Nothing in the docs addresses it.

CmMajorObject at MasterLCModel.xml:240-258 is `<class num="5" id="CmMajorObject" abstract="true" ... base="CmObject">` with Name (MultiUnicode), DateCreated (Time), DateModified (Time), Description (MultiString), Publications (owning col Publication), HeaderFooterSets (owning col PubHFSet). CmObject itself has an empty `<props/>` (MasterLCModel.xml, class num="0"), so nothing further is inherited at model level. The model file is version 7000072 (line 207).

Cross-checks that could have refuted it did not: (1) FLExBridge's own MetadataCache lists the same six Text props plus an historical `SoundFilePath` (Unicode) in its base definition (flexbridge/src/LibFLExBridge-ChorusPlugin/Infrastructure/MetadataCache.cs:1605-1612), but that property is removed at DM 7000046 and replaced by `MediaFiles` OA (MetadataCache.cs:224-229: "Remove: SoundFilePath ... Add: OA MediaFiles [CmMediaContainer]"), so the current-model list matches. (2) FLExBridge CmMajorObject definition matches the six inherited props (MetadataCache.cs:647-654). (3) "Exactly" holds for the static model; LCM's AddCustomField accepts any class name (liblcm/src/SIL.LCModel/Infrastructure/Impl/LcmMetaDataCache.cs:920-950, only CheckClid + name-uniqueness checks), but FLEx's UI never offers Text as a custom-field host: FieldWorks/Src/xWorks/AddCustomFieldDlg.cs:109-127 offers only LexEntry, LexSense, LexExampleSentence, MoForm (Lexicon), Segment (Interlinear) and RnGenericRec (Notebook). So Text only gains extra properties if a tool adds them programmatically (inference).

The stated implications also check out: (a) Text is unowned and FLExBridge writes each Text as its own top-level file `Linguistics\TextCorpus\Text_<guid>.textincorpus` with root `<TextInCorpus><Text ...>` (flexbridge/src/LibFLExBridge-ChorusPlugin/Contexts/Linguistics/TextCorpus/TextCorpusBoundedContextService.cs:20-25 "The Text instances are all unowned, as of DM 59 ... Each Text instance will be in its own file, along with everything it owns"; :86-101; FlexFolderSystem.cs:75; Handling/Linguistics/TextCorpus/TextCorpusFileTypeHandlerStrategy.cs:33-44 validates root name TextInCorpus with a Text child). (b) CmMediaContainer owns `<owning num="2" id="MediaURIs" card="col" sig="CmMediaURI"/>` (MasterLCModel.xml:1647-1656), and CmMediaURI holds a single Unicode `MediaURI` string (MasterLCModel.xml:1632-1646) - so more than one media file per text is possible at model level; FLEx's BIRD import populates multiple MediaURIs (FieldWorks/Src/LexText/Interlinear/BIRDInterlinearImporter.cs:1372-1392) and export writes them (InterlinearExporter.cs:884-889). Caveats (inferred, not contradictions): the model comment "not modifiable or viewable in flex as of Nov 2011" is stale - FLEx shows a Media slice on the text Info pane (DistFiles/Language Explorer/Configuration/Parts/CellarParts.xml, part Text-Detail-Media -> MediaInfoSlice) but it renders MediaURI strings non-editable (Src/Common/Controls/DetailControls/MediaInfoSlice.cs, MediaInfoVc sets ktptNotEditable); and CmMediaURI is a bare URI string, not a CmFile/CmFolder LinkedFiles object, which matters for the "linked file of the text" design idea. Also Text.Description and Text.Source are user-visible/editable in FLEx as "Comment" and "Source" (CellarParts.xml parts Text-Detail-CommentAllWs / Text-Detail-SourceAllWs; Words/Texts/toolConfigInclude.xml columns "Source" and "Comment"), so any FDAT payload stored there would be visible and editable by users.

result.reason:
The citation is accurate as far as it goes: flexbridge/src/LibFLExBridge-ChorusPlugin/Infrastructure/FlexFolderSystem.cs:61-64 literally adds IncludePatterns LinkedFiles/AudioVisual/**.*, LinkedFiles/Others/**.*, LinkedFiles/Pictures/**.* and SupportingFiles/**.*, and lines 14-17 carry the 'explicitly include all the files we understand' comment. The implication that an FDAT .json placed under <project>/LinkedFiles/Others (including a subfolder) is carried by Send/Receive is CONFIRMED, and the '**' inference is now sourced rather than inferred: Mercurial's _globre turns '**' into '.*' and '*' into '[^/]*' (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/indygreg/hg/master/mercurial/match.py:1034-1077; -I/-X patterns are normalized with kind 'glob', lines 189,194), and Chorus's own test IncludeFilesInSubFolders (chorus src/LibChorusTests/VcsDrivers/Mercurial/IncludeExcludeTests.cs:148-178) uses the analogous 'others/**.*' pattern (src/LibChorus/FileTypeHandlers/lift/LiftFolder.cs:41, comment 'Including nested folders/files') and asserts others/subothers/good.other is in the repository.

The claim AS STATED, however, overstates and omits qualifications that the same cited file contains and that the FDAT design depends on:
(1) 'only ... by explicit include pattern' / implicit 'everything in those folders is synced' is wrong: FlexFolderSystem.cs:14 says 'Exclude has precedence', Chorus ProjectFolderConfiguration.cs:29-31 says excludes 'take precedence over any includePatterns', and HgRepository.cs:882-898 passes every include as 'hg add -I' and every exclude as '-X'. FlexFolderSystem.cs:18-45 excludes at all depths **.xml, **.zip, **.log, **.tmp, **.bak, **.orig, **.flextext, **.fwbackup, **.fwstub, **.bad, **.lint, **.oxes/.oxesa/.oxekt, **.fwdata(+-replaced/-x/.lock), **.dupid and 13 video extensions (ProjectFolderConfiguration.cs:68-98). So LinkedFiles/Others/fdat.xml would NOT be synced; .json is not on any exclude list and would be.
(2) 'A file anywhere else in the project folder (project root, ConfigurationSettings, ...) is not synced' is literally contradicted by FlexFolderSystem.cs:47-52 (root files FLExProject.ModelVersion, FLExProject.CustomProperties, do_not_share_project.txt, .hgignore), 55-58 (**.ChorusNotes, **.list, **.style at every level; Chorus adds **.ChorusRescuedFile, Synchronizer.cs:842) and 66-68 plus BaseDomainServices.cs:32,55,179-185,217-235 (FLExBridge copies <project>/ConfigurationSettings into CachedSettings/ConfigurationSettings before each commit and back after each merge, and includes *.fwlayout, **.fwdictconfig, **Overrides.css from there). The practical point survives only in narrowed form: an arbitrary .json in root or ConfigurationSettings is not synced.
(3) Omitted size limit: Synchronizer.cs:389 runs LargeFileFilter before every commit; for an extension no handler claims (.json: DefaultFileTypeHandler.cs:76-79 yields none, TextFileTypeHandler.cs:135 only 'txt', FLExBridge FieldWorksCommonFileHandler.cs:199-204 only its own FLEx extensions) the maximum is LargeFileFilter.Megabyte = 1,048,576 bytes (LargeFileFilter.cs:67,145-153); an oversize file is added to ExcludePatterns and, if already tracked, 'hg forget'-ted with only a progress warning (LargeFileFilter.cs:135-140, Synchronizer.cs:390-395). The 10 MiB limit in the 2022 comment (LargeFileFilter.cs:50-54) applies only to image/audio handlers (ImageFileTypeHandler.cs:86, AudioFileTypeHandler.cs:82).
(4) Omitted location caveat: patterns are resolved against the hg repo root = project folder (HgRepository.cs:888 Path.Combine(_pathToRepository, pattern)). result.summary: Answer: for owning COLLECTIONS and reference COLLECTIONS, FLExBridge keeps both sides' independently added objects without any conflict report. The mechanism: the property element (e.g. StText_Tags, LangProject_Styles, CmFolder_Files, CmMediaContainer_MediaURIs, Custom_<Class>_<name>) gets a singleton strategy with OrderIsRelevant=false and the default AskChildren order policy; the child objects are matched by guid (class strategy: MergePartnerFinder=GuidKeyFinder, OrderIsRelevant=false; refcol: FindByKeyAttribute(guid), order false). Chorus's MergeChildrenMethod only raises AmbiguousInsertConflict when the inserted child's strategy says order is relevant (IsAmbiguous bypasses the check otherwise), and both FLExBridge (Anthropology/Reversal WinnerAndLoserEachAddedNewElement: 0 conflicts, 2 XmlAdditionChangeReports, both guids present) and Chorus (Run_BothAddedDifferentKeyedNodes_OrderIrrelevant_NoConflict) have tests for exactly this. By contrast the same both-add on an owning SEQUENCE (ownseq, order relevant) or on an unsorted possibility list produces AmbiguousInsertConflict (FLExBridge MergeList_HasAmbiguousInsertConflict_OnlyIfUnsorted; Chorus Run_BothAddedDifferentKeyedNodes_OrderIsRelevant_OrderAmbiguityConflict). LCM additionally writes all collection objsur children in guid-sorted order, so both machines' split files agree on child order and the residual 'inconsistent order' branch of the merger cannot fire for pure additions. Caveats that matter for FDAT: (1) StStyle merge is by guid, not name, so if two colleagues each create an FDAT style with the same Name (different guids) the merged Styles file fails FLExBridge validation (duplicate names) and, if it got through, FixFwData's DuplicateStyleFixer deletes the later duplicate and LcmStyleSheet throws on duplicates - so FDAT must create styles with deterministic, pre-agreed guids or names that include a machine/user discriminator, or create them on one machine and sync before others use them. (2) CmFile/TextTag/CmMediaURI have no name-uniqueness validation, so duplicates from two machines are simply both kept; FDAT must reconcile (e.g. two 'FDAT sidecar' CmFiles or two TextTags on the same row) on load. (3) Both-add semantics apply only to distinct objects; two machines editing the same object's atomic fields still conflict per the existing strategies, and the linked file itself (LinkedFiles/Others/**) is synced as an opaque file with no 3-way merge.

findings.claim: For every OwningCollection and ReferenceCollection property of every concrete class (including custom ones), the property element's merge strategy is a singleton with OrderIsRelevant=false, IsAtomic=false, NumberOfChildren=ZeroOrMore and default ChildOrderPolicy (AskChildren); nothing else is configured for collections.
findings.evidence: AddPropertyStrategiesForClass: `var propStrategy = isCustom ? CreateStrategyForKeyedElement(FlexBridgeConstants.Name, false) : CreateSingletonElementStrategy();` then `//case DataType.OwningCollection: // Nothing special done` and `//case DataType.ReferenceCollection: // Nothing special done`. CreateSingletonElementStrategy -> ElementStrategy.CreateSingletonElement() which is `new ElementStrategy(false) { MergePartnerFinder = new FindFirstElementWithSameName() }`; the constructor sets `NumberOfChildren = ZeroOrMore; ChildOrderPolicy = new AskChildrenOrderPolicy()`. The FLExBridge tests OwningCollectionDataTypeReportTests/ReferenceCollectionDataTypeReportTests assert exactly IsAtomic=false, OrderIsRelevant=false, IsImmutable=false, ZeroOrMore, FindFirstElementWithSameName for all such properties.
findings.implication: Order is never treated as significant inside StText.Tags, CmFolder.Files, LangProject.Styles, CmMediaContainer.MediaURIs or a custom reference-collection field; the merge of their children is a set merge keyed by guid.

findings.claim: Children of an owning collection are emitted as elements named by their class (e.g. <Tags><TextTag guid=.../>) and merged with the class strategy: MergePartnerFinder = guid key, IsAtomic=false, OrderIsRelevant=false (constructed with `new ElementStrategy(false)`). Reference-collection children are renamed to <refcol guid=... t='r'/> and use a guid-keyed strategy with orderIsRelevant=false (attribute 't' ignored).
findings.evidence: MakeClassStrategy: `var classStrat = new ElementStrategy(false) { ContextDescriptorGenerator = defaultDescriptor, MergePartnerFinder = GuidKeyFinder, IsAtomic = false };`. CmObjectNestingService.RenameElement: for non-sequence owning props `obj.Name = className; classAttr.Remove();` (only sequences become <ownseq>). Refcol: `// Order is not important in any kind of collection property ... elementStrategy = CreateStrategyForKeyedElement(FlexBridgeConstants.GuidStr, false); elementStrategy.AttributesToIgnoreForMerging.Add("t");`. Key mapper comment: `// There is no need for an OwnCol, since order in irrelevant for them.` Validator test builds `<StText><Tags><TextTag guid=...><BeginAnalysisIndex/>...` and it validates.
findings.implication: A TextTag/CmFile/StStyle/CmMediaURI/custom-refcol entry added on machine A can never be 'matched' against a different one added on machine B: distinct guids are distinct children, each seen as a one-sided addition.

findings.claim: Chorus's MergeChildrenMethod keeps a child that exists only on one side and has no ancestor as an addition (XmlAdditionChangeReport), and only raises AmbiguousInsertConflict when order matters: with the parent policy AskChildren, IsAmbiguous() bypasses the ambiguity test for any inserted child whose strategy has OrderIsRelevant=false; BothReorderedElementConflict likewise requires childOrderMatters.
findings.evidence: Run(): `var childOrderMatters = parentOrder == ChildOrder.Significant; if(parentOrder == ChildOrder.AskChildren && parentNode.HasChildNodes) { var childStrategy = ...GetElementStrategy(parentNode.FirstChild); if(childStrategy != null && childStrategy.OrderIsRelevant) childOrderMatters = true; }` ... `if (ancestorOursOrderer.OrderIsDifferent && childOrderMatters) { ConflictOccurred(new BothReorderedElementConflict...) } else { // only they re-ordered; take their order as primary }` ... `else if (resultOrderer.OrderIsAmbiguous) ConflictOccurred(new AmbiguousInsertConflict...)`. IsAmbiguous(): `if (_parentOrder == ChildOrder.AskChildren) { var strategy = GetElementStrategy(pr._other); bypassAmbiguityStuff = (strategy != null && !strategy.OrderIsRelevant); } ... if (!bypassAmbiguityStuff && pr.OrderIsAmbiguous(_primary.Count)) return true;`. Addition path: `if (ancestorChild == null) ... if (theirChild == null) ChangeOccurred(new XmlAdditionChangeReport(...)) else ChangeOccurred(new XmlBothAddedSameChangeReport(...))`; GetResultList() interleaves both lists so unmatched 'other' nodes are appended into ours.
findings.implication: With FLExBridge's strategies (class and refcol children OrderIsRelevant=false, parent AskChildren) both sides' new collection members are retained and reported as plain additions; no conflict note is generated and nothing is dropped.

findings.claim: Chorus has a direct unit test for the both-added-different-keyed-children, order-irrelevant case with no conflict, and the mirror test showing the same data conflicts (AmbiguousInsertConflict) when the child strategy is order-relevant.
findings.evidence: `Run_BothAddedDifferentKeyedNodes_OrderIrrelevant_NoConflict`: ours `<foo><gloss lang='a'>..`, theirs `<foo><gloss lang='b'>..`, ancestor `<foo/>`; `merger.MergeStrategies.SetStrategy("gloss", ElementStrategy.CreateForKeyedElement("lang", false)); ... TestMergeWithoutConflicts(...)`. `Run_BothAddedDifferentKeyedNodes_OrderIsRelevant_OrderAmbiguityConflict`: same shape with `CreateForKeyedElement("lang", true)` -> `TestMerge<AmbiguousInsertConflict>`. XmlMergerTests.EachAddedDifferentSyblings_GetBoth gets AmbiguousInsertConflict only because its helper installs `CreateForKeyedElement("key", true)` for every element.
findings.implication: The 'order irrelevant' flag FLExBridge assigns to collection children is exactly the switch that turns a both-add from a conflict into a clean union.

findings.claim: FLExBridge itself has end-to-end tests where each side adds a different new object to the same owning collection and the merge yields both objects, zero conflicts and two XmlAdditionChangeReports: RnResearchNbk.Records (RnGenericRec) and ReversalIndex.Entries (ReversalIndexEntry), plus a nested owning collection (ReversalIndexEntry.Subentries) receiving an addition while the parent collection gets another.
findings.evidence: Anthropology `WinnerAndLoserEachAddedNewElement`: ours adds `<RnGenericRec guid='newbieOurs'/>`, theirs `<RnGenericRec guid='newbieTheirs'/>`; DoMerge asserts xpaths for oldie, newbieOurs and newbieTheirs, `0, new List<Type>()` conflicts and `2, new List<Type> { typeof(XmlAdditionChangeReport), typeof(XmlAdditionChangeReport) }`. Reversal `WinnerAndLoserEachAddedNewElement` identical pattern; `WinnerAddedNewEntryLoserAddedNewSubentry` asserts `.../Subentries/ReversalIndexEntry[@guid=...c5...]` present with 0 conflicts. (In these split files the collection's children are the root's direct children; the strategy for them is the same class strategy as for a nested <Tags> or <Files> element.)
findings.implication: This is the concrete both-sides-add owning-collection behaviour the question asks about: both kept, no conflict. There is no TextTag-specific test, but StText.Tags is an OwningCollection handled by the identical generic code path (inferred from the generic property-strategy generation, no special case exists).

findings.claim: The contrasting case: when both sides add different items to an owning SEQUENCE (ownseq, OrderIsRelevant=true / SignificantOrderPolicy) or an unsorted possibility list, FLExBridge reports AmbiguousInsertConflict (items are still both kept, but a conflict note is written).
findings.evidence: `MergeList_HasAmbiguousInsertConflict_OnlyIfUnsorted`: both sides add a new <ownseq class='CmAnnotationDefn'> at two levels; with IsSorted=False expects `2, new List<Type> { typeof(AmbiguousInsertConflict), typeof(AmbiguousInsertConflict) }, 4, ... XmlAdditionChangeReport x4`; comment: 'When the list is unsorted, we want ambiguous insert conflicts, because the user is in control of the order'. Ownseq strategy: `CreateStrategyForKeyedElement(FlexBridgeConstants.GuidStr, true)`; owning-sequence property: `propStrategy.ChildOrderPolicy = new SignificantOrderPolicy();`.
findings.implication: Confirms chart-anchors 5.4: FDAT should not rely on colleagues independently adding to owning sequences (DsConstChart.Rows, ConstChartRow.Cells, Text.MediaFiles which is card='seq') for anchor objects; collections are the conflict-free choice. Note Text.MediaFiles is an owning SEQUENCE of CmMedia (MasterLCModel.xml:2888) while CmMediaContainer.MediaURIs is an owning COLLECTION (line 1654).

findings.claim: LCM writes every owning/reference collection's objsur children (including custom-field collections) in guid-sorted order in the fwdata file, and FLExBridge's flatten step restores collections such as LangProject.Styles in sorted order; therefore both machines' split files list common members in the same order and the merger's residual 'inconsistent order' branch (AmbiguousInsertReorderConflict, which is not gated by OrderIsRelevant) cannot be triggered by pure additions.
findings.evidence: LcmSet stores members in `HashSet<ICmObjectOrId> m_items` and ToXMLString just iterates it; but XMLBackendProvider calls `DataSortingService.SortMainElement(sortableProperties, ...)` for every written rt element, and SortMainElement -> `if (collData.Contains(propName)) SortCollectionProperties(propertyElement);` where custom props are looked up by their name attribute; SortCollectionProperties: `// Write collection properties in guid sorted order, since order is not significant in collections.` GetSortableProperties adds `CellarPropertyType.OwningCollection` and `ReferenceCollection` field names for every concrete class. MergeChildrenMethod: `if (!resultOrderer.OrderIsConsistent || (resultOrderer.OrderIsDifferent && resultOrderer.OrderIsAmbiguous)) ConflictOccurred(new AmbiguousInsertReorderConflict...)`; PositionRecord.OrderIsConsistent = `HasExactPosition || indexofPrecedingPrimaryNode < indexOfFollowingPrimaryNode`. FLExBridge flatten: `// Restore LP Styles property in sorted order.`
findings.implication: Removes the one theoretical path by which a collection both-add could still yield a conflict note (arbitrary HashSet order on the two machines). Inferred from reading the ordering algorithm; not covered by a dedicated test.

findings.claim: LangProject.Styles is split into a single file General/*.style whose root <Styles> holds each <StStyle guid=...> as a direct child; the style file validator rejects a file containing two StStyles with the same Name (returns 'Duplicate Styles: {name} with guids X and Y'), and Chorus's CommitCop treats a validation failure after merge as fatal: the project is rolled back to the last Send/Receive.
findings.evidence: NestStylesPropertyElement: `// Use only one file for all of them. var root = new XElement(FlexBridgeConstants.Styles); ... root.Add(style)`. StyleFileTypeHandlerStrategy.ValidateFile: compares `style.Element("Name").Element(Uni).Value` across styles and builds `"Duplicate Styles: " ... " with guids " ...`; test DuplicateStylesAreNotValid. Synchronizer.Commit: `commitCopValidationResult = commitCop.ValidationResult; ... _sychronizerAdjunct.SimpleUpdate(_progress, true); throw new ApplicationException("The changed data did not pass validation tests. Your project will be moved back to the last Send/Receive before this problem occurred...")`. CommitCop.ValidateModifiedFiles calls handler.ValidateFile on each modified file.
findings.implication: For LangProject.Styles the guid-keyed both-add is technically conflict-free, but two colleagues independently creating an FDAT style with the same Name yields a merged file that fails validation and can roll back the whole Send/Receive. FDAT must either use fixed, pre-agreed GUIDs for its styles (so both machines' additions match as 'both added same'), or include a per-user/per-machine discriminator in the name, or create styles once and sync before others run FDAT.

findings.claim: LCM and FixFwData also enforce style-name uniqueness: FixFwData (run after every merge by FLExBridge's PrepareForPostMergeCommit) deletes the second StStyle seen with the same (Name, owner) and strips its objsur from LangProject.Styles; LcmStyleSheet.LoadStyles throws DuplicateItemException if two loaded styles have the same name.
findings.evidence: DuplicateStyleFixer.InspectElement: `var key = Tuple.Create(name, owner); if (m_stylesSeen.Contains(key)) { m_deletedGuids.Add(guid); } m_stylesSeen.Add(key); // if we see another delete it`; FixElement logs `ksRemovingDuplicateStyle` and returns false; LangProject/Scripture branch removes matching objsur. FwDataFixer registers `new DuplicateStyleFixer()`. FlexBridgeSynchronizerAdjunct.PrepareForPostMergeCommit: `RestoreProjectFile(progress); ... if (RunFixFwData(progress)) { ... FLExProjectSplitter.PushHumptyOffTheWall(...) }`. LcmStyleSheet.LoadStyles: `if (m_StyleInfos.Contains(styleInfo)) throw new DuplicateItemException($"Duplicate style found: {styleInfo.Name}");`.
findings.implication: Even if a duplicate-name style pair got past validation, one copy would be silently deleted (the one appearing later in guid order), and any FDAT data keyed to the deleted style's guid would dangle. Reinforces: never let two machines mint same-named styles with different guids.

findings.claim: CmFile (CmFolder.Files), TextTag (StText.Tags) and CmMediaURI (CmMediaContainer.MediaURIs) have no name/path uniqueness validation in FLExBridge or FixFwData, so duplicates created on two machines both survive the merge; LCM's own dedupe (FindOrCreateFile) is only a same-machine convenience that compares InternalPath and file bytes within one CmFolder.
findings.evidence: DomainObjectServices.FindOrCreateFile: `foreach (ICmFile file in folder.FilesOC) { if (FileUtils.PathsAreEqual(file.AbsoluteInternalPath, srcFile) && FileUtils.AreFilesIdentical(...)) return file; } ... folder.FilesOC.Add(cmFile); cmFile.InternalPath = srcFile;`. FixData folder contains only BasicCustomPropertyFixer, CustomListNameFixer, CustomPropertyFixer, DuplicateStyleFixer, DuplicateWordformFixer, GrammaticalSenseFixer, HomographFixer, MorphBundleFixer, SequenceFixer (no CmFile/TextTag fixer). TextTag model: BeginSegment/EndSegment (ref atomic Segment), Begin/EndAnalysisIndex (Integer), Tag (ref atomic CmPossibility) - no uniqueness comment; the only LCM TextTag side effects are AnalysisAdjuster deleting tags whose referenced text is edited away (`owner.TagsOC.Remove(iar as ITextTag)`).
findings.implication: For these anchors the merge is safe but not idempotent across machines: FDAT can end up with two 'FDAT' CmFiles in the same folder, or two TextTags spanning the same row created by two users. FDAT's loader must treat these as sets (choose by deterministic rule, or merge their payloads), and ideally create such objects with deterministic GUIDs derived from (chart guid, row guid, purpose) so both machines produce the same guid and the merger reports XmlBothAddedSameChangeReport instead of two objects.

findings.claim: Where each FDAT collection would live in the sync tree: StText.Tags and CmMediaContainer.MediaURIs nest inside Linguistics/TextCorpus/Text_<guid>.textincorpus (each Text with everything it owns); LangProject.Styles goes to General/*.style; CmFolder objects owned by LangProject (Media/Pictures folders, hence CmFolder.Files) stay nested inside General/LanguageProject.langproj because nothing extracts them before the LangProject remainder is nested and written; the LinkedFiles/{AudioVisual,Others,Pictures} directories are synced as plain files.
findings.evidence: TextCorpusBoundedContextService: 'Each Text instance will be in its own file, along with everything it owns (nested ownership as well)' and `CmObjectNestingService.NestObject(false, textElement, ...)`; GeneralDomainBoundedContext: after extracting lists, Styles, Filters, unowned pictures and VirtualOrderings, `// Yippee!! Write LP here. :-) ... CmObjectNestingService.NestObject(false, langProjElement, classData, guidToClassMapping); FileWriterService.WriteNestedFile(... LanguageProjectFilename ...)`; grep of Contexts for Media/CmFolder finds no separate handler. FlexFolderSystem: `IncludePatterns.Add(Path.Combine("LinkedFiles", "Others", "**.*"))` etc.
findings.implication: All four collection anchors are merged by the same generic per-object, guid-keyed code regardless of which file they land in; the CmFolder placement inside the LangProject file is inferred from absence of a dedicated context (not spot-checked against a real split project).

findings.claim: A custom ReferenceCollection field is handled identically: its <Custom name=...> element gets strategy Custom_<Class>_<name> (keyed by name, order false) and its objsur children are renamed <refcol> and merged by guid with order irrelevant; custom-property collections are also guid-sorted by LCM on write.
findings.evidence: `var propStrategy = isCustom ? CreateStrategyForKeyedElement(FlexBridgeConstants.Name, false) : ...`; RenameReferenceCollectionObjsurNodes: `var propNode = refColProp.IsCustomProperty ? obj.Elements("Custom").FirstOrDefault(pi => pi.Attribute(Name).Value == refColProp.PropertyName) : obj.Element(refColProp.PropertyName); ... objsurNode.Name = FlexBridgeConstants.Refcol;`; key mapper `case "Custom": ... combinedCustomKey = key + "_" + className + "_" + customPropName`; LCM SortMainElement `if (propName == "Custom") propName = propertyElement.Attribute("name").Value; if (collData.Contains(propName)) SortCollectionProperties(propertyElement);`.
findings.implication: A custom reference-collection field on DsConstChart or ConstChartRow (e.g. pointing at FDAT possibility items) can be independently extended on two machines without conflict; the union of both sides' references is kept.

openQuestions: No FLExBridge test exercises a both-sides-add on a NESTED owning collection inside another object (e.g. <StText><Tags>); the root-level Anthropology/Reversal tests and the Chorus nephew-level test with order-irrelevant strategy together cover the mechanism, but an actual TextTag both-add through the FieldWorksCommonFileHandler has not been run here.

Whether FLEx's own text-tagging UI or InterlinearTaggingChild tolerates two TextTags with identical span and Tag on the same segment (duplicates that a both-add could produce) - only LCM/FLExBridge behaviour was checked, not the FieldWorks UI (sparse checkout, not grepped for this).

Whether two CmFile objects in one CmFolder pointing at the same InternalPath cause any problem in FLEx's LinkedFiles handling (e.g. the 'Move linked files' dialog); LCM's FindOrCreateFile only dedupes at creation time on one machine.

The claim that CmFolder objects remain nested inside General/LanguageProject.langproj is inferred from the absence of a Media/Pictures extractor in Contexts; not verified against a real split project.

How Chorus's LargeFileFilter treats an FDAT JSON sidecar placed under LinkedFiles/Others (size limit and the fact that non-XML files get no 3-way merge - last writer wins or binary conflict) was outside this gap's scope and should be checked before adopting the linked-file idea.

result.summary: End-to-end trace of a custom OwningAtomic StText field (FLEx's "Multiparagraph text" custom-field type) through FLExBridge and FixFwData. (1) NESTING: the split registers custom-property definitions in FLExBridge's MetadataCache before any rt data is cached, mapping LCM's `type="OA"` to `OwningAtomic`; the custom prop therefore lands in the class's "AllOwning" cache and CmObjectNestingService nests the owned StText (and its StTxtPara/Segment tree) under `<Custom name="…">` exactly like a built-in owning property, replacing the `<objsur t="o">`; flattening has an explicit custom-owning branch that restores the objsur. A real fixture (RnGenericRec `<Custom name='Like'><StText>…<ownseq class='StTxtPara'>`) exists in FLExBridge's tests. (2) VALIDATION: CmObjectValidator resolves `<Custom>` by its name attribute and, for DataType.OwningAtomic, calls ValidateOwningAtomicProperty with isCustomProperty=true, which skips the attribute check and validates the single nested child object; the two-attribute rule applies only to basic value types. (3) MERGE: the custom OA property gets a name-keyed, non-atomic, ZeroOrOne-child strategy (`Custom_Text_<name>`); the nested `<StText guid>` is merged by the StText class strategy (GUID-keyed, per-element), `Paragraphs` with SignificantOrderPolicy, each `ownseq` StTxtPara by guid, and only each paragraph's `<Str>` is atomic. So the JSON merges per paragraph with order significance, NOT as one string — PLAN §5/§7's "merges as one string" claim is wrong for this field type (it would be true only for a String/Unicode custom field). The Text and its custom StText live together in Linguistics/TextCorpus/Text_<guid>.textincorpus, whose handler passes addCustomPropertyInformation=true. (4) CLEANUP: if the definition is removed, CustomPropertyFixer strips the undefined `<Custom>` element from the Text; FwDataFixer's multi-pass loop then removes the StText as a "disowned object" on the next pass and its StTxtPara/Segments as "object with nonexistent owner" on subsequent passes — deleted, not orphaned. LCM's own delete path (FieldDescription.UpdateCustomField) explicitly DeleteObjOwner's the owned StText before DeleteCustomField, whose contract requires data removal first. (5) UI caveats: FLEx's Custom Fields dialog never offers class Text, and the Text "FullInformation" detail layout has no `customFields` marker, so an FDAT field on Text is neither creatable/deletable in the dialog nor shown in the Info tab (contradicting PLAN §5's "shows up in the text's Info tab"); it must be created via IFwMetaDataCacheManaged.AddCustomField(…, OwningAtomic, destinationClass=StText). Design consequence: put one logical unit (e.g. one chart, or one row's data) per paragraph so concurrent edits to different units merge cleanly.

findings.claim: FLExBridge nests an owned object under a `<Custom name="…">` element exactly as under a built-in owning property: the nesting service derives the property name from the name attribute, checks it against the class's cached "AllOwning" set, replaces each `<objsur t="o">` with the owned object's element and recurses down the ownership tree.
findings.evidence: `var isCustomProperty = propertyElement.Name.LocalName == FlexBridgeConstants.Custom; var propName = isCustomProperty ? propertyElement.Attribute(FlexBridgeConstants.Name).Value : …; if (!owningProps.Contains(propName)) continue; … owningObjSurElements = propertyElement.Elements(Objsur).Where(objsurEl => objsurEl.Attribute("t").Value == "o") … objsurElement.ReplaceWith(ownedElement); NestObject(isOwningSeqProp, ownedElement, classData, guidToClassMapping);` with `owningProps = MetadataCache.MdCache.PropertyCache[className]["AllOwning"]`.
findings.implication: A custom OwningAtomic StText field on Text is serialised in the split as `<Text><Custom name="FDAT data"><StText guid=…><Paragraphs><ownseq class="StTxtPara" guid=…><Contents><Str>…` — the same tree shape as built-in Text.Contents — so the JSON paragraphs are visible to Chorus as structured elements, not opaque text.

findings.claim: The "AllOwning" property cache includes custom properties: custom props are added to a class's direct properties and ResetCaches recomputes _allOwningProperties from all properties whose DataType is OwningAtomic/OwningCollection/OwningSequence; the cache is built only for concrete classes.
findings.evidence: `_allOwningProperties.AddRange(from prop in _allProperties where prop.DataType == DataType.OwningAtomic || … OwningCollection || … OwningSequence select prop)` after `_allProperties.AddRange(_directProperties)`; `AddCustomPropInfo` does `_classes[className].AddProperty(propInfo)`; CacheProperties iterates `AllConcreteClasses`.
findings.implication: Declaring the field on the concrete class `Text` (which is `abstract="false"`) guarantees the nesting/flattening code treats it as owning.

findings.claim: LCM writes the custom-field definition with the abbreviated type code `type="OA"` for OwningAtomic (plus `destclass`), and FLExBridge converts it to `OwningAtomic` (via AdjustedPropertyType) when it writes FLExProject.CustomProperties during the split, before any rt records are cached; so `FdoPropertyInfo.DataType` (an Enum.Parse of the stored type) resolves to DataType.OwningAtomic both at split time and at merge time.
findings.evidence: LCM: `case CellarPropertyType.OwningAtomic: retval = "OA"` and `new XAttribute("type", GetFlidTypeAsString(…)), (m_destinationClass != 0) ? new XAttribute("destclass", …)`. FLExBridge: `var adjustedTypeValue = MetadataCache.AdjustedPropertyType(typeAttr.Value); if (adjustedTypeValue != typeAttr.Value) typeAttr.Value = adjustedTypeValue; … mdc.AddCustomPropInfo(className, customProp); … mdc.ResetCaches();`; splitter: `if (foundOptionalFirstElement) { FileWriterService.WriteCustomPropertyFile(mdc, pathRoot, record); … } else { CacheDataRecord(...) }`; `case OA: adjustedType = OwningAtomic`; `DataType { … OwningAtomic, … }`; `DataType => (DataType)Enum.Parse(typeof(DataType), _allPropertyValues["type"])`.
findings.implication: No special handling is needed for the owning variant; the type mapping that makes nesting/merge see the field as owning is already in place for the built-in Multiparagraph-text custom field type.

findings.claim: During merge, FLExBridge re-registers custom-property definitions from FLExProject.CustomProperties (skipping unknown classes) before building merge strategies; the TextCorpus (.textincorpus) handler passes addCustomPropertyInformation=true.
findings.evidence: `foreach (var customFieldElement in doc.Element(AdditionalFieldsTag).Elements(CustomField)) { … if (!_classes.TryGetValue(className, out classInfo)) continue; … AddCustomPropInfo(className, new FdoPropertyInfo(customFieldElement)); } ResetCaches();` and `public void Do3WayMerge(MetadataCache mdc, MergeOrder mergeOrder) { FieldWorksCommonFileHandler.Do3WayMerge(mergeOrder, mdc, true); }` / `if (addCustomPropertyInformation) mdc.AddCustomPropInfo(mergeOrder); // NB: Must be done before FieldWorksCommonMergeStrategy is created`.
findings.implication: The merge of Text files knows about the custom owning field, so its per-class strategies (including for the nested StText) are generated with the custom prop present.

findings.claim: CmObjectValidator accepts a `<Custom>` element with a nested owned child: it resolves the property by the name attribute, dispatches on the property's DataType, and for OwningAtomic calls ValidateOwningAtomicProperty with isCustomProperty=true, which skips the 'no attributes' check, rejects more than one child, and validates the single child as a CmObject. The two-attribute rule (BasicValueTypeAttributeCheckIsValid) only applies to basic value types.
findings.evidence: `var isCustomProperty = propertyElement.Name.LocalName == FlexBridgeConstants.Custom; var propertyName = isCustomProperty ? propertyElement.Attribute(Name).Value : …; if (!allPropertyNames.Contains(propertyName)) return … "Not a property element child"; … case DataType.OwningAtomic: result = ValidateOwningAtomicProperty(mdc, isCustomProperty, propertyElement, nextIndentationLevel);` and `if (!isCustomProperty && propertyElement.HasAttributes) return "Has unrecognized attribute(s)"; var children = propertyElement.Elements().ToList(); return (children.Count > 1) ? "Has too many child elements" : ((children.Count == 0) ? null : ValidateObject(mdc, children[0], indentation));`; `BasicValueTypeAttributeCheckIsValid … if (isCustomProperty) { if (element.Attributes().Count() != 2) …`.
findings.implication: A Text file containing `<Custom name="FDAT data"><StText …>` passes FLExBridge validation (the nested StText/StTxtPara are validated recursively like any object), so Send/Receive will not reject the file.

findings.claim: Flattening (rebuilding the .fwdata from the split) has an explicit branch for custom owning properties: it removes the nested child, flattens it recursively, and restores an `<objsur t="o">` under the `<Custom>` element.
findings.evidence: `if (isCustomProperty) { var owningPropertyElement = (element.Elements().Where(customNode => customNode.Name.LocalName == Custom && … == propertyElement.Attribute(Name).Value)).First(); ownedElement.Remove(); FlattenObjectCore(pathname, sortedData, ownedElement, elementGuid); // BEFORE we make the objsur! BaseDomainServices.RestoreObjsurElement(owningPropertyElement, ownedElement); }` → `AddObjSurElement(parentProperty, ownedElement)` → `CreateObjSurElement(guid)`.
findings.implication: The round trip fwdata → split → fwdata preserves the custom OA StText; LCM then reloads it via `customPropertyElement.Element("objsur")` (CmObject.cs load path).

findings.claim: LCM serialises/loads an owning-atomic custom property value as `<Custom name="…"><objsur guid="…" t="o"/></Custom>` in the owner's rt element; the owned StText is its own rt with ownerguid=Text.
findings.evidence: Write: `case CellarPropertyType.OwningAtomic: case ReferenceAtomic: var id = (ICmObjectOrId)data; id.Id.ToXMLString(dataType == CellarPropertyType.OwningAtomic, writer);` Load: `case OwningAtomic: case ReferenceAtomic: myElement = customPropertyElement.Element("objsur"); if (myElement != null) data = surrRepos.GetId(myElement);`.
findings.implication: The on-disk shape that FLExBridge's nesting code expects (`objsur` with `t="o"` under `<Custom>`) is exactly what LCM writes.

findings.claim: An existing FLExBridge test fixture uses precisely this shape — a Data Notebook record with a custom multiparagraph field nested as `<Custom name='Like'><StText guid=…><Paragraphs><ownseq class='StTxtPara' …>` — and the context generator labels changes inside it as `Custom Field "Like"`.
findings.evidence: `<RnGenericRec guid='29fb1310-…'> … <Custom name='Like'> <StText guid='f0b19053-…'> <Paragraphs> <ownseq class='StTxtPara' guid='4125c1ed-…'> <StyleRules>…` and `Assert.That(descriptor.DataLabel, Is.EqualTo("Data Notebook Record \"Type\" Custom Field \"Like\""));`; label built by `label += Space + Resources.kCustomFieldLabel + Space + Quote + displayName + Quote;`.
findings.implication: Custom OA StText fields are an already-supported, production shape in FLExBridge (FLEx's Notebook 'Multiparagraph text' custom fields), not a novel path; only the owner class (Text instead of RnGenericRec) differs, and the nesting/merge code is class-generic. No test exercises a full 3-way merge of such a field, though.

findings.claim: Merge strategy for the custom property element: keyed by the `name` attribute (not the singleton finder), NumberOfChildren = ZeroOrOne, not atomic; registered under key `Custom_<Class>_<name>`. The key mapper derives `Custom_Text_<name>` from the `<Custom>` element's parent element name.
findings.evidence: `var propStrategy = isCustom ? CreateStrategyForKeyedElement(FlexBridgeConstants.Name, false) : CreateSingletonElementStrategy(); switch (propertyInfo.DataType) { case DataType.OwningAtomic: propStrategy.NumberOfChildren = NumberOfChildrenAllowed.ZeroOrOne; break; …} strategiesForMerger.SetStrategy(String.Format("{0}{1}_{2}", isCustom ? "Custom_" : "", classInfo.ClassName, propertyInfo.PropertyName), propStrategy);` / mapper: `case "Custom": var customPropName = element.Attributes["name"].Value; var className = element.ParentNode.Name; … combinedCustomKey = key + "_" + className + "_" + customPropName;`. Test asserts for every OwningAtomic prop incl. custom: `Assert.IsFalse(elementStrategy.IsAtomic); … Assert.AreEqual(NumberOfChildrenAllowed.ZeroOrOne, …)`.
findings.implication: The `<Custom>` wrapper itself is not an atomic merge unit; Chorus descends into the nested StText.

findings.claim: Inside the nested StText the merge is element-level: the `<StText guid>` child maps to the StText class strategy (GUID-keyed, non-atomic — every concrete class gets `MergePartnerFinder = GuidKeyFinder, IsAtomic = false` per chart-anchors 5.4), `Paragraphs` (OwningSequence) gets SignificantOrderPolicy, each `<ownseq>` StTxtPara is matched by guid, `Contents` (String) is ZeroOrOne child, and only the `<Str>` element is atomic. Hence the JSON merges per paragraph, order-significant, not as one string.
findings.evidence: Mapper: class elements `element.Attributes[GuidStr] != null && keys.Contains(key)` → key = element name ("StText"); property elements → `element.ParentNode.Name + "_" + key` (e.g. "StText_Paragraphs", "StTxtPara_Contents"); ownseq children → `element.ParentNode.Attributes["class"].Value + "_" + key`. Strategies: `case DataType.OwningSequence: … else { propStrategy.ChildOrderPolicy = new SignificantOrderPolicy(); }`; `case DataType.String: // Contains one <Str> element propStrategy.NumberOfChildren = ZeroOrOne;`; `elementStrategy = AddSharedSingletonElementType(sharedElementStrategies, FlexBridgeConstants.Str, false); elementStrategy.IsAtomic = true; // TsStrings are atomic`; `ownseq` strategy `CreateStrategyForKeyedElement(GuidStr, true)` with OwnSeqPremerger.
findings.implication: PLAN §5 item 1 and §7 ('Chorus merges it as one string: concurrent edits … conflict wholesale') are wrong for the OA-StText ('Multiparagraph text') variant; they describe a String/Unicode custom field. With an StText, the conflict unit is a single paragraph's `<Str>`; two users editing different paragraphs merge cleanly, and paragraph insert/delete merges by GUID with order significance. FDAT should therefore write one logical unit per StTxtPara (e.g. paragraph 1 = header/version, one paragraph per chart or per row) rather than one giant JSON string, and must tolerate paragraphs arriving in a merged/ordered set.

findings.claim: The Text object and everything it owns (including a custom-owned StText) are written to one file, Linguistics/TextCorpus/Text_<guid>.textincorpus, by a generic NestObject call on the Text element.
findings.evidence: `foreach (var textGuid in texts.Keys.ToArray()) { var rootElement = new XElement("TextInCorpus"); var textElement = …; CmObjectNestingService.NestObject(false, textElement, classData, guidToClassMapping); FileWriterService.WriteNestedFile(Path.Combine(textCorpusBaseDir, "Text_" + textGuid.ToLowerInvariant() + "." + FlexBridgeConstants.TextInCorpus), rootElement); }`; class comment: 'The Text instances … including all they own are stored in the TextCorpus folder.'
findings.implication: FDAT data stored on Text syncs in the same file as the text's baseline/segments; it is separate from Linguistics/Discourse/Charting.discourse where the DsConstChart lives, so chart-row GUID references inside the JSON are cross-file references (plain text in the JSON, not objsur links, so FLExBridge/FixFwData will not validate or repair them).

findings.claim: If the custom-field definition is removed but `<Custom>` data remains, FixFwData's CustomPropertyFixer deletes the undefined `<Custom>` element (and thus its owning objsur) from the owner rt, keyed by name + rt class.
findings.evidence: 'If two users are doing Send/Receive and one deletes a Custom Field … Chorus will keep the edit, but we have no way to recreate the custom field, so delete the (now) undefined custom property.' `foreach (var kvp in customProperties) { if (… m_customFieldNames.ContainsKey(kvp.Key)) continue; logger(String.Format(Strings.ksRemovingUndefinedCustomProperty, …), true); kvp.Value.Remove(); }` with key `nameKey + "_" + ownerClassAttr.Value` from `customProp.Parent.Attribute("class")`.
findings.implication: Removing the field definition on one machine while another machine still has data leads FixFwData to strip the data; the StText is then no longer referenced from the Text.

findings.claim: The stripped StText is not left orphaned: FwDataFixer iterates up to 20 passes (re-initialising ownership info each pass) until no new fixes occur; on the next pass OriginalFixer sees the StText's ownerguid pointing at an existing Text that no longer owns it and deletes it as a 'disowned object'; on subsequent passes its StTxtPara/Segment rts are deleted as 'object with nonexistent owner'.
findings.evidence: Loop: `for (int repeatCount = 0; repeatCount < 20; ++repeatCount) { … if (repeatCount > 0) { InitializeFixers(infile); …} … if (newErrorCount == currentErrorCount) break; // If no errors were fixed on this pass, we can quit.` with comment 'comfortably larger than any iteration we expect (maximum ownership chain depth + 1)' and 'Any deleting of owned objects requires two passes'. Ownership map built from all `objsur[@t='o']` descendants (`foreach (var objsur in rt.Descendants("objsur")) { … if (xaType.Value != "o") continue; … m_owners.Add(guidObj, guid); }`). OriginalFixer: `if (guidOwner != storedOwner) { if (!storedOwner…Empty && m_guids.Contains(storedOwner)) {…rewrite…} else if (!m_guids.Contains(guidOwner)) { errorLogger(ksRemovingObjectWithBadOwner …); return false; } else { errorLogger(ksRemovingDisownedObject …); return false; } }`. Strings: 'Removing disowned object (invalid ownerguid=…)', 'Removing object with nonexistent owner …'.
findings.implication: Answer to the cleanup question: CustomPropertyFixer + OriginalFixer delete the whole owned StText tree over successive passes; nothing is orphaned. This is inferred from the pass structure (fixer order OriginalFixer→CustomPropertyFixer within a pass means the deletion happens on pass 2/3), not from a dedicated test.

findings.claim: LCM's own deletion path for a custom field (FieldDescription.UpdateCustomField with delete) explicitly deletes the owned object of an OwningAtomic custom field before removing the definition, and DeleteCustomField documents that all data must be removed first.
findings.evidence: `// delete all owned objects for this custom field if it is being deleted if (m_doDelete) { switch (m_type) { case CellarPropertyType.OwningAtomic: { int hvo = sda.get_ObjectProp(obj.Hvo, m_id); if (hvo > 0) sda.DeleteObjOwner(obj.Hvo, hvo, m_id, 0); } break; …` then `if (m_doDelete) mdc.DeleteCustomField(m_id);`; `/// All of the data for this field should be removed before calling this method!` on DeleteCustomField.
findings.implication: If FDAT ever offers 'remove FDAT data from this project', it must delete each Text's owned StText (DeleteObjOwner / delete the StText) inside a UOW before calling IFwMetaDataCacheManaged.DeleteCustomField, mirroring FieldDescription.

findings.claim: FLEx's Custom Fields dialog never lists class Text as a location (only LexEntry/LexSense/LexExampleSentence/MoForm, Segment, RnGenericRec), and it offers 'Multiparagraph text' (= OwningAtomic with DstCls StText) only outside the Interlinear area. So a custom OA StText field on Text cannot be created, seen or deleted through FLEx's dialog; it must be created via LCM (AddCustomField with fieldType OwningAtomic, destinationClass StText).
findings.evidence: `case LocationType.Interlinear: m_locationComboBox.Items.Add(new IdAndString<int>(SegmentTags.kClassId, "Segment")); break; case LocationType.Notebook: … RnGenericRecTags.kClassId …`; `// Additional custom field types are valid if we are not in the text and words area if (locationType != LocationType.Interlinear) { m_typeComboBox.Items.Add(… CustomFieldType.MultiparagraphText …)`; `case CustomFieldType.MultiparagraphText: fd.Type = CellarPropertyType.OwningAtomic; fd.DstCls = StTextTags.kClassId;`; LCM: `AddCustomField(string className, string fieldName, CellarPropertyType fieldType, int destinationClass)` with only `CheckClid(className)` (chart-anchors 3.1).
findings.implication: PLAN §5's 'Verify … that the installed FieldWorks version offers custom fields on Text' will fail at the UI level but succeed at the LCM level; users cannot remove the field from FLEx, so FDAT should own its lifecycle.

findings.claim: The Text 'FullInformation' detail layout (the interlinear Info tab) contains no `customFields` marker, and DataTree only generates custom-field slices where a part carries a `customFields` attribute (present only in LexEntry, LexSense, Morphology and Notebook layouts). Therefore a custom field on Text is not displayed in the Info tab at all — it is invisible in FLEx, not 'an opaque JSON block'.
findings.evidence: `<layout class="Text" type="detail" name="FullInformation"> <part ref="TitleAllWs"/> … <part ref="NotebookSection" …>` (no customFields attribute; grep count 0). DataTree: `// This code looks for the a special part definition with an attribute called "customFields" … If this attribute is found, the custom fields will not be generated. if (XmlUtils.GetOptionalAttributeValue(partRef, "customFields", null) != null) { if(!isTestOnly) EnsureCustomFields(obj, template, partRef); …}`; files containing the marker: LexSense.fwlayout, LexEntry.fwlayout, Morphology.fwlayout, Notebook.fwlayout only.
findings.implication: Contradicts PLAN §5 item 1 ('The field shows up in the text's Info tab as an opaque JSON block (name it clearly and put it last)'); the ordering/naming advice is moot, and users get no in-FLEx visibility or accidental-edit risk. Inferred from the shipped layout; a user-customised layout could differ.

findings.claim: The built-in model analog is identical in shape: Text.Contents is `<owning … id="Contents" card="atomic" sig="StText"/>`, StText.Paragraphs is an owning sequence of StPara, and StTxtPara.Contents is a `String` (TsString) — the same classes the custom field would own, so every merge/fix rule above is exercised daily by ordinary texts.
findings.evidence: MasterLCModel: `<class num="54" id="Text" abstract="false" … base="CmMajorObject">`, `<owning num="8" id="Contents" card="atomic" sig="StText"/>`; `<owning num="1" id="Paragraphs" card="seq" sig="StPara"/>`; `<basic num="2" id="Contents" sig="String">`; `<owning num="6" id="Segments" sig="Segment" card="seq"/>`.
findings.implication: Storing JSON in StTxtPara.Contents stays entirely within FLEx's own data model; nothing new is introduced for FLExBridge, FixFwData or data migrations.

findings.claim: The CustomProperties definition file validator requires only name/class/type(+key) and accepts destclass as an optional attribute, so an OwningAtomic definition with destclass=StText's class id validates.
findings.evidence: `var requiredAttrs = new HashSet<string> { "name", "class", "type", Key }; var optionalAttrs = new HashSet<string> { "destclass", "wsSelector", "helpString", "listRoot", "label" };`
findings.implication: No validation obstacle for the definition itself.

Custom field names containing spaces (the plan's "FDAT data") are accepted by LcmMetaDataCache.AddCustomField (only uniqueness is checked) and used verbatim as merge keys; confirm FLEx tolerates such a name on Text since the dialog never sees it.

result.summary: LCM's back-reference machinery does NOT clear custom ReferenceAtomic properties when the target object is deleted (only built-in atomic refs, via generated per-class RemoveAReferenceCore; LexEntry is the one hand-written exception, and even it only catches values set in the current session because disk-loaded custom atomic values are never registered as incoming refs). Custom ReferenceCollection/ReferenceSequence properties ARE cleared generically, because the vector object itself is the IReferenceSource and registers/deregisters on fluff-up. A dangling custom atomic ref is therefore persisted as <Custom name=...><objsur t="r"/></Custom>, reloads as a bare CmObjectId, and the next read through DomainDataByFlid/flexlibs throws KeyNotFoundException (in-session it returns hvo -2). FLExBridge's CmObjectValidator only checks that the objsur guid parses and t=="r" (no existence check), so a dangling objsur is accepted on send and receive; the only cleanup is FixFwData's OriginalFixer (strips any objsur whose guid is absent, including inside <Custom>), which FLExBridge runs only after an actual 3-way merge (PrepareForPostMergeCommit), not on a pull-only SimpleUpdate. Design consequence for FDAT: granular typed custom fields are safe if they are ReferenceCollection (even for single-valued links) or value types; avoid ReferenceAtomic custom fields on ConstChartRow/DsConstChart/Text, or read them defensively (TryGetObject on the guid) and reconcile on load.

findings.claim: When an object is deleted, LCM clears references to it by calling RemoveAReference on each registered incoming referrer, which dispatches to a virtual RemoveAReferenceCore that is GENERATED per class only over the model's atomic reference properties; custom atomic reference properties are never inspected.
findings.evidence: CmObject.ClearIncomingReferences: 'foreach (var referrer in m_incomingRefs.ToArray()) referrer.RemoveAReference(this);' -> IReferenceSource.RemoveAReference -> RemoveAReferenceCore (base is empty; comment: 'Generated code contains a suitable override of this method for each class that has reference atomic properties'). Template: '#foreach( $prop in $class.AtomicRefProperties) if (m_$prop.NiuginianPropName == target) { $prop.NiuginianPropName = null; return; } #end base.RemoveAReferenceCore(target);'
findings.implication: A ConstChartRow -> salience-possibility (or Text -> FDAT item) custom ReferenceAtomic field is NOT nulled when the possibility is deleted; the dangling reference persists in the row's custom-property value.

findings.claim: LexEntry is the only class with a hand-written RemoveAReferenceCore override that also clears custom atomic properties; no such override exists for ConstChartRow, DsConstChart, Text, StText or any discourse class.
findings.evidence: LexEntry override: 'var flid = this.Cache.CustomProperties.Where(x => x.Value == target && x.Key.Item1 == this).Select(y => y.Key.Item2).FirstOrDefault(); if (flid > 0) SetNonModelPropertyForSDA(flid, null, true); base.RemoveAReferenceCore(target);'. Repo-wide grep for RemoveAReferenceCore finds only CmObject.cs, the template, and this LexEntry override (class header at line 769).
findings.implication: FLEx's own custom list-reference fields on lexical entries get special cleanup; discourse/text classes do not. FDAT cannot rely on LCM to keep custom atomic refs on chart objects consistent.

findings.claim: Even where the override exists, it only works for values set in the current session: custom atomic values loaded from the fwdata are stored as CmObjectId surrogates and reading them converts to an hvo WITHOUT registering an incoming reference or replacing the id, whereas generated getters for built-in atomic refs call ConvertIdToAtomicRef which does AddIncomingRef.
findings.evidence: Load: 'case ReferenceAtomic: myElement = customPropertyElement.Element("objsur"); if (myElement != null) data = surrRepos.GetId(myElement);'. Read: 'case ReferenceAtomic: retval = ((ICmObjectOrId)retval).GetObject(Services.ObjectRepository).Hvo;' (no AddIncomingRef, dictionary keeps the id). Set path registers refs only when useAccessor: 'if (dataType == ReferenceAtomic) { ... obj.AddIncomingRef(this); }'. Generated getter: 'm_$prop = ConvertIdToAtomicRef(...)' and ConvertIdToAtomicRef: 'var result = ...GetObject(id); ((ICmObjectInternal)result).AddIncomingRef(this);'. EnsureCompleteIncomingRefsFrom for ReferenceAtomic merely calls 'obj.GetObjectProperty(flid); // forces it to be fluffed up'.
findings.implication: After a project is reopened, the deleted possibility's m_incomingRefs never contains the chart row's custom atomic reference, so ClearIncomingReferences cannot even reach it (inferred from the code paths; no test exercises this). FLEx's delete-warning counts based on ReferringObjects would also miss such referrers (inferred).

findings.claim: The metadata cache DOES register custom fields as incoming fields of their destination class, so the gap is not in field discovery but in the per-object clearing/registration code.
findings.evidence: AddCustomField ends with 'm_customFields.Add(mfr); ConnectMetaFieldRec(mfr);' and ConnectMetaFieldRec -> SetDestClass: 'mfr.m_dstClsid = clid; if (!mfr.Virtual) m_metaClassRecords[clid].m_incomingFields.Add(mfr);'. GetIncomingFields walks m_incomingFields up the base-class chain. EnsureCompleteIncomingRefs iterates GetIncomingFields(ClassID, AllReference) and tolerates deleted custom flids ('This could happen if the (custom) flid was deleted during this session').
findings.implication: Custom reference COLLECTIONS benefit from this registration (see next finding); atomic ones do not because the per-object fluff path skips AddIncomingRef.

findings.claim: Custom ReferenceCollection and ReferenceSequence properties ARE cleared generically when their target is deleted: the LcmReferenceCollection/LcmReferenceSequence object itself implements IReferenceSource, registers an incoming ref on every fluff-up and Add, and its RemoveAReference removes the target and registers the change with the unit of work.
findings.evidence: 'internal class LcmReferenceCollection<T> : LcmSet<T>, ILcmReferenceCollection<T>, IReferenceSource, IVector'; 'void IReferenceSource.RemoveAReference(ICmObject target) { Remove((T)target); }'; 'FluffUpSideEffects(...) { ((ICmObjectInternal)thingJustFluffed).AddIncomingRef(this); }'; AddObject: 'AddIncomingRef(this)'. LcmSet.Remove: 'm_uowService.RegisterObjectAsModified(MainObject, m_flid, originalValue, newValue); RemoveRefsTo(...)'. EnsureCompleteIncomingRefsFrom for collections/sequences: 'obj.GetVectorProperty(flid).LastOrDefault();' which enumerates via FluffUpObjectIfNeeded. Same pattern for LcmReferenceSequence (lines 1653, 1708-1725, 1836-1842).
findings.implication: For row -> band and column-value -> list-item links, a ReferenceCollection custom field (used single-valued) is kept consistent by LCM exactly like built-in refs; this is the safe typed-field choice. Removing an item from a custom collection on ConstChartRow does not trigger the row's auto-delete because RemoveObjectSideEffectsInternal checks 'e.Flid == ConstChartRowTags.kflidCells' (OverridesLing_Disc.cs:31-39).

findings.claim: A dangling custom atomic reference is written to the fwdata as a normal objsur inside the <Custom> element, and LCM performs no existence check when loading it back.
findings.evidence: Write: 'case OwningAtomic: case ReferenceAtomic: var id = (ICmObjectOrId)data; id.Id.ToXMLString(dataType == OwningAtomic, writer);' and ToXMLString emits '<objsur guid="..." t="r"/>'. Load creates an id via surrRepos.GetId(objsurElement) with no lookup. Grep for 'dangling' in SIL.LCModel finds hits only in UnitOfWork.cs and data migrations, none in the XML load path.
findings.implication: The dangling objsur survives save/reload and travels through Send/Receive inside Linguistics/Discourse/Charting.discourse (or wherever the referrer lives).

findings.claim: Reading a dangling custom atomic reference throws KeyNotFoundException after reload; in the same session in which the target was deleted, get_ObjectProp returns the special hvo -2 (kHvoObjectDeleted). flexlibs' GetCustomFieldValue would raise in both cases.
findings.evidence: GetCustomPropertyForSDA calls CmObjectId.GetObject(repo) -> BackendProvider.GetObject -> CmObjectIdentityMap.GetObjectOrSurrogate: 'var result = m_IdentityMap[guid]; if (result is CmObjectId) throw new KeyNotFoundException("Key " + guid.Guid + " not found in identity map (actually just an ID is present)");'. If the stored value is the deleted CmObject itself, 'ICmObject ICmObjectOrId.GetObject(ICmObjectRepository repo) { return this; }' and DeleteObject sets 'm_hvo = (int)SpecialHVOValues.kHvoObjectDeleted' (= -2). flexlibs: 'item = self.project.DomainDataByFlid.get_ObjectProp(hvo, fieldID) ... poss = self.ObjectRepository(ICmPossibilityRepository).GetObject(item)'.
findings.implication: FDAT must never read a custom atomic ref via get_ObjectProp naively; a colleague deleting one salience possibility would crash FDAT's chart load unless FDAT wraps reads (e.g. read the guid and TryGetObject) and reconciles.

findings.claim: FixFwData's OriginalFixer removes any objsur (including those nested in <Custom> elements) whose guid is not present in the file, and removes the parent property element if it becomes empty.
findings.evidence: 'foreach (var objsur in rt.Descendants("objsur")) { ... if (!m_guids.Contains(guidObj)) { ... errorLogger(String.Format(Strings.ksRemovingLinkToNonexistingObject, ...)); m_danglingLinks.Add(objsur); continue; } ... }' then 'objsur.Remove(); if (!parent.Elements().Any()) { // LT-14189: don't keep empty atomic ref property elements ... parent.Remove(); }'. m_guids is filled from every rt guid (lines 358-365). Descendants() is not restricted to model property names, so <Custom> children are covered.
findings.implication: Whenever FixFwData actually runs, the dangling custom ref is silently stripped (logged as 'Removing link to nonexisting object'), i.e. the row loses its band value rather than the project being corrupted.

findings.claim: FLExBridge runs FixFwData only after a real 3-way merge (PrepareForPostMergeCommit); a pull-only update or rollback (SimpleUpdate) just restores the project file without fixing.
findings.evidence: 'public void SimpleUpdate(IProgress progress, bool isRollback) { RestoreProjectFile(progress); }' vs 'public void PrepareForPostMergeCommit(IProgress progress) { RestoreProjectFile(progress); progress.WriteMessage("Checking project for merge problems"); if (RunFixFwData(progress)) { ... PushHumptyOffTheWall(...); } }' with the remark 'This method is not be called at all, if there was no merging.' FLEx only enables S/R if the fix-it app exists: 'display.Enabled = ... FLExBridgeHelper.FixItAppExists' (comment: 'FB needs to call it, after a merge').
findings.implication: Scenario: user A deletes a possibility referenced by a custom atomic field on a chart row; A's LCM leaves the objsur; A sends; colleague B with no local changes pulls (SimpleUpdate) -> B's fwdata now carries the dangling objsur and nothing strips it until some later merge or a manual 'Find and fix errors'. Only when both sides changed (real merge) does FixFwData clean it. Chart-anchors 3.10's 'FixFwData runs before Send/Receive' should be read as 'after a merge, before commit' (the cited lines 89-100 are PrepareForPostMergeCommit).

findings.claim: FLExBridge's CmObjectValidator does not check that an objsur target exists; for reference properties (custom or built-in) it only verifies the guid attribute parses and t=="r". The nesting service drops dangling OWNING objsurs only.
findings.evidence: 'private static bool ReferencePropertyIsInvalid(List<XAttribute> objsurAttrs, out string result) { new Guid(objsurAttrs.Single(attr => attr.Name.LocalName == FlexBridgeConstants.GuidStr).Value); var typeAttrValue = objsurAttrs.Single(attr => attr.Name.LocalName == "t").Value; if (typeAttrValue != "r") { result = "Has incorrect attribute value for reference property"; return true; } result = null; return false; }'. Custom properties are routed through the same validators with isCustomProperty only relaxing the 'unrecognized attribute' check (lines 89-93, 128-130). CmObjectNestingService: 'if (!guidToClassMapping.TryGetValue(guid, out classOfOwnedObject)) { // Dangling owning ref to non-existant object. objsurElement.Remove(); continue; }' applied only to objsur with t=="o".
findings.implication: A dangling custom reference objsur is accepted by FLExBridge on both send (split/validate) and receive; it is neither rejected nor repaired by the bridge itself, so the file set can legitimately contain it after sync.

findings.claim: Deleting the REFERRER (e.g. the row) is handled correctly for custom fields: DeleteObjectBasics clears the deleted object's own custom owning and reference-vector properties and removes its CustomProperties entries; only the reverse direction (target deleted, referrer survives) is unhandled for atomic refs. Note DeleteObjectBasics explicitly skips ReferenceAtomic ('//case CellarPropertyType.ReferenceAtomic: // Skip it.'), so the deleted referrer's entry may linger in the target's in-memory m_incomingRefs (inferred, in-session only).
findings.evidence: '// Clean up optional custom properties, especially owning & ref props. ... foreach (var flid in mdc.GetFields(ClassID, true, AllOwning | AllReference)) { if (!mdc.IsCustom(flid)) continue; ... case OwningAtomic: DeleteObject(); ... case ReferenceCollection: Clear(); case ReferenceSequence: Clear(); } m_cache.CustomProperties.Remove(key);'
findings.implication: FLEx auto-deleting an emptied ConstChartRow does not leave FDAT garbage behind in the file; the FDAT values simply vanish with the row's <rt>.

findings.claim: In-session sets of a custom atomic ref do register an incoming ref (test evidence), but there is no LCM test covering deletion of the target of a custom reference field.
findings.evidence: IDomainDataByFlidTests: 'var crefs = person.ReferringObjects.Count; m_sda.SetObjProp(wf.Hvo, m_customAtomicReferenceFlid, person.Hvo); ... Assert.AreEqual(crefs + 1, person.ReferringObjects.Count, "Wrong number of incoming references.");'. Grep of the test tree for AddCustomField shows only value/undo/redo tests (IDomainDataByFlidTests, IActionHandlerTests, PropChangedTests, IFwMetaDataCacheTests); none deletes the referenced person/possibility. DomainDataByFlid.SetObjProp -> 'GetInternalInterfaceForObject(hvo).SetProperty(tag, newValue, true)' -> SetCustomPropertyForSDA.
findings.implication: The behaviour described above is derived from code reading, not from an executed test; a quick flexlibs/LCM experiment (create custom atomic ref on ConstChartRow, delete the possibility, save, reload, read) would confirm it before committing to a schema.

Only the manual Tools > Utilities 'Find and fix errors' (Src/Utilities/FixFwDataDll/ErrorFixer.cs:132) and the post-merge run were found.
