Empirical confirmation: create a ReferenceAtomic custom field on ConstChartRow via flexlibs, set it, delete the target possibility with LCM in the same session and in a fresh session, save, reload, and read the value (expect hvo -2 in-session, KeyNotFoundException after reload).

Why the LexEntry-only override exists (bug id / history) - the shallow clone's git log did not reveal the originating commit; there may be an LT- issue describing the same dangling-custom-ref problem for other classes.

Chorus 3-way merge behaviour when one branch deletes a possibility and the other adds a custom reference to it: the merged result is repaired by post-merge FixFwData, but whether a conflict report is generated was not examined (chorus repo not cloned).
Whether LcmCache.CustomProperties (the raw dictionary) is accessible from flexlibs/pythonnet so FDAT could read the stored CmObjectId/guid directly and call TryGetObject instead of get_ObjectProp.

result.summary: Successful-reconcile path from the FLEx user's side: FLEx only notices FDAT's commits inside its own Save/Commit, which the LCM save timer runs unconditionally about every 10 s of user idleness (no unsaved changes needed), so FDAT writes surface within ~10-12 s. SharedXMLBackendProvider.Commit reads the unseen commit-log records, and if ChangeReconciler.OkToReconcileChanges passes, ReconcileForeignChanges builds a non-undoable UOW of create/property-change/delete actions and SimulateRedo()s it: data is patched in place and ordinary PropChanged notifications are broadcast on the UI thread. No MasterRefresh is forced and F5 does not poll the commit log. The Text Chart tab is a RootSite whose native VwRootBox is registered as a PropChanged listener; the chart draws rows via AddLazyVecItems(DsConstChart.Rows) and Notes/Label via AddStringProp, so foreign row add/remove/reorder and Notes/Label edits redraw in place (a deleted row is unregistered before the owner's Rows PropChanged fires, and the rootbox falls back to Reconstruct if the index vanished), while the custom-field-only case DOES produce a PropChanged (the reconciler diffs <Custom> elements too, applies them through the custom-field setters, and emits PropChanged for the custom flid) but the notifier finds no displayed occurrence and does nothing: no redraw, no crash, no visible effect. The Lists editor reloads/updates names on Possibilities/Name/Abbreviation PropChanged, and marker abbreviations in the chart regenerate. The Tagging tab, by contrast, draws from a private tag-string cache filled only at segment load and by its own edits, so foreign TextTag changes are likely stale until Refresh (inferred). The critical design constraint is the conflict rule: a foreign change to ANY object the FLEx user has unsaved edits on (even a different field, e.g. an FDAT custom field on a ConstChartRow the user is annotating, or on DsConstChart while the user is adding rows, since Rows is an OwningSequence) is irreconcilable and pops the modal "FieldWorks cannot save your changes" dialog, halting auto-save until the user Refreshes (reverting their unsaved work). Only DateModified and OwningCollection differences are auto-merged on a shared object. Precondition: FDAT becomes a peer only if the project's ProjectSharing setting is on (flexlibs requests kXML, LcmCache upgrades to kSharedXML only then), otherwise open fails with a lock error.

findings.claim: On a successful reconcile FLEx does not force a MasterRefresh: the backend builds a non-undoable UnitOfWork of the foreign creations/property-changes/deletions and 'redoes' it, and the ordinary Redo pass fires PropChanged for every applied property change.
findings.evidence: SharedXMLBackendProvider.Commit: `if (GetUnseenForeignChanges(...)) { ... IReconcileChanges reconciler = uowService.CreateReconciler(foreignNewbies, foreignDirtballs, foreignGoners); if (reconciler.OkToReconcileChanges()) { reconciler.ReconcileForeignChanges(); ...` ; ChangeReconciler.ReconcileForeignChanges: `var uow = new NonUndoableUnitOfWork(UowService); ... uow.AddAction(objectCreation) ... MakeChangeInfoFor(dirtball, action => { ... uow.AddAction(action); ...}) ... uow.AddAction(new LcmStateChangeObjectDeletion(existingObj, ...)); ... uow.SimulateRedo();` ; SimulateRedo is `base.Redo()`, whose third pass is `m_uowService.SendPropChangedNotifications(GetPropChangeInformation(false));`
findings.implication: FDAT writes reach an open FLEx window as in-place data patches plus PropChanged notifications, exactly like an Undo/Redo; whatever FLEx views bind to the changed properties redraw, everything else stays as is.

findings.claim: FLEx only sees foreign changes when it calls Commit (from UnitOfWorkService.Save); but the LCM save timer fires every second and calls SaveInternal unconditionally (there is no HasUnsavedChanges check), throttled to >=10 s since the last save and >=2 s since the last user activity (or 5 min of continuous activity), and SaveInternal always calls m_dataStorer.Commit even with empty change sets. So an idle FLEx polls the commit log roughly every 10 s.
findings.evidence: `m_saveTimer.Interval = 1000; m_saveTimer.Elapsed += SaveOnIdle;` ; SaveOnIdle: `if (now - m_lastSave < TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10.0)) return; ... if (now - m_ui.LastActivityTime < TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2.0) && now < (m_lastSave + TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5))) return; ... SaveInternal();` ; SaveInternal: `GatherChanges(newbies, dirtballs, goners); ... if (!m_dataStorer.Commit(realNewbies, dirtballs, goners))` (Commit is called regardless of counts); SharedXMLBackendProvider.Commit first runs `GetUnseenForeignChanges(...)` before writing anything.
findings.implication: Latency from an FDAT save to the FLEx chart updating is ~10-12 s while the FLEx user is idle, longer while they are actively typing; FDAT should not expect instant reflection and should itself Save (Commit) promptly after each edit.

findings.claim: A change to a custom-field-only value DOES generate a PropChanged on the FLEx peer: the reconciler diffs every non-virtual field of a foreign dirtball including custom ones (matching <Custom name="..."> elements) and emits typed LcmXxxPropertyChanged actions whose Redo sets the value through the custom-field setters and whose GetChangeInfo yields PropChanged(hvo, customFlid). On the writing side the custom setter registers the object as modified so it is a dirtball in the commit record.
findings.evidence: MakeChangeInfoFor: `foreach (var flid in mdc.GetFields(currentObj.ClassID, true, (int)CellarPropertyTypeFilter.All)) { if (mdc.get_IsVirtual(flid)) continue; ... if (mdc.IsCustom(flid)) { element = (from elt in rtElement.Elements("Custom") where AttrValue(elt, "name") == name select elt).FirstOrDefault(); } ...` then per-type `processChangeRecord(new LcmTsStringPropertyChanged(...))` etc.; Redo of a vector/int/string action: `((ICmObjectInternal)m_changedObject).SetProperty(ModifiedFlid, m_newValue, false)` -> CmObject.SetNonModelPropertyForSDA: `if (...IsCustom(flid)) SetCustomPropertyForSDA(flid, newValue, useAccessor)`; multistring Redo: `GetITsMultiStringProperty(ModifiedFlid)).SetAltQuietly(m_ws, m_newValue)`; writer side SetCustomPropertyForSDA: `m_cache.CustomProperties[key] = newValue; if (useAccessor) { ...UnitOfWorkService.RegisterObjectAsModified(this, flid, oldValue, newValue);`
findings.implication: Custom-field values FDAT writes on DsConstChart/ConstChartRow are applied in FLEx's in-memory objects within the polling window and PropChanged fires for the custom flid; FDAT-in-FLEx consistency is maintained without restarting FLEx.

findings.claim: The Text Chart body is a RootSite whose native VwRootBox registers itself as a PropChanged listener with the main SDA; the rootbox dispatches each PropChanged to the notifiers for that hvo and a notifier regenerates only the displayed occurrences of that property, doing nothing if the property is not displayed. Hence a foreign change to a custom field on a chart row/chart causes no redraw and no error, whereas rows/cells/notes/labels, which the VC displays via AddLazyVecItems(kflidRows), MakeCells and AddStringProp(kflidNotes/kflidLabel), regenerate in place.

Anchoring on FDAT-owned objects (own list items, own objects referencing rows) avoids common dirtballs entirely.

findings.claim: A MasterRefresh (F5) does not poll the commit log; it only reverts when a conflict is already pending, then rebuilds every RootSite via Reconstruct. So a stale view can only be fixed by F5 if the foreign data has already been reconciled by the ~10 s save poll.

result.summary: Answer: FDAT-created TextTags (a "Salience" top-level category with band sub-items in LangProject.TextMarkupTags, applied as TextTag objects in StText.Tags) are NOT invisible metadata. They surface in every FLEx view that consumes TextTags: (1) the Complex Concordance's "Tag" constraint chooser lists the whole TextMarkupTags list, so "Salience" and its bands appear there, and its matcher walks StText.TagsOC and builds a "ttag" annotation for every tag, so FDAT spans are hits (and a bare "any tag" constraint matches them too); (2) the simple Concordance's "Tagging" line uses the same list and searches every TextTag instance by possibility; (3) the Tagging tab shows a "Salience" submenu with the bands in the right-click menu (checkable, so colleagues can apply/remove them by hand) and renders each band as a bracketed abbreviation label on an extra tag row under the words of every tagged text; (4) the Lists area "Text Markup Tags" tool shows the category and bands as editable list items (rename/reorder allowed; deletion of an in-use type/tag is refused with a message naming the text). Where FDAT tags do NOT leak: the Print view (InterlinPrintVc extends InterlinVc whose AddExtraBundleRows hook is empty; only InterlinTaggingVc overrides it) and the interlinear exports (InterlinearExporter has no TextTag code, FlexInterlinear.xsd has no tag element, all Interlinear XSLTs have zero tag references), so .flextext/Word/OO/HTML/XLingPap outputs are unaffected. A whole-sparse-Src sweep finds only five non-test TextTag consumers (the two concordances, the Tagging tab child/VC, and the Lists deletion guard). Sync placement: TextTags travel inside Linguistics/TextCorpus/Text_<guid>.textincorpus (and the TextMarkupTags list as its own file in the same folder), not in Charting.discourse, and they anchor to Segment + analysis index, not to ConstChartRow. Net for the design: a TextTag anchor is user-visible clutter in the concordances, Tagging tab and Lists area (though not in printouts/exports); if used, expect colleagues to see and be able to apply/remove "Salience" bands, and expect the data to live in the text-corpus sync files rather than the chart file.

findings.claim: Across the whole sparse FieldWorks Src checkout, the only non-test consumers of ITextTag/TagsOC are the two concordances, the Tagging tab (child + VC) and the Lists deletion guard in FdoUiCore; no xWorks/Discourse/Avalonia code reads TextTags.

findings.claim: The Lists area exposes the TextMarkupTags list as an editable 'Text Markup Tags' tool, and FLEx refuses to delete a text-markup type or tag possibility that any TextTag references (message names the text), but does not block renaming or reordering.

findings.claim: The model defines TextTag as owned in StText.Tags (collection) with BeginSegment/EndSegment (Segment refs), BeginAnalysisIndex/EndAnalysisIndex (indices into Segment.Analyses) and Tag (CmPossibility ref); LangProject.TextMarkupTags is documented as 'Top eval Possibilities are major tag categories (Syntax, Semantics, RRG, etc.) The actual tags are their SubPossibilities'.
findings.evidence: `<owning num="3" id="Tags" sig="TextTag" card="col"/>` on StText; `<class num="22" id="TextTag" ...><rel num="1" id="BeginSegment" sig="Segment" card="atomic"/><rel num="2" id="EndSegment" .../><basic num="3" id="BeginAnalysisIndex" sig="Integer"> ... <rel num="5" id="Tag" sig="CmPossibility" card="atomic"/>`; `<owning num="55" id="TextMarkupTags" card="atomic" sig="CmPossibilityList"><comment><para>Top eval Possibilities are major tag categories ... The actual tags are their SubPossibilities ...`
findings.implication: TextTags anchor to word spans (segment + analysis index), not to ConstChartRow; a per-row salience band via TextTag would have to be derived from the row's WordGroups' segment ranges, and a two-level category>band list shape is exactly what FLEx expects.

findings.claim: In Send/Receive, TextTags sync inside the per-text file Linguistics/TextCorpus/Text_<guid>.textincorpus (nested with the Text via the generic CmObjectNestingService), and the TextMarkupTags list is written as its own file in the TextCorpus folder — i.e. not in Linguistics/Discourse/Charting.discourse.
findings.evidence: `/// Linguistics\TextCorpus\Text_guid.textincorpus, where 'guid' is the guid of a Text.`; `var rootElement = new XElement("TextInCorpus"); ... CmObjectNestingService.NestObject(false, textElement, classData, guidToClassMapping); FileWriterService.WriteNestedFile(Path.Combine(textCorpusBaseDir, "Text_" + textGuid.ToLowerInvariant() + "." + FlexBridgeConstants.TextInCorpus), rootElement);`; list: `langProjElement, FlexBridgeConstants.TextMarkupTags, Path.Combine(textCorpusBaseDir, FlexBridgeConstants.TextMarkupTagsListFilename)`. NestObject nests all owned objects (`NestOwnedObjects`), which includes StText.Tags.
findings.implication: A TextTag-based anchor would split FDAT data across the text-corpus files (tags) and the discourse file (chart), merged independently; that is workable but means FDAT's per-row data would not ride with the chart object it conceptually belongs to. (The nesting of Tags inside the Text file is inferred from the generic nesting service, not from a Tags-specific line.)

result.summary: Answer: YES, a custom field on Segment does show up as a selectable line in the Text Chart tab's "Configure Interlinear Lines" dialog, but if a user enables it the chart body, the ribbon, chart printing and "Export Text Chart" all SILENTLY DROP it, and the exporter's Debug.Assert is never reached. Mechanism (all stated in code): ConstituentChart.OnConfigureInterlinear opens ConfigureInterlinDialog on a Chart-mode InterlinLineChoices; InterlinLineChoices.LineOptions(Chart) explicitly unions GetCustomLineOptions(), which enumerates every custom field on class Segment with no mode filter, so the field appears as a "segment-container" row in the dialog (no drag handle). When enabled, CreateSpec's default branch builds the spec with WordLevel=false. The chart renders words through ConstChartVc.DisplayWordforms/AddWordBundleInternal -> InterlinVc.DisplayAnalysisAndCloseInnerPile, whose per-line loop does `if (!spec.WordLevel) break;`, so non-word-level (custom Segment) specs are never displayed. The only code path that renders custom Segment lines is InterlinVc.AddFreeformAnnotations (reached via kfragFreeformBundle from the paragraph/segment display), which ConstChartVc and RibbonVc never invoke (they override GetSegmentLevelTags to do nothing and dispatch only chart/row/cell-part fragments). DiscourseExportDialog is handed the same ConstChartVc (m_body.Vc), so the exporter sees exactly what the chart shows; DiscourseExporter.AddStringAltMember's Debug.Assert(false, "Unknown field...") is only hit for multi-string members the VC emits, and no custom flid is emitted. Consequences for FDAT: (1) the Segment custom field is NOT invisible: it is offered to the user in the chart's line-configuration dialog under its field label, and in the Baseline/Gloss/Analyze tabs (and Interlinear print/export) it renders as an editable freeform line labelled with the field label and exports as item type "custom" if the user enables it; enabling is per-user local PropertyTable state, not the default (SetStandardChartState/SetStandardState list fixed flids only). (2) It cannot corrupt or break the chart display or Word/XML chart export. (3) Two caveats: GetCustomLineOptions uses CellarPropertyTypeFilter.All, while FLEx's own Custom Fields dialog restricts Segment fields to SingleLineText (String/MultiUnicode) in the Texts & Words area, so a non-string or fixed-ws Segment field created by FDAT via LCM is outside what the interlinear UI expects (CreateSpec Debug.Fail on ws not kwsAnal/kwsVern; AddCustomFreeFormComment does AddStringProp on the flid). Net: for chart-scoped FDAT data the ConstChartRow custom field (not exposed by any line-choice or custom-field dialog, per chart-anchors-report 3.4) remains the cleaner anchor; a Segment field is safe for the chart but is user-visible/editable in the texts tabs.

findings.claim: The Text Chart tab's Configure Interlinear Lines command opens the generic ConfigureInterlinDialog on a clone of the ribbon's InterlinLineChoices, which was constructed in InterlinMode.Chart.
findings.evidence: OnConfigureInterlinear: `LineChoices = GetLineChoices(); ... using (var dlg = new ConfigureInterlinDialog(m_mediator, PropertyTable, Cache, ..., m_ribbon.Vc.LineChoices.Clone() as InterlinLineChoices))` ... `UpdateForNewLineChoices(dlg.Choices)`. GetLineChoices: `new InterlinLineChoices(Cache.LangProject, Cache.DefaultVernWs, Cache.DefaultAnalWs, InterlinLineChoices.InterlinMode.Chart)` and Restore(..., InterlinLineChoices.InterlinMode.Chart, PropertyTable, ConfigPropName).
findings.implication: The chart tab reuses the same line-choice machinery as the interlinear tabs; whatever LineOptions(Chart) returns is what the chart user can tick.

findings.claim: In Chart mode, InterlinLineChoices.LineOptions explicitly appends every Segment custom field to the six standard chart lines; GetCustomLineOptions enumerates all custom fields on class 'Segment' with CellarPropertyTypeFilter.All and no mode filter.
findings.evidence: `if (mode == InterlinMode.Chart) { return new[] { new LineOption(kflidWord, ...), kflidWordGloss, kflidMorphemes, kflidLexGloss, kflidLexEntries, kflidLexPos }.Union(customLineOptions).ToArray(); }` and GetCustomLineOptions: `var classId = m_cache.MetaDataCacheAccessor.GetClassId("Segment"); ... foreach (int flid in mdc.GetFields(classId, false, (int)CellarPropertyTypeFilter.All)) { if (!mdc.IsCustom(flid)) continue; customLineOptions.Add(new CustomLineOption(flid, mdc.GetFieldLabel(flid), mdc.GetFieldName(flid))); }`
findings.implication: An FDAT custom field on Segment WILL be listed, under its field label, as a tickable line in the Text Chart tab's Configure Interlinear Lines dialog. It is not hidden from chart users.

findings.claim: ConfigurationLineOptions (what the dialog renders) always includes every option from LineOptions(Mode) that is not already in AllLineSpecs, and the dialog builds one row per option, classifying custom (non-word-level) rows as 'segment-container' rows without a drag handle.
findings.evidence: ConfigurationLineOptions: `List<LineOption> requiredOptions = LineOptions(Mode).ToList(); ... // Append any required options that are missing. foreach (LineOption lineOption in requiredOptions) lineOptions.Add(lineOption);`. Dialog InitRowChoices: `var lineOptions = choices.ConfigurationLineOptions; foreach (var lineOption in lineOptions) remainingChoiceRows.Enqueue(...)`. IsSegmentRow: `return !choices.CreateSpec(row.Flid, 0).WordLevel;` GenerateRow: class = IsMorphemeRow ? "morpheme-container" : IsSegmentRow ? "segment-container" : "word-container"; `if (!IsSegmentRow(FirstRow, choices)) { ... "row-handle" ... }`. Chart mode only swaps in scriptForChart.js (checkbox dependencies for Word/WordGloss/Morphemes/LexGloss) and uses plain current vernacular+analysis WS columns; nothing filters segment rows.
findings.implication: Confirms the field is rendered as a real, checkable row in the chart's dialog (as a segment-level row, same as Free Translation would be in the Analyze tab).

findings.claim: A custom Segment field's line spec is created with WordLevel = false (segment/freeform level), and its writing system is forced to the default analysis or vernacular WS; CreateSpec Debug.Fails if the custom field's WS is neither the magic kwsAnal nor kwsVern.
findings.evidence: CreateSpec default branch: `fWordLevel = false; ... if (mdc.FieldExists(flid)) { if (!mdc.IsCustom(flid)) throw new Exception("Adding unknown field to interlinear"); bCustom = true; ws = mdc.GetFieldWs(flid); if ((ws != WritingSystemServices.kwsAnal) && (ws != WritingSystemServices.kwsVern)) { Debug.Fail("The code here is not ready to receive writing systems set on custom segments."); } ...}` then `spec.WritingSystem = (wsRequested == 0 || bCustom) ? ws : wsRequested; spec.WordLevel = fWordLevel;`
findings.implication: WordLevel=false is what keeps the field out of the chart body (next finding). Caveat: if FDAT creates the Segment field with a specific WS handle or a non-string type (GetFieldWs = 0), debug builds of FLEx would Debug.Fail when the user opens the dialog or restores saved choices; release builds skip Debug.Fail (inferred from Conditional("DEBUG") semantics) and fall back to default analysis WS. FDAT should create any Segment field with ws = kwsAnal (or kwsVern) to stay inside the assumption.

findings.claim: The chart body renders words through ConstChartVc.DisplayWordforms/AddWordBundleInternal -> InterlinVc.DisplayAnalysisAndCloseInnerPile, whose per-line loop stops at the first non-word-level spec, so an enabled custom Segment line is never displayed in the chart (nor in its label pile).
findings.evidence: ConstChartVc.DisplayWordforms: `foreach (var point in wordGrp.GetOccurrences()) { SetupAndOpenInnerPile(vwenv); DisplayAnalysisAndCloseInnerPile(vwenv, point, false); }`; AddWordBundleInternal likewise. InterlinVc loop: `for (var i = 0; i < m_choices.EnabledCount; ) { ... var spec = m_choices.EnabledLineSpecs[i]; if (!spec.WordLevel) break; if (spec.MorphemeLevel) { DisplayMorphemes(); ... } else { switch(spec.Flid) { case kflidWord: ... case kflidWordGloss: ... case kflidWordPos: ... } }`. Label pile: `InterlinLineSpec spec = m_lineChoices.EnabledLineSpecs[i]; if (!spec.WordLevel) break;`. Add() ordering guarantees word-level specs never follow freeform ones: `// And word-level annotations can't follow freeform ones. if (spec.WordLevel && !m_allLineSpecs[i].WordLevel) continue;`
findings.implication: Enabling the FDAT Segment field in the chart's dialog has no visible effect in the chart: it is silently dropped, not rendered under each word. Because Add() keeps word-level specs ahead of freeform ones, the `break` cannot hide the Word/Gloss lines.

findings.claim: The only code path that renders custom Segment fields is InterlinVc.AddFreeformAnnotations (default branch -> AddCustomFreeFormComment), reached solely via the kfragFreeformBundle fragment emitted by the paragraph-segment display; ConstChartVc and RibbonVc never emit segment/freeform fragments and override GetSegmentLevelTags to do nothing.
findings.evidence: InterlinVc: `vwenv.AddObjProp(flidSelf, this, kfragFreeformBundle);` ... `case kfragFreeformBundle: AddFreeformAnnotations(vwenv, hvo); break;`. AddFreeformAnnotations: `for (int ispec = m_lineChoices.FirstEnabledFreeformIndex; ...) { switch(flid) { case kflidFreeTrans/kflidLitTrans/kflidNote/kflidMedia ...; default: if (mdc.FieldExists(flid) && mdc.IsCustom(flid)) AddCustomFreeFormComment(vwenv, hvoSeg, ispec); break; // unknown type, ignore it. } }`. Grep of Src/LexText/Discourse/*.cs for kfragSegFf/kfragSegFfChoices/AddFreeformAnnotations/FirstEnabledFreeformIndex returns no hits. ConstChartVc.Display cases: kfragChart/row/cell parts, kfragNotesString (`AddStringProp(ConstChartRowTags.kflidNotes)`), kfragComment (`AddStringProp(ConstChartRowTags.kflidLabel)`), kfragMTMarker, default -> base.Display. `protected override void GetSegmentLevelTags(LcmCache cache) { // do nothing (we don't need tags above bundle level). }` in both ConstChartVc and RibbonVc.
findings.implication: Confirms by construction (stated code plus an inferred absence of any segment fragment in the Discourse VCs) that the chart body, ribbon and chart print never reach the custom-field renderer.

findings.claim: Export Text Chart uses the very same ConstChartVc instance (m_body.Vc) as the chart display, so the exporter only receives what the chart renders; DiscourseExporter.AddStringAltMember asserts on unknown tags but is never called with a custom flid, and DiscourseExporter.AddStringProp silently ignores any tag other than row Notes/Label.
findings.evidence: ConstituentChart: `using (var dlg = new DiscourseExportDialog(m_mediator, PropertyTable, m_chart.Hvo, m_body.Vc, m_logic.WsLineNumber))`; DiscourseExportDialog: `m_vc = vc;` ... `exporter = new DiscourseExporter(m_cache, writer, m_hvoRoot, m_vc, m_wsLineNumber);`. DiscourseExporter.AddStringProp: `switch (tag) { case ConstChartRowTags.kflidNotes: ...; case ConstChartRowTags.kflidLabel: ...; }` (no default). AddStringAltMember: cases WfiWordformTags.kflidForm, WfiGlossTags.kflidForm, ConstChartTagTags.kflidTag, CmPossibilityTags.kflidName/kflidAbbreviation, `default: Debug.Assert(false, "Unknown field in AddStringAltMember!"); break;`. AddCustomFreeFormComment (never reached from the chart) would emit `vwenv.AddStringProp(customCommentFlid, this)`, i.e. the non-asserting overload.
findings.implication: An enabled Segment custom field cannot break the chart's Word/XML export: the exporter never sees it, and even if it did, custom fields go through AddStringProp, which has no assert. The exporter assert noted in discourse-code #9 is not triggered by Segment custom fields.

findings.claim: The chart's line choices (including any enabled custom line) are persisted per user in the local PropertyTable settings, keyed by custom-field Name (not flid), and the default chart line set never includes custom fields.
findings.evidence: PersistAndDisplayChangedLineChoices: `PropertyTable.SetProperty(ConfigPropName, m_ribbon.Vc.LineChoices.Persist(...), PropertyTable.SettingsGroup.LocalSettings, true);`. Persist: `if (custOpt == null) builder.Append($",{lineSpec.Flid}%{wsName}%{lineSpec.Enabled}"); else builder.Append($",{lineSpec.Flid}%{wsName}%{lineSpec.Enabled}%{custOpt.Name}");`. Restore: `// Find the custom option by Name since the flid's can change. var custOpt = customOptions.Find(opt => opt.Name.Equals(flidAndWs[3]));`. SetStandardChartState adds only kflidWord, WordGloss, Morphemes, LexGloss, LexEntries, LexPos. CustomLineOption: `/// The Name does NOT change when a custom field is renamed, the Label does change.`
findings.implication: Nothing about the FDAT field is enabled unless a user ticks it, and that choice is local to the user's machine (not part of the project, not synced by Send/Receive). The field's Label (what the user sees in the dialog) can be chosen by FDAT, e.g. 'FDAT data (do not edit)'.

findings.claim: Outside the chart, an enabled Segment custom field is a fully visible, editable freeform line under each segment in the interlinear (Baseline/Gloss/Analyze) views and is written by the Interlinear exporter as a free annotation of type "custom".
findings.evidence: AddCustomFreeFormComment: `InterlinearExporter exporter = vwenv as InterlinearExporter; if (exporter != null) exporter.FreeAnnotationType = "custom"; ... label = m_cache.MetaDataCacheAccessor.GetFieldLabel(customCommentFlid) + " "; ... vwenv.AddStringProp(customCommentFlid, this);`. InterlinearExporter: `public string FreeAnnotationType { get...; set...; }` and `WriteItem(tag, m_sFreeAnnotationType, ws);`. The Analyze/Gloss defaults (SetStandardState/SetStandardGlossState) do not include custom fields, so this requires the user to enable it in those tabs' own dialogs.
findings.implication: Segment is not an 'invisible' anchor in the way a ConstChartRow custom field is: FDAT machine data (e.g. JSON) stored on Segment can be surfaced and hand-edited by users in the texts tabs and leak into interlinear exports. Inferred: this argues for ConstChartRow (no dialog exposes it; chart-anchors-report 3.4) over Segment for chart-scoped data.

findings.claim: FLEx's own Custom Fields dialog only lets users create SingleLineText (String / MultiUnicode) custom fields on Segment; the interlinear line-choice code enumerates Segment custom fields of ALL property types, so a non-string Segment field created by FDAT through LCM would be listed as a line but is outside what the rendering code was written for.
findings.evidence: AddCustomFieldDlg: `m_typeComboBox.Items.Add(... CustomFieldType.SingleLineText ...); // Additional custom field types are valid if we are not in the text and words area  if (locationType != LocationType.Interlinear) { MultiparagraphText, ListRefCollection, ListRefAtomic, Date, Number }`. SetFieldType SingleLineText -> `CellarPropertyType.String : CellarPropertyType.MultiUnicode`. GetCustomLineOptions uses `(int)CellarPropertyTypeFilter.All`. AddCustomFreeFormComment renders with `vwenv.AddStringProp(customCommentFlid, this)`.
findings.implication: Inferred risk: if FDAT wants a Segment custom field at all, make it String/MultiUnicode with ws kwsAnal so it behaves exactly like a user-created one; an Integer/GenDate/reference field on Segment would appear in the dialogs and could misbehave (AddStringProp on a non-string flid) in the texts tabs, though still not in the chart.

openQuestions: Runtime behaviour of AddStringProp on a non-string custom Segment field (Integer/GenDate/ReferenceAtomic) in the Analyze tab was not executed here; the risk is inferred from the code path, not observed. Only matters if FDAT chooses a non-string type on Segment.

Whether the shipped FLEx installer is a Release build (so Debug.Fail in CreateSpec for a custom Segment field with a non-magic writing system is compiled out) was assumed from standard .NET Conditional("DEBUG") semantics, not verified against FieldWorks build configuration.

ConstChartVc.Display's default branch falls through to InterlinVc.Display; the claim that no segment-level fragment can ever reach it from the chart root is inferred from the fragment cases in ConstChartVc and the absence of segment fragments in the Discourse sources, not from a runtime trace.

result.summary: No. A custom field added programmatically to Text does NOT display in the Text Info tab, and there is no FLEx UI in which a custom field on Text, DsConstChart or ConstChartRow is shown, edited or deleted. The Info tab is a DataTree rooted on the Text object using the Cellar.fwlayout layout Text/FullInformation, which has no customFields placeholder; DataTree (and the newer Avalonia DetailComposer) generate custom-field slices only where a part carries customFields="here"/ref="_CustomFieldPlaceholder", and "Show Hidden Fields" only reveals visibility="never" parts already in the layout. The Custom Fields dialog offers Text-and-Words users only Segment and filters existing custom fields to the classes in its combo, so fields on Text/chart classes are neither listed nor deletable there; the Texts browse view generates custom-field columns only from <generate> nodes, of which the Words configuration has none; interlinear line choices enumerate Segment custom fields only; the chart tab renders fixed fragments (existing report 3.5). PLAN.md line 130's assumptions are therefore wrong on two counts: FLEx does not "offer custom fields on Text" in its dialog (only Segment for the interlinear area), and a programmatic Text field does not "show up in the text's Info tab". Consequences: the field is safe from accidental user edits, but the only removal path is IFwMetaDataCacheManaged.DeleteCustomField (FDAT's own uninstall or a FLExTools/flexlibs script; flexlibs exposes no add/delete helper), and FLEx cannot show the user that FDAT data exists. Inferred, unverified alternative: FLEx loads user layout overrides from <project>/ConfigurationSettings/*.fwlayout and FLExBridge syncs them via CachedSettings/ConfigurationSettings/*.fwlayout, so FDAT could ship an override of Text/FullInformation containing a customFields placeholder to make the field visible (via the class-agnostic CmObject-Detail-Custom part) - but that would also make the JSON user-editable, which is probably undesirable.

findings.claim: The Text Info tab is a DataTree (StTextDataTree) that shows the owning Text object (not the StText) with layout name "FullInformation".
findings.evidence: Words/areaConfiguration.xml guicontrol TextInformationPane: <parameters area="textsWords" clerk="interlinearTexts" ... layout="FullInformation" ...>; InfoPane.cs StTextDataTree.ShowObject: 'if (stText.OwningFlid == TextTags.kflidContents) showObj = stText.Owner; base.ShowObject(showObj, layoutName, layoutChoiceField, showObj, suppressFocusChange);'
findings.implication: The layout that governs what the Info tab shows for a Text is <layout class="Text" type="detail" name="FullInformation"> in Cellar.fwlayout.

findings.claim: The Text/FullInformation layout contains no part with a customFields attribute (nor ref="_CustomFieldPlaceholder"); the only layouts with that hook are LexEntry, LexSense, Morphology (MoForm etc.) and Notebook (RnGenericRec).
findings.evidence: Cellar.fwlayout lines 62-75 list only TitleAllWs, AbbreviationAllWs, SourceAllWs, IsTranslated, Media, Genres, CommentAllWs, DateCreated, DateModified, NotebookSection. grep customFields over Configuration hits only LexSense.fwlayout:43,57; LexEntry.fwlayout:26; Morphology.fwlayout:73,88,101,116,129,142; Notebook.fwlayout:33-407 (12 hits); ViewsLayout.xsd (schema).
findings.implication: A custom field on Text has no insertion point in the Info tab layout; PLAN §5 option 1's statement that it 'shows up in the text's Info tab' is false for stock FLEx.

findings.claim: DataTree generates custom-field slices only when a part in the layout carries a customFields attribute; EnsureCustomFields is called from nowhere else. Without such a part, custom fields of the object's class are never enumerated.
findings.evidence: ApplyLayout: 'This code looks for the a special part definition with an attribute called "customFields" ... If this attribute is found, the custom fields will not be generated [sic - i.e. generated here]. if (XmlUtils.GetOptionalAttributeValue(partRef, "customFields", null) != null) { if(!isTestOnly) EnsureCustomFields(obj, template, partRef); continue; }'. EnsureCustomFields iterates FieldDescription.FieldDescriptors(m_cache) for fields with IsCustomField && class in the object's class chain and inserts <part ref="Custom" param=fieldName/> after the placeholder. grep 'EnsureCustomFields' in Src finds only this call site (other hits are unrelated 'customFields' identifiers in LexImport code).
findings.implication: Stated by code: a programmatically added Text (or DsConstChart/ConstChartRow) custom field is invisible in every DataTree whose layout lacks the placeholder - which is all of them for these classes.

findings.claim: "Show Hidden Fields" does not surface custom fields; it only lifts visibility="never" on parts already present in the layout.
findings.evidence: 'string visibility = "always"; if (!m_fShowAllFields) { visibility = XmlUtils.GetOptionalAttributeValue(partRef, "visibility", "always"); if (visibility == "never") return NodeTestResult.kntrNothing; ...'
findings.implication: There is no user toggle that would reveal an FDAT custom field on Text.

findings.claim: The newer Avalonia detail UI behaves the same: a CustomFieldPlaceholder view node is created only from <part customFields=.../> or ref="_CustomFieldPlaceholder" in the imported layout, and WalkCustomFields expands only that node.
findings.evidence: XmlLayoutImporter: '// Custom-field placeholder: <part customFields="here"/> or ref="_CustomFieldPlaceholder". if (callerEl.Attribute("customFields") != null || refName == "_CustomFieldPlaceholder") { output.Add(MakeLeaf(stableId, ViewNodeKind.CustomFieldPlaceholder, ...'; DetailComposer: 'case ViewNodeKind.CustomFieldPlaceholder: // Runtime expansion of `customFields="here"` from live MDC metadata. WalkCustomFields(node, obj, depth);' and WalkCustomFields enumerates _mdc.GetFieldIds() where IsCustom && class in chain.
findings.implication: The conclusion holds for both the legacy WinForms DataTree and the Avalonia rewrite; the same fwlayout files drive both.

findings.claim: FLEx's Custom Fields dialog never offers Text, DsConstChart or ConstChartRow as a location: the Interlinear (Texts & Words) location offers only Segment; Lexicon offers LexEntry/LexSense/LexExampleSentence/MoForm; Notebook offers RnGenericRec. Existing custom fields on any other class are filtered out of the dialog's list.
findings.evidence: 'case LocationType.Interlinear: m_locationComboBox.Items.Add(new IdAndString<int>(SegmentTags.kClassId, "Segment")); break;' ... 'm_customFields = (from fd in FieldDescription.FieldDescriptors(m_cache) where fd.IsCustomField && GetItem(m_locationComboBox, fd.Class) != null select new FDWrapper(fd, false)).ToList();'
findings.implication: PLAN.md:130's 'Verify ... that the installed FieldWorks version offers custom fields on Text' resolves to NO for the UI; the field can only be created by LCM code (report 3.1). And it can never be seen or deleted in the dialog.

findings.claim: The dialog's Delete path operates only on entries in its filtered m_customFields list (MarkForDeletion -> FieldDescription.UpdateCustomField -> mdc.DeleteCustomField), so a field on an unlisted class cannot be deleted via FLEx UI.
findings.evidence: 'fd.MarkForDeletion = true;' (line 948) on the selected FDWrapper; 'var deletedFieldList = from fdw in m_customFields where fdw.Fd.IsCustomField && fdw.Fd.MarkForDeletion select fdw.Fd;' (515-517); FieldDescription.UpdateCustomField calls 'mdc.DeleteCustomField(m_id)' (FieldDescription.cs:386). grep MarkForDeletion in Src shows only AddCustomFieldDlg and DeleteCustomList (list-deletion cascade, report 3.6).
findings.implication: The only removal path for an FDAT custom field on Text/DsConstChart/ConstChartRow is code calling IFwMetaDataCacheManaged.DeleteCustomField (FDAT uninstall, PLAN rule 5, or a FLExTools script) - or the indirect DeleteCustomList cascade if the field references a custom list that the user deletes.

findings.claim: flexlibs exposes custom-field helpers only for lexicon classes (entry/sense/example/allomorph) and has no AddCustomField/DeleteCustomField wrapper; FDAT must call the LCM IFwMetaDataCacheManaged methods directly through pythonnet.
findings.evidence: FLExProject.py defines GetCustomFieldValue(senseOrEntryOrHvo, ...), __GetCustomFieldsOfType(classID), LexiconGetEntryCustomFields, LexiconGetSenseCustomFields, LexiconGetExampleCustomFields, LexiconGetAllomorphCustomFields, ...CustomFieldNamed; grep for AddCustomField/DeleteCustomField returns nothing.
findings.implication: No third-party UI (FLExTools) removes such fields either; FDAT owns the lifecycle end to end.

findings.claim: Browse (list) views can show custom-field columns only where the column configuration contains <generate> nodes; PossibleColumnSpecs comes from PartGenerator.GetGeneratedChildren, which passes through non-generate children unchanged. The Words area configuration contains no <generate> elements, so the Texts list cannot show a Text custom field column.
findings.evidence: XmlBrowseViewBaseVc: 'return PossibleColumnSpecs = PartGenerator.GetGeneratedChildren(m_xnSpec.SelectSingleNode("columns"), m_xbv.Cache, vc, (int)ListItemsClass);'; PartGenerator: 'if (child.Name != "generate") { result.Add(child); continue; }' then generator.Generate() with restrictions such as "customOnly" -> IsCustom(flid). grep '<generate' under Configuration/Words returns nothing; customOnly generate nodes exist only in Reversal.fwlayout (MoForm) and lexicon/notebook configs.
findings.implication: Neither the Texts list nor Configure Columns will reveal the FDAT field.

findings.claim: Interlinear line configuration enumerates custom fields of Segment only; the interlinear exporter writes custom-field items only for those lines. RecordClerk's custom-field scan is an export-time name check for notebook/lexicon classes.
findings.evidence: InterlinLineChoices.GetCustomLineOptions: 'var classId = m_cache.MetaDataCacheAccessor.GetClassId("Segment"); ... foreach (int flid in mdc.GetFields(classId, false, ...)) { if (!mdc.IsCustom(flid)) continue; customLineOptions.Add(...)'; RecordClerk.AreCustomFieldsAProblem(new int[] { RnGenericRecTags.kClassId }) under areaChoice == "notebook".
findings.implication: Segment custom fields ARE user-visible in FLEx (interlinear lines), unlike Text/chart fields - relevant only if FDAT ever wanted visible per-segment data, which the owner wants to avoid (baseline-tab level).

findings.claim: If a placeholder were present, rendering would work for any class: the generated <part ref="Custom" param=fieldName/> resolves to the class-agnostic part CmObject-Detail-Custom (paramType FieldName, editor autoCustom), and MakeAutoCustomSlice picks a slice by field type (String/MultiUnicode/MultiString, Integer, GenDate, references, owning atomic).
findings.evidence: StandardParts.xml: '<part id="CmObject-Detail-Custom" type="detail" paramType="FieldName"><slice editor="autoCustom" menu="mnuDataTree-Help" helpTopicID="khtpCustomFields"/>'; SliceFactory: 'case "autocustom": slice = MakeAutoCustomSlice(cache, obj, caller, node);' and 'This is invoked when a generated part ref (<part ref="Custom" param="fieldName"/>) invokes the standard slice'. (StandardParts.xml is at DistFiles/Parts/, outside the sparse checkout; read via git grep HEAD.)
findings.implication: Visibility is purely a layout question, not a class restriction.

findings.claim: INFERRED, not verified: FDAT could make the field visible by writing a user override of the Text/FullInformation layout (adding <part ref="_CustomFieldPlaceholder" customFields="here"/>) into <project>/ConfigurationSettings/Text.fwlayout; FLEx loads override files from that folder, and FLExBridge syncs *.fwlayout from CachedSettings/ConfigurationSettings (copied from the project's ConfigurationSettings) to colleagues.
findings.evidence: Inventory.LoadUserOverrides: 'string path = UserOverrideConfigurationSettingsPath; ... AddElementsFromFiles(DirectoryUtils.GetOrderedFiles(path, sPattern), version, true);' with UserOverrideConfigurationSettingsPath => LcmFileHelper.GetConfigSettingsDir(m_projectPath) = <project>/ConfigurationSettings; PersistOverrideElement writes '<key-attr>.fwlayout' there (doc: 'layout class="LexEntry" type="Detail" name="Full" ... we want to make a file LexEntry.fwlayout'). FlexFolderSystem: 'IncludePatterns.Add(Path.Combine("CachedSettings", Path.Combine("ConfigurationSettings", "*.fwlayout")))'; BaseDomainServices copies to 'CachedSettings/ConfigurationSettings' ('Copying dictionary configuration settings.').
findings.implication: A possible (untested) route to give users a visible/deletable handle on FDAT data, at the cost of exposing the JSON to hand edits in the Info tab. The override's version attribute, the 'default$$' vs project-name file pattern, and Avalonia's ViewDefinitionOverrideFileMigrator would all need checking before relying on it.

findings.claim: PLAN §5 option 1 explicitly assumes both UI availability and Info-tab visibility of a Text custom field.

(Note: Segment IS offered by the dialog, per AddCustomFieldDlg.cs:123-125.)

result.summary:
A word token in FLEx has no GUID of its own. Its only identity is the pair (Segment object, index into Segment.Analyses) — AnalysisOccurrence is literally that pair, with equality defined on it. The GUID FLEx puts on `<word>` in its own interlinear export is the IAnalysis (WfiWordform/WfiAnalysis/WfiGloss) GUID, which FLEx's own comment says "may well not be unique in the file", and which is swapped in place whenever the user glosses/approves the word. So PLAN §4's "`<word guid>` per analysis" cannot be a token key.

AnalysisAdjuster does keep (segment, analysis-index) keys valid across baseline edits — shifting indices by the number of analyses removed/added, moving endpoints across segments, snapping to the nearest wordform, or deleting the reference when its text is gone — but ONLY for objects it collects from the model: `para.GetTags()` (TextTag) and `para.GetChartCellRefs()` (ConstChartWordGroup), the two implementers of IAnalysisReference. A (segmentGuid, index) snapshot that FDAT stores in a custom field or JSON is never touched and goes stale. Two further caveats: Make-phrase/Break-phrase and full reparse rewrite Segment.Analyses directly with no reference adjustment at all ("Joining words renumbers the occurrences"), and FLExBridge merges Segment.Analyses atomically while WordGroup/TextTag indices merge per object, so indices can drift after a conflicting Send/Receive.

Design consequence: the sidecar should emit the FLEx occurrence key itself — segment GUID + index (e.g. `data-guid="<segGuid>:<idx>"`) — as a render-time identity, alongside the IAnalysis GUID as descriptive data and the enclosing ConstChartWordGroup GUID. Anything FDAT persists per token should be anchored to a FLEx-maintained IAnalysisReference: the containing WordGroup (GUID + ordinal within the group's GetOccurrences()) or, for a durable per-token GUID, an FDAT-created one-token TextTag in StText.Tags, which the adjuster maintains exactly like WordGroups. The proposed row fallback (chart GUID + first WordGroup's BeginSegment GUID + BeginAnalysisIndex + column GUID) is sound only if those values are read live from the WordGroup at reconciliation time — that is what FLEx maintains — not compared against a stored snapshot; add the first word's baseline text as a tie-breaker (FLEx's own IsAnalogousTo compares column + baseline text). Note also that in the RemoveMissingMarker recreation path the row had no WordGroup at all (only the marker), so that fallback is uncomputable there; only the row index/label carry over.

findings.claim: A word token (analysis occurrence) has no GUID; its identity is the pair (Segment, Index), and equality/hash are defined on exactly those two values.
findings.evidence: `public class AnalysisOccurrence { ... public ISegment Segment { get; private set; } ... public int Index { get; private set; }` and `public bool Equals(AnalysisOccurrence other) { return other.Segment == Segment && other.Index == Index; }` / `GetHashCode() { return Segment.GetHashCode() ^ Index; }`. The class does not derive from CmObject and has no Guid.
findings.implication: FDAT must emit a composite key (segment GUID + index) for a token; no single FLEx GUID names a token.

findings.claim: The GUID FLEx itself writes on `<word>` in the interlinear XML export is the IAnalysis object's GUID (WfiWordform/WfiAnalysis/WfiGloss) and FLEx's own comment states it is not unique in the file.
findings.evidence: `protected override void WriteStartWord(int hvo) { ... // Note that this guid may well not be unique in the file, since it refers to a // WfiWordform, WfiAnalysis, WfiGloss, or PunctuationForm (the last is not output), // any of which may be referred to repeatedly in an analyzed text. ... WriteGuidAttributeForObj(hvo); }`
findings.implication: PLAN §4's `<word guid>` per analysis (PLAN.md:90) and the XSL's `data-guid` pass-through (docs/textchart/textchart-to-html.xsl:507-508) would carry a non-unique key; it can only be descriptive, never the anchor for token-level data.

findings.claim: Segment.Analyses is a reference sequence of IAnalysis, so the same analysis object is legitimately referenced from many positions.
findings.evidence: `<class num="6" id="Segment" ...> <rel num="5" id="Analyses" sig="IAnalysis" card="seq"/>`
findings.implication: Model-level confirmation that analysis GUIDs are shared across occurrences.

findings.claim: The IAnalysis at a token position is replaced in place (same segment, same index) when the user glosses/approves the word, so the analysis GUID at a given token changes over time even without baseline edits.
findings.evidence: `internal void SetAnalysis(int iSegment, int iAnalysis, IAnalysis analysis) { var seg = SegmentsOS[iSegment]; ... seg.AnalysesRS.Replace(iAnalysis, 1, new ICmObject[] {analysis}); }` and the AnalysisOccurrence.Analysis setter: `Segment.AnalysesRS.Replace(Index, 1, new ICmObject[] {value});` ("Setter modifies the segment").
findings.implication: Even ignoring duplicates, keying token data by analysis GUID would lose the link the moment a colleague glosses the word. The (segment, index) position is what stays put.

findings.claim: AnalysisAdjuster adjusts only IAnalysisReference objects it collects from the model — the paragraph's TextTags and ConstChartWordGroups — and nothing else.
findings.evidence: `m_oldParaRefs = new HashSet<IAnalysisReference>(); // This adds TextTags that only reference this paragraph m_oldParaRefs.UnionWith(m_para.GetTags()); // This adds ConstChartWordGroups that only reference this paragraph m_oldParaRefs.UnionWith(m_para.GetChartCellRefs());` and the interface doc: "Interface that multiple diverse classes with similar functions implement ... For now: TextTag and ConstChartWordGroup".
findings.implication: A (segmentGuid, index) pair that FDAT stores in a custom field or JSON is a snapshot FLEx never maintains. Only keys held as fields of a TextTag or ConstChartWordGroup are kept valid. Token-level data must therefore be anchored to one of those objects (or recomputed from them at read time).

findings.claim: The adjuster keeps (segment, index) references valid under baseline edits: it shifts Begin/End indices by the counts of removed/added analyses, moves an endpoint to a following segment when the index overflows, snaps inexact endpoints to the nearest wordform, and deletes references whose text was entirely deleted.
findings.evidence: UpdateAffectedReferences: `if (ibeg >= ifirstAnalysisInSegToFix + m_cRemovedAnalyses) { ibeg -= m_cRemovedAnalyses; iar.ChangeToDifferentIndex(ibeg, true, false); ...}` / `ibeg += m_cAddedAnalyses; AdjustReferenceEndPoint(endSeg, iar, ibeg, true);` / `var actualPoint = new AnalysisOccurrence(begSeg, ibeg - 1).NextWordform(); if (actualPoint == null) { refsToDelete.Add(iar); ...}`; AdjustReferenceEndPoint: `if (newIndex >= seg.AnalysesRS.Count && newSeg != null) { iar.ChangeToDifferentSegment(newSeg, fbeg, !fbeg); newIndex -= seg.AnalysesRS.Count; ...}`; CheckForDeleteableIAR doc: "Delete any IAnalysisReference objects whose begin and end references fall within the range of indices removed and not added back in"; DeleteReferences removes TextTags from `owner.TagsOC` and cell parts from `owner.CellsOS`.
findings.implication: Yes — FLEx maintains (BeginSegment GUID, BeginAnalysisIndex) on ConstChartWordGroup and TextTag across baseline edits, so a row-reanchoring fallback that reads those values LIVE from the row's first WordGroup is built on keys FLEx itself keeps current.

findings.claim: When segments are deleted or merged, the adjuster re-homes hanging references onto the surviving segment and re-computes their indices (FixHangingReferences); it can also give up and delete a reference it cannot repair.
findings.evidence: `if (!iar.BegRef().IsValid) { if (cOldAnalyses > 0 && iFirstSegmentSurviving > 0) { // segment break deleted, try to preserve position in previous segment newSeg = m_para.SegmentsOS[iFirstSegmentSurviving - 1]; iar.ChangeToDifferentSegment(newSeg, true, false); iar.ChangeToDifferentIndex(iar.BegRef().Index + cOldAnalyses, true, false); }` ... `DiscardDeletedRefs(newSeg); //It should be gone, we can't fix it, get rid of it.`
findings.implication: The Segment GUID part of a stored key is not stable either: after a sentence merge, WordGroups that pointed at the second segment now point at the first. Reconciliation must compare against live WordGroup values, not a stored segment GUID.

findings.claim: ChangeToDifferentIndex clamps the new index into [0, AnalysesRS.Count-1] rather than invalidating the reference, so a WordGroup/TextTag may silently end up on a different word instead of being deleted.
findings.evidence: `BeginAnalysisIndex = newIndex; var max = BeginSegmentRA.AnalysesRS.Count - 1; BeginAnalysisIndex = Math.Min(BeginAnalysisIndex, max); BeginAnalysisIndex = Math.Max(BeginAnalysisIndex, 0);` (identical code in TextTag).
findings.implication: FLEx's key maintenance is best-effort. FDAT should treat WordGroup/TextTag anchors as authoritative but tolerate them drifting; a baseline-text tie-breaker (as FLEx's IsAnalogousTo does) catches gross drift.

findings.claim: Existing Segment objects (and thus their GUIDs) are preserved by the adjuster for unaffected sentences: new Segment objects are inserted only for net-new sentences, and merges delete only the second of two partly surviving segments; ParagraphParser likewise reuses pre-existing Segment objects in order on reparse.
findings.evidence: AdjustSegments: "Since segments after the old last-modified variables must not change ... `m_para.SegmentsOS.Insert(i, m_para.Services.GetInstance<ISegmentFactory>().Create());` ... `var segToDelete = m_para.SegmentsOS[m_iSegFirstModified + 1]; ConcatenateTranslationsAndNotes(...); m_para.SegmentsOS.Replace(m_iSegFirstModified + 1, 1, new ISegment[0]);`"; header rule 1: "Any segment whose text is unaffected by edits should be unmodified in every other way". ParagraphParser.CreateSegment: `Segment unusedSeg = (Segment)m_preExistingSegs.FirstOrDefault(); if (unusedSeg != null) { // Reuse it. ... unusedSeg.BeginOffset = ichMin; return unusedSeg; }`
findings.implication: Segment GUID is a reasonable component of a token key for sentences the user has not edited; it is the index part that moves within an edited sentence.

findings.claim: Make-phrase, Break-phrase and full reparse rewrite Segment.Analyses directly and do NOT invoke AnalysisAdjuster, so ConstChartWordGroup/TextTag indices after the changed word are not adjusted on those paths.
findings.evidence: MakePhraseWithNextWord: `Segment.AnalysesRS.Replace(Index, 1 + next.Index - Index, new ICmObject[] {wordform}); ... Paragraph.ParseIsCurrent = false;` BreakPhrase: `Segment.AnalysesRS.Replace(Index, 1, wordforms.Cast<ICmObject>());` — no IAnalysisReference handling in either. FocusBoxController: "// Joining words renumbers the occurrences. // We need to clear the analysis cache" / "// Breaking phrases renumbers the occurrences." ParagraphParser.Parse: `if (AnalysesChanged(seg, newAnalyses)) seg.AnalysesRS.Replace(0, seg.AnalysesRS.Count, newAnalyses);`. The adjuster's own comment: "the reparse might indeed create a phrase, changing the index of later wordforms with unpredictable effects."
findings.implication: Even FLEx-owned keys can go wrong (point at the neighbouring word) after a phrase join/break in the interlinear tab; the chart then depends on CleanupInvalidChartCells (chart-anchors report 2.13) or the user noticing. FDAT's reconciliation should not assume WordGroup indices are always semantically right — keep the baseline-text tie-breaker and log/flag mismatches rather than silently re-binding.

findings.claim: FLExBridge merges Segment.Analyses as one atomic unit (one side wins wholesale), while ConstChartWordGroup/TextTag index fields merge per object, so after a conflicting Send/Receive a WordGroup's indices can point into the other user's analyses list.
findings.evidence: `case DataType.ReferenceSequence: // Trying to merge the Analyses of a segment is problematic. Best to go all-or-nothing, and ensure // we get a conflict report if it fails. if (classInfo.ClassName == "Segment" && propertyInfo.PropertyName == "Analyses") propStrategy.IsAtomic = true;` (per-object, non-atomic merge of concrete classes is claim 5.4 of the chart-anchors report).
findings.implication: Inferred: index drift is possible across Send/Receive without any local edit. Another reason FDAT should verify a token anchor against baseline text when reconciling after a sync.

findings.claim: FLEx's own chart logic identifies charted tokens by (segment, index) — a HashSet<AnalysisOccurrence> built from each WordGroup's GetOccurrences() — and its persisted 'where was I' bookmark is paragraph index + character offsets in local (non-synced) settings, resolved back to an occurrence by FindWagform.
findings.evidence: `var chartedTargets = new HashSet<AnalysisOccurrence>(); foreach (var cellPart in m_chart.RowsOS.SelectMany(row => row.CellsOS.OfType<IConstChartWordGroup>())) chartedTargets.UnionWith(cellPart.GetOccurrences());` ... `new Tuple<int, int>(point.Segment.Hvo, point.Index)`. Bookmark: `m_propertyTable.SetProperty(BookmarkPropertyName("IndexOfParagraph"), ... LocalSettings ...); ..."CharBeginOffset" ... "CharEndOffset"`; `FindWordformAtBookmark ... curSeg.FindWagform(ibeg - segOffset, iend - segOffset, out fExactMatch)`.
findings.implication: FLEx has no token GUID either; where it must persist a token position outside the model it uses paragraph index + char offsets and re-resolves by content. FDAT's composite key (segment GUID + index, with baseline text as check) mirrors FLEx's own practice.

findings.claim: FLEx's own notion of 'the same WordGroup after changes' is content-based: same column and same baseline text of each occurrence.
findings.evidence: `public bool IsAnalogousTo(IConstChartWordGroup otherWordGrp) { ... if (this.ColumnRA != otherWordGrp.ColumnRA) return false; var myWordforms = this.GetOccurrences(); ... return !myWordforms.Where((t, i) => t.BaselineText.Text != otherWordforms[i].BaselineText.Text).Any(); }` ("Mostly designed for testing").
findings.implication: Supports adding column GUID + baseline text of the first word to FDAT's row re-anchoring fallback as a tie-breaker.

findings.claim: TextTag is the FLEx-native, GUID-bearing object that anchors data to a token range by (BeginSegment, EndSegment, BeginAnalysisIndex, EndAnalysisIndex) and is owned by the text (StText.Tags); it is maintained by AnalysisAdjuster identically to ConstChartWordGroup.
findings.evidence: `<class num="22" id="TextTag" ...> <rel num="1" id="BeginSegment" sig="Segment" card="atomic"/> <rel num="2" id="EndSegment" .../> <basic num="3" id="BeginAnalysisIndex" sig="Integer"> "These indices refer to the index of an IAnalysis object in a Segment.Analyses sequence." ... <rel num="5" id="Tag" sig="CmPossibility" card="atomic"/>`; StText: `<owning num="3" id="Tags" sig="TextTag" card="col"/>`; TextTag implements BegRef/EndRef/ChangeToDifferentSegment/ChangeToDifferentIndex; adjuster collects `m_para.GetTags()` and DeleteReferences does `owner.TagsOC.Remove(iar as ITextTag)`.
findings.implication: If FDAT needs a durable per-token GUID (e.g. for a token-scoped custom field value), create a one-token TextTag (Begin==End) in StText.TagsOC with an FDAT-owned Tag possibility; its GUID is stable and FLEx keeps its (segment, index) current or deletes it when the word is deleted — exactly the lifecycle FDAT wants. PLAN §5 already uses TextTags for bands, so this is the same mechanism.

findings.claim: In the RemoveMissingMarker recreation path the row being recreated contained only the missing-marker cell (and no Notes), so the recreated row has no ConstChartWordGroup at the moment of recreation; only its index and Label/flags carry over.
findings.evidence: `if (row.CellsOS.Count > 1 || row.Notes != null) { // Easy case; ... row.CellsOS.Remove(cellPart); return; } // In this case the row will disappear before we can add anything to it! // Save its properties and recreate it after. var irow = row.IndexInOwner; var label = row.Label; ... var newrow = m_rowFact.Create(Chart, irow, label);`
findings.implication: The 'first WordGroup BeginSegment + index' fallback cannot fire for this path — there is no WordGroup. For rows that consisted only of a marker, the only re-association keys are chart GUID + row position/Label (+ whatever the user charts into it next).

findings.claim: FDAT's current renderer keys tokens by a browser-side registry keyed on row index, token kind and ordinal position, and the XSL copies a `<word guid>` attribute to `data-guid` when present; the plan intends that guid to be the analysis GUID.
findings.evidence: app.js: "// Token GUID registry: key shape `${rowIdx}:${kind}:${pos}` → guid" ... `pair.setAttribute('data-token-guid', guid);`; XSL: `<xsl:if test="@guid"> <xsl:attribute name="data-guid"><xsl:value-of select="@guid"/></xsl:attribute>`; PLAN §4 row for ConstChartWordGroup: "`<word guid>` per analysis".
findings.implication: The sidecar's `guid` on `<word>` should be redefined as the occurrence key (segment GUID + index, plus the parent WordGroup GUID), with the analysis GUID moved to a separate attribute, so `data-guid` is unique per token in the rendered chart.

openQuestions: Does FLEx's Tagging view (and its 'delete overlapping tag' logic) tolerate one-token TextTags whose TagRA is an FDAT-owned possibility outside the Text Markup Tags list, or a sub-list of it? Not verified in the sparse checkout (Src/LexText/Interlinear tagging code not read for this question).

After a phrase join/break in the interlinear tab, does CleanupInvalidChartCells (or anything else) detect WordGroups whose indices now point at the wrong word but are still 'valid' (in range)? The clamping in ChangeToDifferentIndex suggests they are silently kept.
Does Undo/Redo of a baseline edit restore deleted TextTags/WordGroups with their original GUIDs? (Also open in the chart-anchors report.)

How does ConstChartWordGroup.GetOccurrences() ordinal (position within the group) behave when the adjuster grows/shrinks a group — is 'WordGroup GUID + ordinal' stable enough, or should FDAT always fall back to a one-token TextTag for per-token data?

Whether flexlibs/LCM from Python exposes ISegment.Guid and Segment.AnalysesRS indices cheaply enough to emit segment GUID + index for every token at export time (expected yes; not checked in flexlibs source).

result.summary: LCM's incoming-reference bookkeeping does NOT protect a band item from deletion, and it only cleans up custom reference COLLECTION/SEQUENCE fields, not custom ReferenceAtomic fields. Deleting a CmPossibility in FLEx's Lists area is gated solely by CmPossibility.CanDelete (base: not-already-being-deleted; plus discourse-template / chart-column / text-markup-tag / IsProtected checks) - there is no "is referenced by anything" check, so an FDAT band item referenced only from custom fields on ConstChartRow is freely deletable unless FDAT sets IsProtected=true. What happens to the row's reference then depends on the field type: (a) custom ReferenceCollection/ReferenceSequence - the LcmReferenceCollection/Sequence objects are IReferenceSource, register themselves in the target's m_incomingRefs when fluffed, and CmObject.DeleteObject -> ClearIncomingReferences() -> RemoveAReference() removes the deleted item from the row's collection as a normal registered modification: no dangling objsur, but the band assignment is silently lost. (b) custom ReferenceAtomic - GetCustomPropertyForSDA never calls AddIncomingRef (unlike the generated model path ConvertIdToAtomicRef), so refs loaded from disk are never registered; and even refs set in-session (which SetProperty does register) are not cleared because the generated RemoveAReferenceCore only iterates the class's MODEL atomic-ref properties (ConstChartRow has none) and the base is a no-op. The row therefore keeps an objsur to the deleted GUID in Charting.discourse. FLExBridge's CmObjectValidator only checks objsur structure, not target existence, so validation would not fail; FixFwData's OriginalFixer removes any objsur (custom or not) whose guid is unknown and drops the emptied <Custom> element, logging "removing link to nonexisting object" - i.e. the band assignment is silently stripped before Send/Receive. Deleting a single item is entirely different from deleting the whole list (DeleteCustomList deletes the custom fields via FieldDescription.MarkForDeletion). Design consequence: if FDAT uses a list reference it should use a custom ReferenceCollection (FDAT enforcing single membership) and/or set IsProtected on band items; a ReferenceAtomic custom field is the worst choice; an Integer/String code sidesteps the problem entirely.

findings.claim: CmPossibility.CanDelete does not consult incoming references at all; it is base.CanDelete (which only checks the object is not already being deleted) plus discourse-template, chart-column, text-markup-tag and IsProtected checks. A band item referenced only by FDAT custom fields is therefore deletable unless IsProtected is true.
findings.evidence: OverridesCellar.cs: `return base.CanDelete && !IsDefaultDiscourseTemplate && !IsThisOrDescendantInUseAsChartColumn && !IsOnlyTextMarkupTag && (OwningList != Cache.LangProject.TextMarkupTagsOA || !...GetByTextMarkupTag(this).Any()) && !IsProtected;`. CmObject.cs base: `public virtual bool CanDelete { get { return !Cache.ObjectsBeingDeleted.Contains(this); } }` with the remark that it only 'suppresses side effects of ClearIncomingReferences'.
findings.implication: LCM offers no automatic 'in use' protection for list items referenced via custom fields. If FDAT wants users to be unable to delete a band item in the Lists area, it must set CmPossibility.IsProtected=true (model Boolean, MasterLCModel.xml:379) on each band item; nothing else will stop the deletion.

findings.claim: FLEx's delete UI is gated only by ICmObject.CanDelete: RecordClerk.OnDeleteRecord returns early if !CanDelete(), ConfirmDeleteObjectDlg enables its Delete button from obj.Object.CanDelete, CmObjectUi.CanDelete(out msg) just wraps Object.CanDelete, and CmPossibilityUi.CanDelete(out) adds only chart-column and text-markup-tag checks. No UI path counts ReferringObjects for a possibility.
findings.evidence: RecordClerk.cs: `if (!CanDelete()) { ReportCannotDelete(); return; }` ... `if (uiObj.CanDelete(out cannotDeleteMsg)) dlg.SetDlgInfo(...)`; `protected virtual bool CanDelete() { return CurrentObject.CanDelete; }`. ConfirmDeleteObjectDlg.cs: `m_deleteButton.Enabled = obj.Object.CanDelete;`. FdoUiCore.cs: `public virtual bool CanDelete(out string cannotDeleteMsg) { if (Object.CanDelete) {...return true;} cannotDeleteMsg = FdoUiStrings.ksCannotDeleteItem; return false; }`; CmPossibilityUi (class at 1516): `if (!CanModifyChartColumn(out cannotDeleteMsg)) return false; if (!CanDeleteTextMarkupTag(out cannotDeleteMsg)) return false; return base.CanDelete(out cannotDeleteMsg);`
findings.implication: Confirms that, from the user's side, deleting an FDAT band item in the Lists area proceeds with no warning about chart rows that use it (unless IsProtected blocks it).

findings.claim: The generic object-deletion path is OnBeforeObjectDeleted -> ClearIncomingReferences -> DeleteObjectBasics, where ClearIncomingReferences calls EnsureCompleteIncomingRefs() and then referrer.RemoveAReference(this) for every IReferenceSource in m_incomingRefs. Cleanup of referrers therefore depends entirely on (1) the referrer being registered in m_incomingRefs and (2) the referrer's RemoveAReference actually clearing the property.
findings.evidence: CmObject.cs: `OnBeforeObjectDeleted(); ClearIncomingReferences(); DeleteObjectBasics();` ... `private void ClearIncomingReferences() { EnsureCompleteIncomingRefs(); foreach (var referrer in m_incomingRefs.ToArray()) referrer.RemoveAReference(this); }`
findings.implication: Sets up the two conditions that decide the custom-field outcome below.

findings.claim: The metadata cache does register custom reference fields as incoming fields of their destination class: AddCustomField builds the field with the destination class name as signature and calls ConnectMetaFieldRec, whose SetDestClass adds the record to m_metaClassRecords[destClid].m_incomingFields; GetIncomingFields walks that list up the base-class chain. So EnsureCompleteIncomingRefs on a CmPossibility does enumerate an FDAT custom ref flid on ConstChartRow.
findings.evidence: LcmMetaDataCache.cs AddCustomField: `if (m_metaClassRecords.TryGetValue(destinationClass, out mcrSig)) fieldSig = mcrSig.m_className; AddField(className, flid, uniqueName, null, null, null, fieldSig, fieldType, FieldSource.kCustom, Guid.Empty, 0); ... m_customFields.Add(mfr); ConnectMetaFieldRec(mfr);` SetDestClass: `mfr.m_dstClsid = clid; if (!mfr.Virtual) m_metaClassRecords[clid].m_incomingFields.Add(mfr);` GetIncomingFields iterates `metaClassRec.m_incomingFields` for clid and its bases. CmObject.EnsureCompleteIncomingRefs: `foreach (var flid in mdc.GetIncomingFields(ClassID, (int)CellarPropertyTypeFilter.AllReference)) { try { objrepo.EnsureCompleteIncomingRefsFrom(flid); } catch (LcmInvalidFieldException) { /* custom flid deleted this session */ } }`
findings.implication: The bookkeeping is wired up for custom fields at the metadata level; whether it works then depends on the per-type accessor code.

findings.claim: For a custom ReferenceAtomic field the incoming reference is NOT registered when the value comes from disk: EnsureCompleteIncomingRefsFrom(flid) calls obj.GetObjectProperty(flid) on every instance, which for a custom flid routes to GetCustomPropertyForSDA, and that method merely returns `((ICmObjectOrId)retval).GetObject(repo).Hvo` - it neither replaces the stored ICmObjectId with the real object nor calls AddIncomingRef. The generated model path (ConvertIdToAtomicRef) does call AddIncomingRef. Only an in-session set via SetProperty registers the incoming ref.
findings.evidence: RepositoryAdditions.cs: `case ReferenceAtomic: foreach (ICmObjectInternal obj in m_dataReader.AllInstances<ICmObject>(classId)) { obj.GetObjectProperty(flid); // forces it to be fluffed up. }`. CmObject.cs GetObjectPropertyInternal default: `return (int)GetNonModelPropertyForSDA(flid);` -> `IsCustom(flid) ? GetCustomPropertyForSDA(flid) : ...`. GetCustomPropertyForSDA: `case CellarPropertyType.OwningAtomic: case CellarPropertyType.ReferenceAtomic: retval = ((ICmObjectOrId)retval).GetObject(Services.ObjectRepository).Hvo; break;` (no AddIncomingRef, no store-back). Contrast ConvertIdToAtomicRef: `var result = ...GetObject(id); ((ICmObjectInternal)result).AddIncomingRef(this); return result;`. SetProperty (in-session only): `if (dataType == CellarPropertyType.ReferenceAtomic) { if (oldValue != null) {...RemoveIncomingRef(this);} if (newValue != null) {...AddIncomingRef(this);} }`. Load stores only an id: `case ReferenceAtomic: myElement = customPropertyElement.Element("objsur"); if (myElement != null) data = surrRepos.GetId(myElement);`
findings.implication: With a custom ReferenceAtomic band field, deleting the band item in a later session (the normal case after Send/Receive) leaves every referencing ConstChartRow untouched: the deleted GUID stays in the row's <Custom> objsur.

findings.claim: Even when a custom ReferenceAtomic ref IS registered (set this session), deletion does not clear it: CmObject.RemoveAReferenceCore is an empty virtual and the generated override iterates only the class's MODEL AtomicRefProperties; ConstChartRow has no model atomic reference properties (Notes, ClauseType, EndParagraph, EndSentence, Start/EndDependentClauseGroup, Cells, Label). There is no custom-property branch anywhere in RemoveAReference.
findings.evidence: CmObject.cs: `internal virtual void RemoveAReferenceCore(ICmObject target) { }` with remark 'Generated code contains a suitable override of this method for each class that has reference atomic properties'; `void IReferenceSource.RemoveAReference(ICmObject target) { RemoveAReferenceCore(target); }`.
